## The `.plr` legacy-subset shim + default policy (S1-J-5 increment 1)

The pre-S1-J-5 `.plr` writer was a **subset mirror** stamped release 279: it
stopped after the 58-slot inventory and omitted `team` (release 283),
`hideMisc` (119), the dead 324 bool and the 322 armour/dye favourited bools.
Those files are **not valid vanilla 279 files** — the C# `Deserialize` gates
would read `hideMisc` and run off the end — so they cannot be read through the
C# walk. `player_file::read_legacy_port_subset` is a **port-only backward-compat
shim**: `read_player_bytes` first tries the faithful gate walk, and on a
truncation error for a file stamped exactly 279 retries the old subset layout.
This is a deliberate deviation (the shim has no C# counterpart); it exists only
so characters saved by older port builds keep loading. New saves stamp 326
(`Player.cs:54738`) and never take the shim.

**Default-value policy.** The port models only the character-card state; every
other field the writer emits through `voidVaultInfo` (`Serialize:54863`) carries
the fresh-vanilla default (the `Player` ctor `Player.cs:56036-56096` + field
initializers) — play time 0, empty banks/misc slots, no favourites outside the
inventory. The reader's inventory guard uses `ItemID.Count = 6196`
(`ItemID.cs:14861`); the old subset reader's 5455 was stale and wrongly
air-gapped the 5455..6195 band (the shim keeps the corrected constant — the old
writer never emitted ids in that band, so old saves read identically).
Increment 1 ends at `voidVaultInfo`; the `Serialize` tail (`:54864-54933`) is
the next round, so a port `.plr` is byte-comparable with vanilla **through the
vault byte** only until then.

**Increment 2 (S1-J-5b, 2026-11-18).** The writer/reader now run through
`hideInfo` (`Serialize:54893` / `Deserialize:55623`): buffs (`:54864-54876` —
44 pairs, `maxBuffs` `Player.cs:57106`; fresh `buffType`/`buffTime` are all-zero
`:1510-1512` and `Main.buffNoSave[0]` is false, so the (0,0) else-arm bytes are
identical to the no-save arm), the spawn list (`:54877-54888` — fresh
`spN[0] == null` `:2488` writes only the `-1` sentinel), `hbLocked`
(`:54889`, default false `:1436`) and `hideInfo[13]` (`:54890-54893`, fresh
`bool[13]` `:812`). The reader gates mirror `Deserialize:55578-55623`, including
the buff-count 44/22/10 version gates and the zero-type compaction
(`:55593-55597`, which still consumes exactly `count` pairs). **Second shim**:
the increment-1 port files are stamped 326 but end at the vault byte, so the
C# gates would truncate in the buffs; `read_player_bytes` retries release-326
truncations with `through_vault_only` (stop at `:55504`), the same port-only
pattern as the 279 shim. Genuine vanilla 326 files never take it (they always
carry the buffs tail). `golden_layout_through_hide_info` pins every byte and
byte-compares the 370-byte tail with `assets/test/golden.plr` at offsets
2402-2772. A port `.plr` is now byte-comparable with vanilla **through the last
hideInfo bool**; the remainder is `:54894-54933`. Note: the C# envelope uses
RijndaelManaged's default PKCS7 padding (`Player.cs:54734-54736`) while the
port zero-pads to the block boundary — invisible to field readers, but the
final encrypted block differs from vanilla; full-envelope parity is a separate
concern.

## The world-format contract (S1-J-8)

**Decision: the two-format split stays, as a documented contract.** The port
keeps `.trwld` (native) and `.wld` (vanilla-shaped) as different routes with
different jobs; converging them would either drop the vanilla-world
interoperability or force the native format to be byte-vanilla, and both cost
more than the doubled save surface they would save.

- **`.trwld` is the canonical save route.** Every new piece of persisted state
  lands here first as a versioned tail block (v13 signs/plates, v14 the rain
  triple, v15 `downedQueenSlime`), the loader version-gates each block and a
  pre-N file loads with that block's reset defaults. The production boot world
  (`app::latest_own_world`) and the save routing (`is_native_trwld`) already
  make it the live surface.
- **`.wld` is the vanilla-interchange route.** Loading vanilla worlds
  (field-by-field codecs, the C# version gates) and writing them back at the
  byte SHAPE the vanilla expects. Its value coverage is a documented subset
  (the flags writer zero-fills the rain/Queen-Slime bytes, the loader
  skip-reads unimplemented sections) — the byte-parity tasks (S1-J-1's wire
  bits, S1-J-3's golden fixture) grow that coverage only where parity is
  actually demanded, against the C#'s own `SaveWorld` layout.
- **Stage-2 cost, bounded.** The two readers stay, but only `.trwld` is the
  live save surface — the `.wld` route is load-dominant interchange, so the
  compressor/reader doubling applies to the interchange path only. The
  app-side twins that neither format carries (the TownManager rooms, the
  bestiary sights/chats, the CreativePowers table — the recorded M6-SAVE-1b
  remainder) need a `WorldSide` twin on the app save path, not a format
  convergence.
- **The routing rule** (`is_native_trwld`, `app/mod.rs:3074`): the save picks
  the format by the world path's extension; a `.trwld` world saves native, a
  `.wld` world saves vanilla-shaped — the user's file never changes identity
  mid-session.
## The map reveal + refresh (S1-L-3, 2026-11-13)

The audit's D10 is closed: `WorldMap::update`'s reveal window now follows
`LightingEngine.ExportToMiniMap` (`LightingEngine.cs:246-262`) — the
engine's processed area shrunk 28 px per side, intersected with the world
bounds inset 40 and `MapHelper.sceneArea` (the scene-metrics scan's
player-centred `SceneMetrics.ZoneScanSize` box, `SceneMetrics.cs:917-919` =
169×124 tiles). The old fixed player-centred 75×47 box (smaller than
vanilla, trail-prone at speed) is gone; a stale/empty scene area intersects
to nothing, exactly like the C#'s `Rectangle.Empty` static. The view
centre rides the processed area (camera-centred), matching every other map
consumer.

The refresh machinery is ported whole: `WorldMap.UpdateType`/`QueueUpdate`
(`WorldMap.cs:65-105` — the queued re-derive keeps the light; the C#'s
`ref mapTile` flag-clear write-through is explicit in the port so the
clear persists on the early returns), `MapUpdateQueue`'s two queues with
the `WorldMap.QueueUpdate` dedupe (`MapUpdateQueue.cs:21-108`), the
per-frame drain (`Main.cs:61862`) feeding the minimap upload (the
`MapRenderer.QueueChange` analog), `UnlockMapSection`/`UnlockMapTilePretty`
(`WorldMap.cs:109-174` — the Manhattan falloff with the solid/lava skips
and the wall 0.8 / underground 0.7 tints) and `ClearEdges` at the map load
(`:210`).

Scope notes:

- **The edit hooks cover the player-edit paths** (the pickaxe/hammer/
  placement funnel in `world_sim/editing.rs`): the edited tile's
  `SquareTileFrame` ring queues (`WorldGen.cs:81334`'s head over
  `:80185-80197`'s walk). The projectile-side craters (the bombs, the
  magical ice) run inside the AI with a world-only signature — their map
  refresh rides the follow-up; the reveal pass still re-derives any tile
  it covers, so in-window craters refresh naturally.
- **`Main.sectionManager.TileLoaded(x, y)` passes** (`WorldMap.cs:80`): the
  section manager is the MP section tracker; the port's single-player world
  is fully loaded.
- **The fullscreen-map call site** (`Main.cs:41335`'s column layout) rides
  the map tasks (S1-L-4's layers).

### Second pass (2026-11-16): the driver

The primitives above were already present (the audit's "MISSING" rows for
`UnlockMapSection`/`ClearEdges`/`MapUpdateQueue` were stale). What was missing
was the *caller* and the *throttle*:

- **`UnlockMapSection` had no caller.** The `/map` chat command
  (`ToolkitDebugCommands.cs:480-494`) sets `DebugOptions.unlockMap` and
  `Main.refreshMap`, which Main consumes at `:61873-61877` by walking the
  section manager's draw queue. The port has no section manager (the whole
  world is resident), so `WorldMap::unlock_map` walks every 200×150 section
  directly; `unlock_section` applies the same `Utils.Clamp(v, 40, max-40)`
  the C# does (`WorldMap.cs:111-119`) to the dirty rect it re-uploads.
  Exposed as the F3 World-tab row "Reveal Map (pretty)" — the missing chat
  dispatcher is why the debug panel carries it.
- **The refresh was a `dt` timer, not `mapTime`.** `WorldMap::update` used a
  hardcoded 0.25 s accumulator; the C# gates `ExportToMiniMap` on
  `Main.mapTime == 0` (`LegacyLighting.cs:349`) after decrementing it per
  frame (`Main.cs:61818-61821`) and re-arming from `mapTimeMax`
  (`:16995-17000`, the gfx-quality budget — 0 above quality 0.8, which is why
  a good machine exports every frame). The port now carries `map_time`/
  `map_time_max` and the frame feeds `gfx_quality.map_time_max` in; `dt` is
  ignored. `mapDelay` and the `renderCount == 3` phase gate ride the same
  legacy-engine state the port has no equivalent of (it exports inline), so
  only the `mapTime` half is modelled.

## The crafting focus + quantity (S1-H-7, 2026-11-13)

`Main.HoverOverCraftingItemButton` (`Main.cs:42252-42305`) is ported into
`clicks.rs::handle_crafting_clicks`: the unfocused click selects the row
(`focusRecipe` — the port keys the focus by the recipe id rather than the
C#'s list position, which keeps it stable across the frame's re-sort),
`stackSplit = 15`, the click-consumed lock and the MenuTick sound; the
focused click crafts through the held-frame pacing (`stackSplit <= 1`,
`frame.rs`'s per-tick decay), with `num = (superFastStack + 1)` ×10 behind
`ItemSlot.ShiftInUse` and `flag4`'s reset arms (a different recipe being
crafted, or a non-stacking product). `craft.rs::try_craft_qty` is
`CraftingRequests.CraftItem(recipe, num)` (`Main.cs:42286`) — the C#'s
request queue processes the quantity asynchronously; the port loops the
single craft synchronously, each iteration re-checking the ingredients, so
a partial set crafts as many as it can (the request loop's net effect).

Scope notes: the filter/search bars stay draw-only (the station-filter
semantics are S1-L-11c's row and the search box rides the keyboard work);
`TryAllowingToCraftRecipe`'s mouse-blocking fetch (`:42278`) has no port
counterpart (the mouse item never blocks the craft here); the
`UsingOrReusingItem`/`IsStackingItems` gates of `flag3` (`Player.cs:23098`)
are unmodelled item-use state.

## The crafting pipeline (S1-L-11d, 2026-11-14)

`CraftingRequests.CreateResult` (`CraftingRequests.cs:122-131`) is ported as
`craft.rs::create_result`: the recipe's `createItem` cloned, `Item.OnCreated`'s
type swap (`Item.cs:48936-48942` — the ShellphoneDummy 5437 becomes the
Shellphone 5358) and `Item.Prefix(-1)`'s natural roll for a stack ≤ 1
(`Item.cs:504-610`). The grant carries the rolled prefix (`Item.CanStack`,
`Item.cs:49865-49872`), and the C#'s cursor gate
(`Main.CursorHasSpaceToCraftRecipe`, `Main.cs:42309-42345`) makes a prefixable
recipe craft **once** per click while the stackable ones (the torches) keep
crafting — the gate refuses a prefixable result outright
(`!item.CanHavePrefixes()`).

The crafting reach is the C#'s formula, `craft.rs::tile_reach`: the statics
`Player.tileRangeX/Y` (the defaults 5/3, `Player.cs:2496-2498`/`:57113-57114`)
with the per-tick writes — the Journey mode's Far Placement Range power
(×2 and +8/+8, `Player.cs:18818-18826`), the Extendo Grip / the Architect's
Gizmo Pack (+3/+2, `:13040-13044`), the held Toolbox (+1/+1, `:14955-14958`) —
then `TileReachCheckSettings.Simple`'s 20-tile clamp
(`TileReachCheckSettings.cs:20-34`, `:84`) and the artisan loaf's +4
(`Player.cs:35671`). The two gated recipes are ported too
(`needTorchGodsFavor` — the Torch God's potion 5573 and the master 5638 — and
`needMechdusa` — the 5334 row), with the gates `player.unlockedBiomeTorches`
and `SpecialSeedFeatures.Mechdusa` (`Recipe.cs:349-356`).

Deviations:

- **The crafted item goes into the inventory, not the cursor.** The C# hands
  the result to `Main.mouseItem` (`Main.CraftItem_GrantItem`,
  `Main.cs:42607-42612`) and the player places it with a click; the port grants
  it straight into the inventory (`clicks.rs::handle_crafting_clicks`). The
  cursor gate is therefore evaluated against the **previous result** instead of
  the cursor's content (`craft.rs::result_fits_next`) — the observable
  quantity matches the C#'s (a prefixable recipe crafts once), but the player
  never holds the crafted item on the cursor.
- **The artisan loaf's effect is not ported.** The flag
  `Player.ateArtisanBread` rides the player and the reach reads it, but the
  item that sets it (5326, `Player.cs:45218-45221`) has no ported use effect,
  so the +4 is unreachable in play.
- **The Torch God's unlock is not ported.** `player.unlockedBiomeTorches`
  (`Player.cs:2046`) rides the player and the gate reads it, but the unlock
  itself (the Torch God's dialogue) is unported, so the two gated recipes stay
  closed.
- **The prefix roll's stream.** The C# draws `Item.Prefix` from the same
  global `Main.rand` as the alchemy discount; the port's natural rolls ride
  `App::prefix_rng` and the crafting discount rides `App::craft_rng` — two
  stand-ins for one C# stream (the S1-A-11/S1-L-6c residual).
- **The quickCraft / remote-craft half is out** — the C#'s request queue
  (`CraftingRequests.CraftViaRequest`, `:142-174`) is the multiplayer path and
  the port's MP has no crafting requests.

The recipe table grew with it: the generator's tail branch broke out of the
expansion loop **before** copying the text that precedes
`Recipe.CreateReverseWallRecipes()` (`Recipe.cs:15148`), so the 414 authored
rows between the last expansion mark and that call were dropped (the audit's
"2 481 executed sites" was the generator's own truncated output). The branch
now copies that text: the table is **3 206 rows = 2 895 authored + 311
reverse**, and the pin in `tools/test_gen_recipes.py` re-taken.

## The sliced block light chain (S1-G-9, 2026-11-13; corrected 2026-11-16)

`DrawSingleTile_SlicedBlock` (`TileDrawing.cs:3517-3664`) is the port's
`render/tiles.rs::push_sliced` — and the chain now matches the C# exactly:
`Lighting.GetColor9Slice`'s 3×3 neighbourhood colours average with the
tile's own **raw** light (`(slices[i] + vector) * 0.5`, `:3578-3581`), then
`GetFinalLight` (`:4391-4402`) applies the tint and the actuation ghost
(`Tile.actColor`, `Tile.cs:282-288`, ×0.4) to that average. The high/medium
split (the 9-slice vs the 4-quad paths on `_highQualityLightingRequirement`/
`_mediumQualityLightingRequirement`, `:3524` / `:3605`) rides the existing
thresholds, and a Glow-coated block replaces every slice with
`_glowPaintColorSlices` (`:3530-3533` / `:3611-3614`, all `Vector3.One`).

Two defects in the 2026-11-13 landing, fixed by `S1-G-9-sliced-final-light`:

* **The double ghost.** `GetFinalLight`'s `Color` overload (`:4358`) takes
  `tileLight` **by value** and `:1019` assigns the result to
  `drawData.finalColor` — `drawData.tileLight` stays the raw
  `Lighting.GetColor` (`:871`). Only the `Vector3` overload (`:4391`) writes
  through `ref`. So `:3528`'s `vector` is unghosted, and the port's caller-side
  ghost plus the per-slice ghost composed to 0.16 instead of 0.4. `push_sliced`
  now samples the raw light itself and the `own` argument is gone, so the
  double-ghost cannot come back.
* **The Glow slices.** `fullbrightBlock()` blocks draw their slices at
  `Vector3.One` `_glowPaintColorSlices`; the port fed the neighbourhood light
  instead, so Glow-coated blocks stayed dark. Both arms apply the replacement.

Each slice is pushed with `push_sprite_paint`, carrying the tile's paint byte
as the flat arm does.

Scope notes: `GetFinalLight`'s shine arm (`ShouldTileShine` → `Main.shine`)
has no port counterpart — `Main.tileShine2` is unported (drawdata.rs:509), so
the branch is unreachable; the non-White `colorTint` is the minecart path
only (`:3788`). Both ride the paint work (S1-G-2's row).

## The map overlay layers (S1-L-4, 2026-11-14)

`Main.MapIcons`' overlay stack (`Main.cs:66551`'s registration: Digtoise →
BossBag → Spawn → TeamBasedSpawn → TeleportPylons → Pings) is ported over a
faithful `MapOverlayDrawContext` (`MapOverlayDrawContext.cs:8-70`): the
tile-position → screen transform `(position - mapPosition) * mapScale +
mapOffset`, the optional clip (the minimap's screen rect), the Alignment
origin multiplier and the `DrawResult.IsMouseOver` rect. The layers that
have port drivers draw: SpawnMapLayer (the world spawn + the bed marker —
the C# reads `localPlayer.SpawnX/SpawnY`, the port keeps the bed spawn on
`World.bed_spawn`), BossBagMapLayer (the `ItemID.cs:1383` 21-kind set over
the drop pool) and PingMapLayer (the 100-cap pool, the 15 s expiry, the 1x5
row cycling at 10 Hz).

**Second pass (2026-11-16, `S1-L-4-map-overlay-layers`)** closed the three
stubs and the missing call site. Digtoise draws: `digtoise_marker` scans the
projectile pool for the first active 1098/1123 whose `owner == 0` (the port's
standing stand-in for `Main.myPlayer`, as in `projectile.rs`/`grapple.rs`),
yielding `(Bottom, spriteDirection)` — `Bottom / 16 + (0.5, 0)` bottom-aligned,
column 1 when `spriteDirection <= 0` (`DigtoiseMapLayer.cs:14-26`). TeleportPylons
draws the live network: `tr_core::pylons::scan_pylons` feeds `MapIconInputs::pylons`,
each marker anchored at `PositionInTiles.ToVector2() + (1.5, 2)` centre-aligned
through `MapOverlayContext::draw_tinted` (the `MapOverlayDrawContext.cs:218-242`
`color * opacity` form), dimmed to `Color.Gray * 0.5f` = 0.25 when
`is_player_near_a_pylon` is false (`TeleportPylonsMapLayer.cs:39-42`/`:65-89`).
`PylonType::style()` (`self as u8`) is the inverse of `from_tile_style` and
supplies the `SpriteFrame` column, since the map layer's column *is* the type
discriminant. `WorldMap::tile_revealed` (`WorldMap.cs:406-409`) backs the
`IsRevealed` fog gate (`TeleportPylonsMapLayer.cs:112-119`) with a bounds guard
the C# gets for free from its world-sized jagged array. TeamBasedSpawn stays
gated: both `Main.teamBasedSpawnsSeed` and `ExtraSpawnPointManager` are unported
(M5-SEED-2's deferred list), so the branch is the faithful shape with no data
behind it.

Scope notes: the fullscreen call rides `Main.cs:55996`'s position (the
map's top-left minus the 10 px frame inset, `mapPosition = Vector2.Zero`
is the tile-space identity); the **minimap** call (`Main.cs:55696-55703`) is
wired in the same pass — the clip is `map_minimap_quad`'s destination rect and
the draw scale is the C#'s `num46 = ((mapMinimapScale * 0.25f * 2f + 1f) / 3f)`
capped at 1. The pylon scan is snapshotted once per frame and only while the map
or minimap is actually drawing, so the TE walk stays off the hot path.
`DrawNPCMapIcons` and `NPC.RevengeManager`'s marker layer are their own passes;
the hover text feeds the map's text line through `ui::text::hud_text` (the C#
`ref text`).

## Dust & gore (module 15) (S1-E-1, 2026-11-14; S1-E-3, 2026-11-17)

`crates/tr-core/src/particles.rs` is the `Main.dust` analog: the C# keeps the pool as the static `Main.dust[6001]` array plus the three static pressure counters (`Dust.dCount`, `lavaBubbles`, `SandStormCount`, `Dust.cs:12-16`), and the port carries the same global-pool semantics — one pool the App owns, spawns addressed by slot, slot 6000 the refuse sentinel `NewDust` returns and never scans (`Main.cs:66985`, `Dust.cs:79`/`:103`). The spawn path is a 1:1 transcription of `Dust.cs:10-407`: the guard chain (`:77-101`), the off-screen cull with the `400*(1-dCount)` margin (`:89-97`), the first-inactive-slot scan and the five pressure bands (`:103-152`), the default block with the per-100 frame shift (`:153-193`), the `ChildSafety` re-type arm (`:194-213`, `ChildSafety.cs:33`) and the per-type tweak chain (`:214-252`). The pool draws from the caller-passed stream (the `DustRng` seam, the C# `Next`/`NextFloat` conversions `UnifiedRandom.cs:120-141`), so per-consumer streams are preserved: the pool's band rolls are the only added draws on the clients' streams. The sand spawn site additionally regained the C# `NewDust` velocity/scale rolls the stand-in had skipped (`Sandstorm.cs:226`; the final 0.9 scale pin unchanged), and `Settings::blood` arms `pool.child_safety` at spawn — blood on is the vanilla default (the gate skipped), blood off sets `ChildSafety.Disabled` false and the re-type fires.

The migration retired one stand-in cap: the wheel sparks' `MAX_SPARKS` = 500 (the `minecart::Sparks` pool, pinned to no pressure) — the cart's queued requests now spawn type 213 through the shared pool with the cart's own stream. The flying sand's emit budget is not a stand-in and did not retire: it is the C#'s own line, `num7 = 1000*screenW/maxScreenW` with `gfxQuality` pinned to its no-pressure value 1.0 (`Sandstorm.cs:161`, ported at `sand.rs:106` over `MAX_SCREEN_W = 1920`); the migration only switched its subtrahend to the shared pool's live type-268 count — the budget stands, its pressure is now the pool's.

Scope notes and documented drops, each recorded at its site: the `shader`/`customData` record fields (no draw-shader chain; the `customData` followers live in `UpdateDust`, S1-E-3), the `Main.rand == null` re-seed and `Main.netMode == 2` server guards and the dead `Main.NoPooling` realloc arm (`Main.cs:67208` sets it false), and the `DANGEROUS` set = the 8 listed ids (5, 227, 273, 237, 248, 249, 250, 251 — `SetFactory.cs:97-107`; research/15's earlier inverted reading of that set is corrected). tr-app injects the wet probe through the seam (`player::wet_collision`, the `Dust.cs:248` probe). The child-safety sync runs `sync_child_safety` once per frame, so a settings toggle lands one tick late; `max_dust_to_draw`'s first frame reads the seed 0 (unreachable in production — the frame loop sets it before any spawn); the 268 draw keeps the stand-in's 10-px cell until E-3 ports the real draw, and the `NewDust` `Next(1)` gate draw is absent in both the stand-in and the port (pre-existing).

**The shared update loop (S1-E-3, 2026-11-17).** `UpdateCtx` + `DustPool::update_dust` transcribe the whole `Dust.cs:420-2423` skeleton verbatim: the head resets (`lava_bubbles`/`SandStormCount` — `snow_dust` is a `Main` static `Main.cs:621` and is not carried, the omission cited at the site), the `i < maxDustToDraw` split with the `else` kill (`:2393-2395`), `d_count++` (`:440`), the scale>10 kill with fall-through (`:447-449`), the `ChildSafety` firstFrame re-type (`:445-466`), `position += velocity` (`:477`), the per-type hook, the gravity tail (`:2335-2342`, 304 exempt and fadeIn-gated), the screen-bottom kill (`:2343-2346`), the `==` dCount nibbles (`:2347-2366`), the num86 ladder (`:2367-2391`), the scale-floor kill and the post-loop recompute (`:2398-2422`).

**Two dead arms, ported DEAD.** Both keep their C# citations because neither can fire in the C# either: `num` never increments (only the recompute's `else { dCount = 0 }` is reachable), and the `==` dCount nibbles never match — the C# compares the rounded-down byte-width drawing count against an integral `dCount`.

**The clients fold to one pass.** `minecart::tick` (frame.rs's dust phase — `Main.cs:18045-18047`'s single ported pass) runs `update_dust` ONCE per frame, dispatching the type-213 arm (its own body) and type 268 (`sand::type_268_arm`, world/player_vy/sandstorm-visuals as captured inputs). `scene_scan.rs`'s separate sand tick call is deleted (its emit stays, `Main.cs:17247`), the duplicated generic tails are deleted, and the per-tick `dust_index` pin is deleted — `Main.cs:18062-18066` is the crash-recovery re-init in `UpdateWorld_Dust`'s catch, not a per-tick reset.

**The corrected chain reading.** The 213/268 arms are standalone statements of the C# FIRST ladder (`Dust.cs:2119-2127`, `:2127`): the burn-out `else if (type != 304)` closes that ladder and the fresh `if (dust.type >= 130 ...)` chain head follows. They therefore do NOT exclude the second chain's final `else if (type != 304 && noGravity)` tail (`:2335`) — the hooks return false, and the weightless-213 test re-pins the ×0.92 damp and the fadeIn-gated −0.04 on top of the folded pass.

**Stream-draw enumeration.** The loop draws nothing new: the `ChildSafety` firstFrame re-type's `Next` reads ride the client streams through the pool's `DustRng` seam exactly as at spawn (S1-E-1), and the 213/268 arms draw none — they read only captured inputs. 15 `s1_e_3_*` tests pin the skeleton, the dead arms, the fold and the chain reading.

**Review path and its deviations.** Independent review round 1 PASSED the tr-core skeleton (`0d1cb0e9`); the tr-app fold's round 1 FAILED and produced the two defects fixed forward in `c361d656` — the double head-run per frame and the wrong either/or reading of the arms vs the gravity tail. The round-2 review agent was quota-cut three times before it could land verdicts (an infrastructure deviation, recorded); the fix was instead verified in-session — the single call-site grep, the one-move/damp pins and the 4094/0 test counts.

What remains: E-2 (the per-type table + `GetAlpha`/`GetColor` — the `Dust.cs:467-2334` if-chain arms and light arms that E-3's skeleton skips), E-4 (gore: `NewGore`/`GoreID.Sets`/`Gore.Update` + the leaves, incl. the foliage leaf tail), the `rain.rs` re-point and the NPC/Projectile/player call sites — the caller-coverage table in `docs/research/15-dust-gore.md` stays authoritative.


What remains: E-2's if-chain arms and light arms (`Dust.cs:467-2334`) and the `customData` follower arms, E-4's remaining `Gore.NewGore*` drop sites and the gore draw pass, the `rain.rs` re-point and the NPC/Projectile/player call sites — the caller-coverage table in `docs/research/15-dust-gore.md` stays authoritative; the band's neighbours landed alongside (S1-E-2's colour table and S1-E-4's gore pool/update — their own sections below), so only the parts named here stay outstanding.


## Dust colour table (S1-E-2, 2026-11-16)

`crates/tr-core/src/dust_table.rs` is the colour/fade half of the per-type table: `Dust.GetAlpha` (`Dust.cs:2425-2727`), `Dust.GetColor` (`:2729-2772`) and the two visual accessors (`:2774-2790`), transcribed arm for arm in source order so the fall-through chain reads like the C#. The XNA colour algebra the arms use is three private helpers at the top of the file — `Color * float` (every channel scales, then the ctor truncates), `Color.Lerp` (per-channel `MathHelper.Lerp`, truncating cast) and the `ToVector3`/`ToVector4` product (normalised channels, so `a*b/255`) — because the port has no `Microsoft.Xna.Framework` and inventing a full colour type for three operators would be more code than the operators.

The record stays byte-based (`particles::Color`, sRGB bytes, the `Dust.color` carrier), so every `new Color(int, …)` argument takes the C# `(byte)` cast the ctor performs: truncate, wrap past 255. The 213 draw already relied on that wrap before this task (`minecart.rs`, `int num2 = (int)(scale / 2.5f * 255f)`); it now calls the shared table instead of keeping its own copy of the arm.

Two arms are documented drops because they read globals the port does not carry: type 157 (`Main.mouseTextColor`, `Dust.cs:2627-2651`) and type 327 (`Main.rand` + `Main.DiscoR/G/B`, `:2658-2676`). Both fall through to the default formula (`:2712-2724`) rather than inventing a stand-in constant. Type 157 is the rarity-sparkle dust and type 327 the disco dust; neither is spawned by any ported call site yet.

The row’s other columns are deliberately not in this file. Gravity / `noGravity` / velocity scaling has two halves: the spawn-time chain is already verbatim in `particles.rs::new_dust` (`Dust.cs:214-252`, S1-E-1) and the per-tick gravity tail (`:1819-1828`) belongs to the update walk that S1-E-3 sequences. The light column is the ~70 `Lighting.AddLight` arms spread from `Dust.cs:485` to `:2050`, which cannot be ported without the entity-light seam (S1-E-5) — and they are not a table anyway, they are code interleaved with the per-type update arms. The `DustID` names already live at `tr-app::id_tables::DUST_ID` (S1-F-6, 196 named constants + `DustID.Count = 332`), so no second copy exists here.

Verification: five tests (`s1_e_2_*`) assert every constant arm against its C# literal (the table rows, the grey families, the `noLight`/`alpha == 255`/`noGravity` gates), the formula arms against hand-computed values (`306 * num`, `263`’s integer halving, `213`’s `scale/2.5*255`, the three lerp fractions, the two Vector products), the default tail’s `(num+3)/4` and `(num+9)/10` divisors, and the accessors. The arm id-sets (`:2494`, `:2584`, `:2681`) were additionally diffed mechanically against the C# conditions, and the constant-arm colours were extracted from the C# and compared row by row.

## Gore: the pool, the spawn family and the update walk (S1-E-4, 2026-11-16)

`crates/tr-core/src/gore.rs` carries `Main.gore[601]` (`Main.cs:66990`) as
[`GorePool`]: 600 live slots plus the sentinel 600 that `NewGore` returns for a
refused spawn and never scans (`Gore.cs:1308-1320`). The record is
`Gore.cs:14-42` field for field; `sticky = true`, `timeLeft = goreTime` and
`Frame = new SpriteFrame(1, 1)` are the struct initialiser, and `goreTime` is
the pool-level static (`:1507-1510`, 600).

The RNG contract, resolved against `Gore.cs:1327-1328` verbatim (an earlier
checkpoint summary misread it as `Next(2)` → X → Y): one `Next(10, 31)` on
`velocity.Y` **first**, then one `Next(-20, 21)` on `velocity.X`. Nothing else
in `NewGore` rolls except the two ChildSafety draws (`Next(11, 14)` then
`NextFloat()`, `:1336-1338`, only when the gate is armed and the type is
dangerous) and the two type-1225 draws (`:1375-1382`). The per-type arms
(`:1355-1456`) are pure writes.

`crates/tr-core/src/gore_id.rs` is `GoreID.Sets` (`GoreID.cs:20-23`) built the
way `SetFactory` builds it (`SetFactory.cs:97-130`): a default for the whole
array plus the listed `(id, value)` pairs. `special_ai` (default 0),
`disappear_speed` (default **1**), `disappear_speed_alpha` (default **1**) and
`is_drip` (default false) replace the earlier fabricated range table
(`219..=331`, `943..=1242`) that shipped with the draft — the defaults matter:
a zero `disappear_speed` would have frozen every timer.

The update walk is `Gore.Update` (`Gore.cs:308-1083`) split into the driver(`update`, `Main.UpdateWorld_Gores` `Main.cs:17971-17996`), `update_slot` (the
main chain) and the twelve helpers the C# factors out: the four cloud/spark
rows (`:110-260`), the drip animation (`:378-529`), the drip collision pass
(`:915-977`), the sticky rest (`:978-1019`), the chum bucket and its floating
chunk plus `ChumFloatingChunk_GetWaterLine` (`:552-671`, `:262-290`), the
`SpecialAI == 2` smoke row (`:767-843`), the 411-430 pages (`:844-912`),
`Gore_UpdateLeaf` (`:1085-1209`) and `Gore_UpdateSail` (`:1211-1271`).

Documented drops, each at its site: the texture-gated arms are the port's
`TextureAssets.Gore[...].IsLoaded == false` path throughout (`Gore::width`/
`height`/`aabb_rectangle` return the C#'s own 1/1 fallbacks, and the size
probes keep `32f` — `4f` for the ogre-spit rows — so the collision boxes are
exactly the C#'s unloaded-texture sizes); the entity lights (`Lighting.AddLight`
at `:258`, `:940`, `:1076`) wait for S1-E-5; the 716/1383 shimmer tint
(`:917-941`) needs `LiquidRenderer.GetShimmerBaseColor`; the `SoundEngine` hits
and the water-shader ripple (`:953`, `:965`, `:967`) need the audio and shader
seams; and the player-rect/dust-burst arms (`:794-841`, `:850-864`, `:883-910`,
`:1119-1122`) need the entity and dust pools on the core side. None of those
draws a random number, so the stream order is untouched — which is the property
the port actually needs from them.

`tr-core` cannot depend on `tr-app`'s collision ports, so the walk takes a
[`GoreCollision`] seam (`tile_collision` = `Collision.cs:2292`, `wet_collision`
= `:1572`, `slope_collision` = `:1791`), the same injection pattern the dust
pool uses for its wet probe (`particles.rs:197-202`). The App implements it in
`crates/tr-app/src/gore_seam.rs` over `collision::tile_collision`,
`player::wet_collision` and `collision::slope_collision`. The C#
`SlopeCollision` declares a `gravity` parameter (`Collision.cs:1791`) and never
reads it, so the port's `slope_collision` without it is exact, not a
simplification.

The App owns the pool as `App.gore` (`Main.gore`), ticks it in the `gores`
phase of the fixed step — between `npcs` and `projectiles`, the C# order at
`Main.cs:17767-17775` — on the stage's own named stream
(`Main.SwapRandom("UpdateGores")`, `RngKey::UpdateGores`), and feeds it
`Main.WindForVisuals` = `Wind::speed_current` (`Main.cs:2823`). The blood
toggle drives the same `ChildSafety.Disabled` static for both pools
(`ChildSafety.cs:15` — one static in the C#, so `sync_child_safety` sets both).
The draw pass stays unported, which is why no gore is visible yet.

Tested (`cargo test -p tr-core gore --lib`, 14 passing): the spawn order and
velocity, the drip sheet, the `SpecialAI` 1/2/3/4-6 arms, the balloon rows, and
the three lifecycle tests (sticky countdown → alpha fade → deactivate; the free
gore's double-speed fade `:1020-1023`; the floor cloud's wind drift and expiry
`:112-136`). The seam has its own forward test (`gore_seam::tests`), and the
App's phase-order golden test now pins `gores` between `npcs` and
`projectiles`.
## The carrier's life pool (S1-D-6, 2026-11-14)

`NPC.realLife` (`NPC.cs:6161`) is the C#'s carrier link: an NPC index that
points at the NPC whose life the linked NPC shares. `AI_006_Worms` gives the
head `ai[3] = whoAmI` + `realLife = whoAmI` and hands the link to every
child (`NPC.cs:51305-51363`); `AI_037_Destroyer` does the same for the
Destroyer (`:49836-49853`) and the crawltipede's own arm for its chain
(`:51369-51392`). The Eater of Worlds is the one exception — C# forces
`realLife = -1` for types 13-15 (`:51129-51132`), so every EoW segment owns
its own life.

The three consequences the port now carries:

* **One pool.** `StrikeNPC_Inner`'s `realLife` arm (`:81374-81378`) puts the
  damage on the carrier's `life` and copies the carrier's `life`/`lifeMax`
  back onto the struck segment. The pool's size is the carrier's `lifeMax`:
  the Devourer 100 (`:8771`), the Giant Worm 30 (`:8858`), the Leech 60
  (`:10413`), the solar crawltipede 10000 (`:15273`), the Destroyer **80000**
  (`:10667` — the port carried the per-segment 8000, so the whole worm was
  eight times too tanky).
* **A carrier-bound death.** `checkDead` returns early for a link whose
  carrier is not itself (`:78040-78042`), so a segment never runs the death
  events: no loot, no coins, no bestiary credit, no banner, no invasion
  kill credit. Only the carrier's death carries them.
* **A chain without orphans.** A classic family's link dies with its leader
  (`:51425-51433`); the `Transform(13)`/`Transform(15)` split is the Eater
  of Worlds' rule only (`:51498-51519`). The port used to split the
  Devourer's and the Giant Worm's bodies into new heads — a segment that
  outlived its chain.

Port notes:

* **The carrier link is a stable identity, not an index.** The vanilla's
  `realLife` is an NPC index, but `App::npcs` compacts every frame (the
  death retain in `world_sim/npcs.rs`), so an index would not survive the
  frame. The port's chain identity (`worm_id` + `seg_index`) stands in: the
  carrier is the link with `seg_index == 0` (`Npc::carrier_index`).
* **The mirror is continuous.** C# copies the carrier's `life` onto the
  segment when the segment is struck; the port's worm pass mirrors it every
  frame, so a segment never shows a stale life. The observable result is the
  same: the pool empties the whole chain at once, and the DoT on a segment
  (which C# also loses — it writes the segment's stale `life`) cannot kill a
  link.
* **The two strikes without the NPC list defer.** The EoC shield-dash and
  the thorns reflect (`Npc::contact`) have no access to the NPC list, so
  their damage is parked in `pending_pool_damage` and the worm pass pays it
  to the carrier in the same frame. The melee, the projectile and the net
  paths resolve the carrier directly (`Npc::strike_melee` /
  `Npc::strike_projectile`).
* **The net mode carries no chains.** The net snapshot rebuilds `App::npcs`
  from the wire (kind/position/life), so the links have no `worm_id` there
  and a remote strike lands on the segment itself. The host owns the
  simulation, as in the vanilla.
* **The tail's damage multiplier.** `NPC.takenDamageMultiplier`
  (`:81244-81246`) multiplies the strike before it lands; the solar
  crawltipede's tail (414) carries 10 (`:15316`) — the tail is the softest
  point of the chain by a factor of ten.
* **Still open.** The worm families' boss health bar (`Main.cs:45979`'s
  `DrawInterface_Healthbar_Worm`, the carrier's life on the bar) and the
  Moon Lord carrier + the DD2 anchors (the port's kind-search pre-passes
  instead of the C#'s explicit index links) are the S1-D-6b row.
## The missing projectile AI arms (S1-D-4b-1, 2026-11-14)

The ROADMAP's S1-D-4b row ("19 styles have a `proj_data` row but no
dispatch arm — those projectiles hold position forever") is not one
landable task: the 19 styles span ~5 300 C# lines of arms plus the two
mega-families (`AI_026`'s 6 922 lines over 68 types, `AI_067`'s 2 081
over 16). The row is therefore split into S1-D-4b-1..8 by family — the
same precedent S1-D-4c set for the vortex styles — and the contract
stays "arm them, never remove the rows": every style keeps its
`proj_data` row and gains its dispatch arm.

**Slice-D audit (2026-11-18, `task/S1-D-4b-14-styles-d`, code-only mode).**
The slice-D assignment (styles 133/134/137/138, fallback 157) ran under a
user directive reserving the CPU: no cargo/rustc/rustfmt/test runs, no
dotnet, no graphify — file reads/writes + git only. Each style was located
in `Projectile.cs`'s `AI()` dispatch and its whole machine re-read against
the port:

* **133** (`:36435-36498`) — `ai_dark_mage_raise` matches the 673's ramp
  (hand-check: tick 1 → `ai[0]=1`, `GetLerpValue(0,20,1)=0.05`,
  `alpha=(int)(0.95*255)=242`; `ai[0]=20..59` → alpha 0; `ai[0]=79` →
  0.05 → 242; `ai[0]=80` → Kill then `Opacity=0` → alpha 255 — the C#
  assigns Opacity after the kill arm, the port keeps that order). The
  674 heal arm has no ported row (documented in the arm).
* **134** (`AI_134_Ballista` `:68510-68651`) — the dispatch arm matches:
  the 160/100/60/30 delay ladder (`:68653-68669`), the init latch before
  the pickup gate, the captured firing centre (677's −4 px), the
  0.08/0.05 `AngleLerp` aim, the fire state at `ai[1]==5`, the
  `1 + (int)(ai[1]/5)` frame and the 25-tick cycle; the 680 bolt's
  aiStyle-1 spawn clamp decays the 16-px shot once (15.52) and the 21-px
  setSquireT2 shot nine times (21 → 15.9648…) — hand-checked ×0.97 ladder.
* **137** (`AI_137_LightningAura` `:68854-69023`) — the knockback pin,
  the monk-set constants (10→14 tiles, 30→25 period, 4→8 min tiles), the
  `Searches.Down(500)`/`Up(num)` scans, the half-brick +8 lift, the
  height clamp ×2 + 999 width cap, the 8-tick frame machine, and the
  ground-scan early return that leaves `AI()` but not `Update()` (the
  movement still runs) — all match.
* **138** (`AI_138_ExplosiveTrap` `:69301-69374`) — the facing pin, the
  tier→blast switch, the backpack branch (num3=20, num2 48→34), the
  12-tick frame machine, the 3-tick scan cooldown, the 144×144
  `CenteredRectangle` at `Center+(0,−num2)` inflated by num3, the
  90/60/30 huntress cooldown and the gravity tail — all match.
* **157** (`AI_157_SharpTears` `:51358-51494`) — the 961 parameter row
  (fade-in 10, fade-out from 10, kill at 20, 5 frames), the phase gates
  read before the counter advance, the negative-age arm, the one-shot
  rotation + `Main.rand.Next(5)` frame roll (kept — visible state) and
  the ±0.1/−0.2 `Opacity` ramps — all match.

**RNG argument:** 133/134/138 draw no `Main.rand` in their arm bodies
(the 134 targeting/shot are deterministic); 137's only draws are the
three cosmetic dust loops' gating rolls (`:68961`/`:68965`, `:69005` —
the `:68982` loop is `k < 0`, dead code in the C# too), skipped with the
dust layer per the standing precedent; 157 keeps its single `Next(5)`
frame roll on the pass's stream and skips only the dust-loop draws. No
stream order changes.

**Deferrals (code-only mode):** no builds/tests were run — verification
was C# line-by-line re-reading + hand arithmetic against the existing
`s1_d_4b_1_tests`/`s1_d_4b_2_trap_tests`/`s1_d_4b_5_tests` pins. No new
code landed: the five styles were already armed by the DONE rows
-1/-2/-5, so a new `projectile_styles_d.rs` module would have duplicated
landed arms (AGENTS "avoid duplicating an existing implementation").
The remaining unarmed styles are **26/67/120/123/130** (S1-D-4b-3/-7/-8).

S1-D-4b-1 ports the four self-contained styles:

* **aiStyle 70 — the Flairon Bubble** (`Projectile.cs:30304-30354`):
  the one-shot acquire scan (the closest chaseable NPC inside 650 px
  with a clear `Collision.CanHit` line — the running-minimum distance,
  so the tightest target wins), the first steering step
  (`(v * 20 + d * weight) / 21` with `weight = Next(35, 75) / 30f` and
  the ±100 px jitter), the steady homing (`(v * 40 + d * 12) / 41`), the
  no-target path (the counter starts at −15 and climbs back to 0, the
  alpha falls 25/tick to its 50 floor, the velocity decays 5%) and the
  scale roll (`Next(80, 121) / 100f`).
* **aiStyle 133 — the Dark Mage raise marker**
  (`Projectile.cs:36435-36453`): the counter, the `GetLerpValue`
  opacity ramp (0 → 1 over 20 ticks, 1 until the 60th, back to 0 by the
  80th) and the kill. The 674's heal arm has no ported row.
* **aiStyle 187 — the Insanity shadow** (`Projectile.cs:42502-42634`):
  the four variation windows (180/120/90/90 ticks) with the alpha ramp
  (+25/tick over the last 15 ticks of a window, −25/tick before it,
  floored at 50) and the kill on the window's last tick, then the four
  choreographies (the drift, the tethered swing, the burst, the spin).
* **aiStyle 189 — the Volcano / Cascade Explosion**
  (`Projectile.cs:42264-42303`): the two-remap alpha flash, the scale
  ramp and the five-frame life (the frame advances every second tick,
  the fifth frame kills).

Deviations (each deliberate, each with its C# citation in the arm):

* **The dust and gore of the explosion are SKIPPED**
  (`:42305-42369`) — the port has no dust or gore layer (S1-E-1 /
  S1-E-4 are in flight). With them the arm's `Main.rand` draws go too
  (every one of them belongs to a dust/gore block), so the arm keeps the
  gem-staff arm's zero-RNG invariant (`Projectile.cs:37643-38001`).
* **The tracked sounds are SKIPPED** — the summon cue
  (`:36438-36440`), the shadow's per-tick sound-position update
  (`:42507-42515`) and the explosion cue (`:42266-42269`): the pool has
  no tracked-sound layer (S1-E-23). The shadow's `localAI[1]` slot stays
  untouched, as in the C#'s other arms with no sound layer.
* **`Projectile.Opacity` (`:540`) is a state-only field**: the port has
  no projectile draw pass yet, so the aiStyle-133 ramp writes the slot
  and nothing reads it yet. The field defaults to the C#'s `1f`.
* **The Flairon Bubble's target is an NPC-slot index** in the C#
  (`Main.npc[(int)ai[0] - 1]`, `:30324`/`:30329`). The port's NPC vec
  drops the dead, so a stored index can name a different NPC (or none)
  than the C#'s slot did; the port keeps the index shape (the Nebula
  Arcanum's `ai[1] = index + 1` precedent) and reads it with
  `npcs.get`, so a vanished target steers nowhere instead of at the
  C#'s stale slot.
* **Four `proj_data` rows were wrong and are now faithful**: the
  Flairon Bubble (405, `:4864`), the Dark Mage marker (673, `:7213`),
  the Insanity shadow (965, `:9121`) and the Cascade Explosion (1125,
  `:10536`) all write `alpha = 255` in their `SetDefaults` arms, and the
  1125 also writes `usesLocalNPCImmunity = true` with
  `localNPCHitCooldown = -1` (`:10538-10539`). The port's rows dropped
  all of it (the `RESET_STATE` alpha 0), so the arms would have started
  from the wrong alpha — the aiStyle-70 fade arm floors the alpha at 50,
  which would have *raised* a 0 to 50 on the first fade tick.

## The composite arm poses (S1-G-16, 2026-11-14)

`Player.compositeFrontArm`/`compositeBackArm` (`Player.cs:1906/:4347-4365`)
were never ported: the renderer used a `swing_stand_in` stand-in that
enabled the front arm for three use styles (2/11/13), never the back arm,
and read the stretch ladders off a normalised swing instead of the C#'s
`itemAnimation` — so the arms posed wrong in most item animations (the
style 11 ladder was inverted, the style 13 stretch was inverted, the style 2
pose never reached its relaxed row). The sim now owns the state:

* `AnimatePlayerAndGetItemFrame` (`Player.cs:43372-43386`) resets both arms
  to DISABLED per frame and dispatches: `itemAnimation > 0` →
  `ItemCheck_ApplyUseStyle`, otherwise → `ItemCheck_ApplyHoldStyle`.
* `ItemCheck_ApplyUseStyle`'s composite assignments (`:50885-51375`) are
  ported per use style — 2 (both arms `-PI/2 * dir`, the `num10` quarters),
  8 (the wind-up/swing-arc phases), 9 (the `num7 → num8` arc), 11 (the
  `num12` two-cycle + the back arm Full at `-PI/16`), 12 (the `num30`
  two-cycle + `num31 = cos(num30 * PI) * 0.2`), 13 (the `num20` thirds +
  `itemRotation * Directions.Y - PI/2 * dir`), 14 (the back arm Full at
  `-3*PI/4 * dir`) and 15 (both arms at `-2*PI/5 * dir`).
* `ItemCheck_ApplyHoldStyle`'s composite assignments (`:50520-50582`) are
  ported per hold style — 4 (the umbrella: the front Full + the back
  ThreeQuarters around `num9 ± num8`), 5 (the back Quarter at `-PI/4 * dir`
  + the front Full at `-0.39269912 * dir`), 6 (the back ThreeQuarters at
  `-3*PI/5 * dir`) and 8 (both arms at `-2*PI/5 * dir`).
* The draw consumes the live state: `PlayerDrawSet.UpdateCompositeArm`
  (`PlayerDrawSet.cs:2246-2275`) picks the front column 7 / the back
  column 8 at the stretch row (Full 0 / ThreeQuarters 1 / Quarter 2 /
  None 3) and the rotation pivots the arm around the composite pivot
  (`render/player_layers.rs::update_composite_arm`).

The shooting styles' `itemRotation` (`Player.cs:47371-47378`) is now the
C#'s `atan2(aimY * direction, aimX * direction) - fullRotation`: the port
keeps the aim as an angle, so the mirrored `atan2` is the aim + PI when
the player faces left (`item_rotation_for_aim`). The old stand-in used
`aim * direction` — the negated angle, not the mirrored vector — so the
useStyle 5 body rows (`num21 = itemRotation * direction`, `:36423`) and the
useStyle 13 composite arm were off by PI when facing left.

Deviations (deliberate, bounded):

* The useStyle 8 overshoot branch (`itemAnimation > useAnimation`,
  `:51226-51244`) is unreachable — the port's swing counter never exceeds
  `itemAnimationMax`.
* The useStyle 13 stretch base is `itemAnimationMax`, where the C# uses
  `itemTimeMax` when it is non-zero (`:51176-51184`) — the port has no
  per-item use time.
* The useStyle 9 branch also moves `itemLocation` through
  `GetFrontHandPosition` (`:50901-50905`); the port draws the held item
  from its own item-row chain (the held-item positions are the
  M2-DRAW item-row work).
* `AnimatePlayerAndGetItemFrame` reads `lastVisualizedSelectedItem` while
  the animation runs (`:43374`); the port uses the currently selected item.
* The petting composite arms (`ItemCheck_ApplyHoldStyle`'s `isPetting`
  block, `:50242-50269`) and the football arm (`:36139-36143`) stay
  unported (no petting/football systems).
* `Player.Directions.Y` (the gravity direction, `:3849`) is 1 in the port
  (no gravity flip).

Tests: `s1_player_composite_tests` — the eat style's quarters, the mow
style's two-cycle + the back arm's constant pose, the rapier's stretch
thirds + its item-rotation arm, the shoot style's back arm, the hold
styles' arms and the aim mirror. All seven are mutation-checked (RED on
the pre-fix code).


## The saucer projectile arms (S1-D-4b-4, 2026-11-14)

The ROADMAP's S1-D-4b-4 slice (the aiStyle-79 deathray and the aiStyle-80
missile — the Martian Saucer's two shots, `Projectile.cs:30791-31000`) is
the second half of the S1-D-4b-1 split (the row was split into S1-D-4b-1..8
because the 19 styles span ~5 300 C# lines of arms plus the two
mega-families).

**aiStyle 79 — the Saucer deathray (447)**. The ray is a beam that hangs
from the NPC that spawned it: the C#'s spawn passes `ai0 = base.whoAmI + 1`
(`NPC.cs:35917` for the shell, `:36437` for the core) and the arm reads that
slot. The arm's gates are the owner's state — the shell's `ai[0]` must name a
live core (`:30805-30813`), the core's phase must be `ai[3] % 120 >= 60` with
`ai[0] == 2` (`:30829-30832`), and the owner's own `ai[0]` must not be one of
the three "no target" states (`:30833-30835`). Then the geometry: the beam's
top is the owner's centre + 46, its column is the owner's centre, and its
height is the scan down to the first solid row at or below the player's feet
(the 150-row cap), trimmed by the last row's `num601 % 16 - 2`.

**aiStyle 80 — the Saucer missile (448)**. The spawn passes `ai1 = 20f`
(`NPC.cs:35845`) and the arm counts it down (the arming delay); on the
arming tick the arm picks the target (`Player.FindClosest` — the port's
local player is the only one) and speeds the flight up by 4 px. The flight
turns toward the target for its first 30 ticks at 0.2 rad/tick, dies at the
180-tick life end, and dies on a living player within 42 px.

Deviations (each deliberate, each with its C# citation in the arm):

* **The dust is SKIPPED** (the deathray's `:30863-30878`, the missile's
  `:30920-30929`/`:30946-30956`/`:30963-30971`) — the port has no dust layer
  (S1-E-1 is in flight). With it the arms' `Main.rand` draws go too (every
  one of them belongs to a dust block), so the arms keep the gem-staff
  arm's zero-RNG invariant (`Projectile.cs:37643-38001`).
* **The owner is an NPC-slot index** in the C# (`Main.npc[(int)ai[0] - 1]`,
  `:30794`). The port's NPC vec drops the dead every tick, so a stored index
  can name a different NPC than the C#'s fixed slot did; the port keeps the
  index shape (the Nebula Arcanum's `ai[1] = index + 1` precedent) and
  re-checks the owner's kind (the C#'s own `type` gate), so a stale index
  kills the ray instead of aiming it at a stranger.
* **The shell's core link is by kind**: the C#'s shell holds the core's slot
  in its `ai[0]` (`:35895-35907`), while the port's saucer family links
  through the carrier write-through (the position link, the port's
  link-by-kind convention for the boss families). The arm therefore looks
  the core up by its kind.
* **The target is the local player**: the C#'s beam reads the owner's
  `NPC.target` (the core's, when the owner is the shell) and the missile
  uses `Player.FindClosest`; the port's NPCs carry no target field and the
  local player is the only one (the MP roster is its own row).
* **The spawn-site `ai0`/`ai1` payload rides the sim's shot drain**: the
  request tuple (`Npc::wants_hostile_shot`) carries no ai slots yet, so the
  drain fills the two values the saucer pair needs (the deathray's owner
  slot + 1 — the drain knows each requester's index — and the missile's
  `ai1 = 20f`) and hands them to the pool's `spawn_hostile_ai`. The
  per-shot ai payload the shadow-hand spawn needs
  (`Projectile.RandomizeInsanityShadowFor`, `Projectile.cs:42408-42493`)
  is the follow-up that widens the request tuple.
## The held item's placement (S1-G-17, 2026-11-14)

`ItemCheck_ApplyUseStyle` (`Player.cs:50686-51375`) and
`ItemCheck_ApplyHoldStyle` (`:50275-50584`) set the held item's
`itemLocation` + `itemRotation` per use/hold style — the C# computes them
in the sim, the port computed them in the draw with a single generic arm.
Three real defects came out of that:

* The useStyle-1 swing's **middle third took the X sign from the swing
  start** (`itemLocation.X = position.X + width*0.5 - (frame.W*0.5 - num) *
  direction`, `Player.cs:50829`) — the C# only subtracts in the *start*
  third; the end (`:50742`) and the middle (`:50773`) add. The item jumped
  to the other side of the body in the middle of every swing.
* The useStyle 5 item's rotation was the raw mouse angle, not the C#'s
  `Player.itemRotation` (`atan2(aimY * direction, aimX * direction) -
  fullRotation`, `:47371-47378`) — off by PI when facing left (the same
  mirror the S1-G-16 composite arm needed).
* The rest anchor was the holdStyle-1 one for *every* hold style, and the
  use styles 2/6/7/9/11/12/14/15 rode the useStyle-1 arc.

The port now places the item per style (`render/player_layers.rs`'s
`use_item_placement` / `hold_item_placement`):

* the use styles 1 (the thirds + `item_rotation`), 2 (the `num11` table
  over the composite stretch), 3 (the thrust), 4 (the hold-up), 5 (the
  aim), 6/7 (the drinks), 9 (the bow — through the ported
  `GetFrontHandPosition`, `:50617-50647`), 11 (the `num13` table over the
  composite stretch), 12 (the guitar), 14 and 15;
* the hold styles 1, 2, 3, 4 (the umbrella), 5, 6 and 8.

The port's frame: `pos_x`/`pos_y` are `base.position`, `center_x` is
`base.Center.X`, `mounted_y` is `MountedCenter.Y` (`position.Y + height/2`
= `position.Y + 21`) and `headgear` is `Main.OffsetsPlayerHeadgear`
(`Main.cs:66638-66662`). The `gfxOffY` ease rides the anchor
(`PlayerDrawSet.cs:368`).

Deviations (deliberate, bounded):

* The useStyle 8 (the throw) keeps the useStyle-1 arc: the C#'s three
  phases compare the raw `itemAnimation` counter with the item's
  `useAnimation` (`:51199/:51226`) and the port's draw only carries the
  normalised fraction.
* The useStyle 13 (the rapier) keeps the useStyle-1 arc: the C# leaves
  `itemLocation` at the hold-style value (the branch sets no location,
  `:51174-51196`).
* The per-item nudges (the style-1 types 2330/2320/2341/671, the hold
  styles' torch/fishing-pole/staff specials, the biome torches) are not
  ported; the generic arms carry them.
* `mountOffset` is 0 and `gravDir` is 1 (the port has no mount offset and
  no gravity flip).

Tests: `render::player_layers::tests`'s four `s1_g_17_*` cases (the swing
thirds' X sign, the shoot style's item rotation, the hold styles' anchors
and the eat style's stretch table) — all mutation-checked (RED on the
pre-fix code).


## The throw and rapier item placement (S1-G-18, 2026-11-14)

Two more `ItemCheck_ApplyUseStyle` arms and one real bug from the
S1-G-16 composite work:

* The useStyle 8 (the throw) branch (`:51197-51273`) has three phases — the
  wind-up (the first ticks, while `itemAnimation` is at the item's
  `useAnimation`), the overshoot (`itemAnimation > useAnimation`, which the
  port's swing counter never reaches) and the swing arc
  (`num26 = 1 - itemAnimation/itemAnimationMax`). The item's anchor follows
  the phase (`MountedCenter + (num22 + PI/2).ToRotationVector2() * -2` for
  the wind-up, `... * (-5 * (1 - num26))` for the arc) and the draw rotates
  it a quarter turn (`PlayerDrawLayers.cs:3181-3189`). The port now carries
  the raw animation counters into the draw (`swing_anim_ticks`/
  `swing_max_ticks` — the port's swing timer runs in seconds, the C#'s
  `itemAnimation` in ticks) and places the item per phase.
* The useStyle 13 (the rapier) branch (`:51174-51196`) sets no location: the
  item keeps the hold-style anchor and is turned by the aim
  (`Player.itemRotation`). The port now does the same instead of riding the
  useStyle-1 arc.
* **The bug:** the umbrella's (and the throw's) `itemRotation` is
  `new Vector2(10 * direction, 10f).ToRotation() + PI/4` (`:50524`,
  `:51201`) — the XNA `ToRotation` is `atan2(Y, X)`, but the S1-G-16 port
  used `hypot`, i.e. the vector's *length* (14.14) instead of its angle. The
  umbrella's and the throw's poses were therefore rotated by a nonsense
  angle. Fixed to `atan2(10, 10 * direction)` in both the sim's composite
  arms and the draw.

Tests: `s1_g_18_the_throw_style_rides_its_wind_up_and_arc`,
`s1_g_18_the_rapier_keeps_the_hold_anchor` and
`s1_g_18_the_umbrella_rotation_is_the_vector_rotation` — all
mutation-checked (RED on the pre-fix code; the left-facing cases pin the
mirrored `atan2`, which is where the `hypot` slip showed).

## The draw phase order (S1-B-7, 2026-11-14)

`Main.DoDraw` (`Main.cs:61707-62507`) draws the world in a fixed
sequence; the port had one draw branch with no order assertion, and the
dropped items were drawn **before** the NPCs and the player — the C# draws
them last of the entity group (`Main.cs:62278`):

```
projectiles → the players (`:62256`) → the NPCs over the players (`:62263`)
→ the items (`:62278`) → the rain (`:62279`) → the gore/dust (`:62282`/`:62293`)
→ the waters (`:62300`) → the wires (`:62303`) → the projectiles over the
wires UI (`:62315`)
```

The port now draws the dropped items after the players and the NPCs
(`render/tiles.rs`: the items' pass moved behind the player passes), and
the draw passes carry a phase marker (`frame.rs`'s `draw_phase`,
`render/tiles.rs`'s `draw_phase`) so the order is assertable:
`the_draw_passes_run_in_the_csharp_order` pins the marker order — the
world pass's `npcs_behind_tiles → npcs → player → items` and the frame's
`sky → world → rain → wires → projectiles`. The markers move with the
passes, so a future reorder fails the test (mutation-checked: RED on the
pre-fix code).

Scope notes (the remaining divergences, all deliberate):

* The C# splits the NPCs into two buckets — `DoDraw_DrawNPCsOverTiles`
  (`:63301`, before the players) and `DrawCachedNPCs(DrawCacheNPCsOver-
  Players)` (`:62263`, after them). The port has one NPC bucket, at the
  "over the tiles" slot, so the NPCs that vanilla draws over the player
  are drawn under it.
* The C# splits the projectiles into four buckets (`CacheProjDraws`:
  behind the projectiles, over the players, over the NPCs, over the wires
  UI). The port has one bucket, at the "over the wires UI" slot, so the
  projectiles are drawn over the player.
* The C#'s leaves ride the particle system (`ParticleSystem_World_Over-
  Players`, `:62259`); the port draws them with the dust cluster
  (`frame.rs`'s leaf pass) — the same neighbourhood as the rain/sand.
* The gore pass (`Main.cs:62282`) is unported (the gore pool is empty).
## The scene-metrics zone chain (S1-L-1, 2026-11-14)

`SceneMetrics.CalculateZones` (`SceneMetrics.cs:660-710`) computes more
than the port carried: the depth bands (`ZoneSkyHeight`,
`ZoneOverworldHeight`, `BelowSurface`, `ZoneDirtLayerHeight`,
`ZoneRockLayerHeight`, `ZoneUnderworldHeight`, `:672-677`), the centre
tile's wall zones (`ZoneLihzhardTemple` 87, `ZoneGranite` 184/180,
`ZoneMarble` 183/178, `ZoneHive` 108/86, `ZoneGemCave` 48..53 and
`ZoneUndergroundDesert` — the desert + under the surface + a
sandstone/hardened-sand/223 wall + no `Main.wallHouse` wall, `:694-699`)
and the candle zones (`:706-708`). The port's `SceneMetrics` now carries
them, `SceneMetrics::calculate_wall_zones` reads the centre tile, and
`Player.UpdateBiomes`' chain (`Player.cs:16692-16730`) feeds the spawner's
`SpawnFlags`: before this, the dungeon/jungle/evil/temple/
underground-desert/meteor/graveyard/sandstorm arms in `GetSpawnRate`
(`NPC.cs:473-810`) were constants-off, so every zone-gated spawn rate
multiplier was dead.

Scope notes: the per-tile `SetSpawnFlagsForChosenTile`
(`NPC.cs:1050-1278` — the marble/granite proximity and the dual-dungeons
rescan) rides the per-candidate work; the moon-tower proximity zones
(`CloseEnoughTo*Tower`) ride the pillar/tower systems; `ZoneEvil` is the
port's merged corrupt-or-crimson flag (the C# keeps the two apart in some
arms).

Doc-truth fix: the research's music-box deviation (research/14's D9 — "the
vanilla scans the VISUAL screen rect") pointed at a stale line reference.
The arm is `SceneMetrics.cs:468-480`, INSIDE `ScanTiles` — the C# scans the
same 169×124 zone window the port scans, so the port's window is verbatim;
the port's comment now says so.

## The Deerclops' projectile family (S1-D-4b-5, 2026-11-14)

The ROADMAP's S1-D-4b-5 slice covers the Deerclops' two projectile
families: the aiStyle-157 ice spike (`Projectile.cs:51358-51477`) and the
Insanity Shadow's spawn (`Projectile.RandomizeInsanityShadowFor`,
`Projectile.cs:42408-42493`) — the spawn that feeds the aiStyle-187 arm
landed with S1-D-4b-1.

**The aiStyle-157 arm** (the 961; the 1041 rides the same style and has no
ported row). The arm's parameter row for the 961 (`:51376-51389`) is the
fade-in window 10, the fade-out from the 10th tick and the kill at the
20th; the first tick takes the rotation from the velocity and rolls one of
the sheet's five frames (`Main.rand.Next(5)`, `:51439`).

**The `Opacity` property** (`Projectile.cs:540-549`) is a view over
`alpha`, not a field of its own: the getter is `1 - alpha / 255` and the
setter writes `alpha = (int)Clamp((1 - value) * 255, 0, 255)`. The port
models it with the `opacity_of`/`alpha_of` helpers. The S1-D-4b-1 arm (the
aiStyle-133 Dark Mage marker) had carried the opacity as a separate slot
field; that field is gone and the arm writes the alpha, exactly as the
C#'s property does — the marker's alpha now runs 255 → 242 → 0 → 127 → 255
(the dying tick) instead of the separate opacity value.

**The shadow hand's spawn** now rides the C#'s pick
(`Projectile.RandomizeInsanityShadowFor`): the four cases are the arm's
four variations (`Projectile.cs:42592-42634`), each handing the arm the
variation's start age (0 / 180 / 300 / 390) and the angle, plus the
position and the velocity. The port's old spawn (a made-up ring of six
hands with a stand-in velocity) had no `ai` payload, so every shadow ran
the arm's variation 0 (the drift) — the arm's other three variations were
dead code.

**The spawn-site `ai0`/`ai1` payload** (`NewProjectile`'s trailing
arguments, `Projectile.cs:10862-10863`) rides the new
`Npc::wants_hostile_shot_ai` request list (`HostileShotAi`): the shots
whose call site passes a non-zero `ai0`/`ai1`. The list joins the plain
`wants_hostile_shot` one (whose call sites pass zero). The S1-D-4b-4
slicer's per-kind table in the sim's drain is retired: the Saucer deathray
now carries its owner slot from the spawn site (`ai0 = whoAmI + 1`, the
C#'s own value — the port's `Npc::slot` is the sim's current index) and
the missile its `ai1 = 20f`.

Two more Deerclops divergences fell out of the port:

* **The rubble is the 962, not the 961** (`NPC.cs:44463`: the chunk, the
  aiStyle-1 flight, `ai1 = 6 + Next(6)`), and the port now has the 962's
  row (`:9199-9206`). The port's rubble shot the 961 (the forward spike)
  instead.
* **The "blizzard" state spawns no projectile** (`NPC.cs:44285-44320`):
  it chills the player (the buff 32, 720 ticks, inside 800 px). The port
  fired a damage-0 spike at the Deerclops instead — a stand-in with no
  vanilla counterpart, now gone. The buff itself is the buff row
  (S1-E-7).

Deviations:

* **The dust and the sound are SKIPPED** (the arm's `:51431-51464` and
  `:51453-51461`) — no dust/sound layer. The frame roll is kept: it is
  the visible state.
* **The C#'s rejection loop never rejects in the port**
  (`Projectile.cs:42476-42493`): the only player IS the target, and the
  C# skips the target in that check, so the pick runs once.
* **The C#'s spike cadence and tile scan are the port's stand-in**: the
  forward/both-sides rows (`MakeSpikesForward`/`MakeSpikesBothSides`,
  `NPC.cs:44466-44534`) and `FindBestY` (`:44586-44640`) pick the spike's
  tile row from the ground scan; the port fires its own rows at the
  Deerclops' feet (the `ai1` scale factor is the C#'s). The rubble's
  `ShootRubbleUp` tile scan and up-bias (`:44448-44465`) are the same
  stand-in. The follow-up row is the cadence row.

## The invasion surface band (S1-F-18, 2026-11-14)

`Spawner.ShouldSpawnInvasionEnemies` (`NPC.cs:442-463`) compares
`position.Y < Main.worldSurface * 16.0 + NPC.sHeight` — and `NPC.sHeight` is
**1200** (`NPC.cs:6769`), not the 200 the port used. The invasion's
above-surface band was therefore ~6× too narrow; it now reads
`crate::spawner::S_HEIGHT` (the port's constant already carried the
vanilla's 1200) and the window test pins both edges (3000 px below the
surface spawns, 3200 px does not — the test world's surface is row 120 =
px 1920). The ±3000 px window around `invasionX` and the town-NPC fallback
stay as they were (the latter rides the town roster).

## The drop-rate report (S1-E-15, 2026-11-14)

`IItemDropRule.ReportDroprates` and its data (`DropRateInfo`,
`DropRateInfoChainFeed`) are ported into `tr_core::loot`: the trait gains
`report_droprates` (the default reports nothing, so the rule classes that
S1-E-14 still has to port compile unchanged), and the port's rule classes
report with the C#'s formulas — `CommonDrop`'s
`(numerator / denominator) * the parent's rate`, `CommonDropWithRerolls`'s
`1 - (1 - numerator/denominator)^rerolls`, `OneFromOptionsDrop`'s shared
per-option rate, the nested rules' (expert/master/extra-gel) pairs, and
`DropOneByOne`'s chunk-scaled stack range. `Chains.ReportDroprates`
scales per chain kind (`Chains.cs:24-30`: `TryIfFailedRandomRoll` feeds
`1 - the parent's own rate`; `:50-56`/`:76-82`: `TryIfSucceeded` and
`TryIfDoesntFillConditions` feed the parent's rate itself — corrected
2026-11-18 with S1-E-14a, the earlier port scaled every kind by `1 - rate`).
`LeadingConditionRule` reports its chains at rate 1
(`LeadingConditionRule.cs:22-26`, S1-E-14a). `ItemDropDatabase::report_droprates` is
`BestiaryDatabase.ExtractDropsForNPC` (`BestiaryDatabase.cs:70-88`): the
NPC's rules report their rows with a fresh feed (the rate 1.0) and the
globals stay out.

The bestiary's "Drops:" list now prints those rows instead of the 4-row
hand-written table (`ui/bestiary.rs`) — the stack range + the rate, in
`UIBestiaryInfoItemLine.GetDropInfo`'s format (`UIBestiaryInfoItemLine.cs:78-104`)
with `Utils.PrettifyPercentDisplay`'s trimmed percentage
(`Utils.cs:1105-1109`).

Scope notes: the C#'s condition lists (`DropRateInfo.conditions`) and the
chains' `hideLootReport` flag are not modelled by the port, so the rows
carry no condition text and the chained rows always print; the town-NPC and
critter providers, the search filters, the sorting, the flavour and the MP
kill-sync ride the town/MP subsystems. `MasterModeDropOnAllPlayers` sites
pass `this._masterModeDropRng` (`ItemDropDatabase.cs:15` = 4) but the
generated rows carry the factory default 1 (pre-existing since M4-LOOT-2,
kept for row stability — S1-E-14a leaves it unchanged; the per-player
master-drop chance is 1/1 instead of 1/4 until a dedicated fix).

## The hurting-tile family (S1-E-13a, 2026-11-14)

`crates/tr-app/src/touch_damage.rs` now carries the vanilla's tile-contact
hazards in full. `Collision.CanTileHurt` (`Collision.cs:3206-3225`) reads the
four `TileID.Sets` tables (`TileID.cs:605-609` — `TouchDamageDestroyTile`,
`Suffocate`, `TouchDamageHot`, `TouchDamageBleeding` and the
`TouchDamageImmediate` value table), all of which the S1-F-8 generator already
emits into `tr-core/src/tiledata/sets.rs`: the hand-written nine-row
immediate table is gone, and the generated bitsets replace the "no ported
members yet" note the module used to carry. `Collision.HurtTiles`
(`Collision.cs:3115-3204`) adds the suffocate shrink (`num6 = 2`,
`:3155-3163`) — the sands pull the box in by two pixels on every side, and a
sloped suffocating tile is skipped outright (`:3164-3169`).

`Player.ApplyTouchDamage` (`Player.cs:28977-29019`) is ported arm by arm:
the rolled immediate damage (`Main.DamageVar(num, -luck)`), the burning
(buff 67 for 20 ticks) and bleeding (buff 30 for 600-1200 ticks) buffs that
fire only when the hit was *not* swallowed — the C#'s `flag` is set when
`Hurt` returns 0, so an immune player does not burn or bleed — the
`suffocateDelay` counter (five ticks in the sand, the sixth suffocates with
buff 68) and the destroy-on-touch `WorldGen.KillTile` for the four thorn
tiles. The counter is the C#'s `byte` field (`Player.cs:2318`) and keeps the
source's quirk: it only resets when another hurt tile is touched, not when
the player walks out of the sand.

Deliberate deviations:

1. `Player.fireWalk` (the Obsidian Skull) has no ported accessor, so the hot
   arm always fires — the C#'s `player == null || !player.fireWalk`
   (`:3220`) with a player that cannot walk on fire.
2. `Player.shimmering` (the C#'s gate around the whole pass,
   `Player.cs:27608`) has no ported player state, so the pass always runs.
3. `Player.TouchedTiles` (the movement-traced fallback in `GetHurtTile`)
   is still not modelled — the port's box scan covers the same area with the
   source's own ±1 margin.
4. `ImmunityCooldownID.TileContactDamage` collapses into the port's single
   `hurt_cd` (the port carries one immunity window, not the C#'s per-source
   array).
5. The bleeding duration's roll rides the port's `item_rng` stream (the C#'s
   `Main.rand`), the same stream the damage roll already used.

Out (the rest of S1-E-13): `HitTiles`/`HitTilesInACircle`, `StickyTiles` +
`Player.StickyMovement`, `SwitchTiles`, `BuildTileContacts`,
`noSlopeCollision`, `AdvancedTileCollision` and `DrownCollision`/
`GetWaterLine`.
## The goblin family's ids (S1-D-3d, 2026-11-14)

The port's four goblin kinds carried **each other's** vanilla `NPCID`: the
kind named `GoblinThief` sat on the type 26 (the vanilla's **peon**), the
`GoblinWarrior` on the 27 (the **thief**), the `GoblinArcher` on the 28
(the **warrior**) and the `GoblinPeon` on the 111 (the **archer**) — the
peon/thief/warrior/archer cycle rotated by one.

The C#'s rows (`ID/NPCID.cs:10729-10733`/`:10899`, the `SetDefaults` arms
`NPC.cs:15644-15730`):

| kind | type | HP | damage | defense | kb resist | value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| the peon | 26 | 60 | 12 | 4 | 0.8 | 100 |
| the thief | 27 | 80 | 20 | 6 | 0.7 | 200 |
| the warrior | 28 | 110 | 25 | 8 | 0.5 | 150 |
| the archer | 111 | 80 | 20 | 6 | 0.7 | 200 |

The port's stats rows followed the **ids** (the thief carried the peon's
60 HP, the warrior and the peon the thief's 80, the archer the warrior's
110), and the bestiary's `net_id` — the C#'s `NPC.type` — carried the
same rotation. The loot tables key on that net id, so a "Goblin Thief"
dropped the peon's loot and credited the peon's bestiary entry.

The fix moves the ids and the stats back onto the names: the bestiary's
four `net_id`s follow the C# (`cs_id` reads them through the S1-F-3
fallback), and the stats rows carry the C#'s values per name. The port's
`docs/NPC_AI_TAXONOMY.md` had the C#'s mapping all along ("26/27/28 |
Goblin Peon/Thief/Warrior | 60/80/110 | 12/20/25 | 4/6/8") — the code
had drifted from the doc.

Two duplicate match arms died with the fix: the stats functions carried a
second, by-name set of goblin rows *after* the by-id set, so the correct
values were unreachable (`unreachable pattern` warnings). The dead rows
are gone and the effective rows carry the C#'s values.

The port's own wire ids (the `NpcKind` u16 roster: 57/58/59/60) and the
sprite sheets (`NPC_27`/`NPC_28`/`NPC_111`/`NPC_26`) were already keyed by
name and are untouched — the kinds, their art and their ids now agree.
