`AI_003_Fighters` (`NPC.cs:55856-59800`) is the vanilla's ground-fighter
machine: the per-type walk groups, the shooters' stop-and-fire cycle and
the boss riders. The port ran every kind that rides its walker step at one
speed — the skeleton's 0.8 for the cave walkers, the pirates and the
martians, the zombie's own 0.6, the shooters' 5.0 — while the C#'s arm
carries a per-type velocity cap per group:

| group | cap | kinds (the C#'s rows) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the `num107` default (`:58322-58374`) | 1f | the zombie (3), the undead miner (44), the goblin warrior (28) |
| the `num83` group (`:57606-57691`) | 1.5f | the skeleton (21), the goblin peon (26); the gray grunt 1.8, the giga zapper 2.25, the vortex rifleman 6, the vortex soldier 4 |
| the cap-2 group (`:57554-57578`) | 2f | the goblin thief (27), the pirate deckhand (212) |
| the cap-3 group (`:57520-57552`) | 3f | the pirate captain's mate (213) |
| the shooters' group (`:59717-59750`) | 1f | the pirate captain (216), the martian officer (383); the pirate archer 2, the corsair 1.5, the scrambler/ray gunner 2, the stardust spider/soldier 2, the vortex hunter 4, the martian walker 4 |
| the Martian engineer's own arm (`:58032-58069`) | 1.5f | the martian engineer (386) |

`NpcKind::ai3_walk_speed` is the port's table; the zombie, the cave
walkers (the skeleton, the undead miner, the pirate deckhand, the pirate
captain's mate), the goblins and the shooters read it instead of their
hard-coded speed. The kinds whose arm is bespoke (the pillar mobs, the
vortex family, the Goblin Archer) keep their own speed and are not in the
table.

Deviations:

* **The C#'s acceleration model is not ported**: the vanilla ramps the
  velocity toward the cap at 0.07/tick (0.09/0.08/0.5/1.0 for the shooter
  rows) and decays it ×0.8 past the cap; the port's walker step sets the
  velocity to the cap directly. The cap itself — the value the C#'s
  acceleration converges to — is the port's table.
* **The C#'s scale factor on the `num107` group** (`num107 *= 1f + (1f -
  this.scale)`, `:58374-58376`) rides the kind's `scale` (the vanilla's
  humanoid scales are 0.9-1.1); the port's scale is 1 for these kinds, so
  the factor is 1 — except for the kinds whose scale the port does not
  carry (the goblins' 0.9/0.95/1.1), which the group does not scale
  anyway.

## The drowning family (S1-E-13b, 2026-11-14)

`crates/tr-app/src/collision.rs` ports `Collision.DrownCollision`
(`Collision.cs:1383-1432`) and the two water-line helpers
(`GetWaterLine` `:1498-1544`, `GetWaterLineIterate` `:1551-1570`). The
drown probe is the C#'s: the 10x12 box at the entity's head (the centre
column, `Position.Y + height/2 - 6` for the vanilla gravity, `:1385-1400`),
the liquid's surface offset (`(256 - liquid) / 32 * 2`, `:1421-1423`), the
lava and shimmer exclusion (the honey drowns, `:1416`) and the solid-floor
row (the gravity-side row of the scan, `:1409`/`:1416`) — the `includeSlopes`
mode lifts that exclusion for the sloped and half-brick blocks, exactly like
the C#'s `blockType() != 0` arm.

`Player::check_drowning` (`Player.cs:23191-23281`) replaces the port's
"the player is in water" stand-in with that probe: the breath meter now
drains only while the **head** is under the surface, and refills with the
C#'s 3 ticks per tick (`breathCD`/`breathCDMax` kept). Before this row the
port's breath drained whenever the wet flags said "somewhere in water", so
wading through a shallow pool cost air.

Deliberate deviations:

1. The C#'s accessory arms (the Merman armour 250/4275, the breathing reed,
   the gills, the shimmering and the mount 4) have no ported counterparts —
   the port has no accessory system for them, so the probe's own flag
   decides.
2. The C#'s drowning bubbles and the drowning death sound (23) ride the
   effect and audio systems, which are out of scope here.
3. `Utils.Clamp(value, 0, Main.maxTilesY - 40)` folds a negative bound back
   onto itself for the small test worlds; the port clamps the bound at zero
   instead (the scan then runs empty either way).
4. The port runs the breath drain inside `update_survival` (the merged
   life-regen step); the C#'s `CheckDrowning` sits later in `Player.Update`
   (`:27655`, after `StickyMovement`).

Out (the rest of S1-E-13): `HitTiles`/`HitTilesInACircle`, `SwitchTiles`,
`BuildTileContacts`, `noSlopeCollision` and `AdvancedTileCollision`.
## The sticky-surface family (S1-E-13c, 2026-11-16)

`crates/tr-app/src/collision.rs::sticky_tiles` ports `Collision.StickyTiles`
(`Collision.cs:3362-3435`): the ±1-tile scan window clamped to
`Main.maxTilesY - 40` (`:3369-3384`), the cobweb (51) arm with its zero margin
and `16.01` tall box (`:3396-3406`), and the honey-block (229) arm gated on
`slope() == 0` (`:3410`) with the 1 px margin plus the half brick's `+8` / `-8`
shrunken box (`:3414-3423`). The source's inline `Main.rand.Next(30)` type-30
web puff (`:3401`, `:3425`) is drawn **inside** the probe, at the source's
position relative to the return, and handed back as a flag: the caller owns
`Main.dust`, so `Player::sticky_movement` queues it. The 229 arm's copy of that
`if` tests `Main.tile[i, j].type == 51`, which is always false there and
short-circuits before the `Next(30)`, so the port passes `false` — drawing it
would add a stream step the C# never takes.

`Player::sticky_movement` (`Player.cs:22910-23087`) keeps the source's order:
the `Next(20,100)` / `Next(80,300)` break roll for `stickyBreak`
(`:22938-22954`) — the C#'s bitwise `|` means the draw happens even when the
`flag` cart test short-circuits the assignment — then the cart-above-5-px
early return (`:22956-22958`), `fallStart` (`:22960`), the honey's jump
exemption (`:22961-22964`), the gel/slime mount's halving with its `0.0025`
floor (`:22965-22972`), the `±1` X cap with the `0.85`/`0.6` damp and the
`±1`/`-5` Y cap with the `0.96`/`0.3` damp (`:22975-23028`), and the type-153
honey puffs on the hit row plus the two rows below (`:23030-23081`) with their
`Next(0,6)` scale / `velocity *= 0.1` / `noGravity` tail. The tick only has
`&World`, so the tile kill (`WorldGen.KillTile`, `:22949`) and the puffs are
queued and drained in `world_sim/player.rs` — the same `pending_sparks`
pattern the minecart uses; the drain runs `DustPool::new_dust` on the
`UpdatePlayers` stream, so the pool's own rolls stay interleaved exactly as the
C# interleaves `Main.rand`.

Call site: `Player::update_with_grapple` invokes it between the grapple block
and `check_drowning`, matching `Player.cs:27653-27655`
(`GrappleMovement` → `StickyMovement` → `CheckDrowning`).

Deliberate deviations:

1. **No shimmer gate.** `Player.shimmering` (`:22912-22915`) has no port
   counterpart yet (the shimmer absorption pass is unported), so the early
   return is absent rather than always-false.
2. **No gravity flip.** The C# mirrors the Y drag on `gravDir` (`:22991`,
   `:23010`); the port has no gravity flip, so only the `gravDir == 1` arm
   (`:23012-23027`) runs, matching the vanilla's default `1f` (`Player.cs:1956`).
3. **Hook multi-player gates folded.** `whoAmI == Main.myPlayer` (`:22936`)
   collapses (the port is single-player) and the `Main.netMode == 1` break
   replication (`:22950-22953`) is net-only.
4. **`stickyBreak` survives a respawn.** The C# writes the counter at exactly
   four sites, all inside `StickyMovement` (`:22938`, `:22948`, `:23085`);
   `Player.Spawn` never clears it, so the port's revive path does not either.
## The remaining collision family (S1-E-13d, 2026-11-16)

`crates/tr-app/src/collision.rs` gains the five functions S1-E-13's parent row
still listed after the 13a/13b/13c splits.

* `no_slope_collision` (`Collision.cs:2033-2133`) is `tile_collision` with the
  slope gates removed (`:2059`'s solid conjunct has no `slope()` arm at all).
  The up arm keeps its `+ 0.01f` (`:2124`); the down arm has no `gravDir` term
  (`:2088` is bare `vector4.Y - (vector3.Y + Height)`), unlike
  `TileCollision`'s caller-supplied `gravDir`.
* `advanced_tile_collision` (`:4422-4566`) keeps the slope gates but adds the
  `forcedIgnoredTiles` conjunct (`:4449`), the neighbour-slope exemptions on the
  two side arms (`:4514-4518` skips a slope 2/4 tile to the left,
  `:4534-4538` a slope 1/3 tile to the right) and the `gravDir`-dependent
  nudges — `-0.01f` on the down arm when `gravDir == -1` (`:4507`), `+0.01f` on
  the up arm when `gravDir == 1` (`:4557`).
* `hit_tiles` / `hit_tiles_in_a_circle` (`:3063-3108`, `:3016-3061`) share one
  scan. Its box test is **inclusive** on all four edges (`:3101`), unlike
  `TileCollision`'s strict comparisons, and the horizontal clamp stops at
  `Main.maxTilesX`, not `maxTilesX - 1` (`:3027`). The circle arm adds the
  centre-distance gate `(centre - (tile + (8, 8))).Length() < (Width + Height) / 4`
  (`:3054`).
* `build_tile_contacts` (`:2135-2290`) enumerates `TileContact`s: the position
  truncates to whole pixels first (`:2137`), the window is `(x - 1) / 16 - 1 ..
  (x + 1 + w) / 16 + 1` and `(y - 1) / 16 - 1 .. (y + 3 + h) / 16 + 1`
  (`:2140-2143`), the Left/Right arms exclude slopes 3/1 and 4/2 respectively
  (`:2177`/`:2181`), and the Top/Bottom arms switch on the slope with the
  slope-3/4 inset variants (`:2232-2257`) and a diagonal `BottomLeft`/
  `BottomRight` fallback when the box only grazes a corner (`:2260-2287`).
  Overlaps are `(int)Math.Max(Math.Min(...) - Math.Max(...) + 0.5f, 1f)`.

`tile_dust_amount` ports `WorldGen.KillTile_GetTileDustAmount`
(`WorldGen.cs:66597-66685`) so the hit scan's effect half is expressible.

Deliberate deviations:

1. **`HitTiles` never destroys a tile, because the source does not either.**
   Both call sites answer a hit with `WorldGen.KillTile(i, j, fail: true,
   effectOnly: true)`; that overload runs `CheckTileBreakability`, the
   item/furniture-rack drops and the dust loop, then **returns** at
   `WorldGen.cs:63704-63707` before any removal, framing or item spawn. The
   port therefore returns the hit cells and `tile_dust_amount` gives the counts
   the C# would spawn. `tr_core::edit::kill_tile` is the *destructive*
   `KillTile` and must not be called here: doing so would break tiles the
   vanilla only shakes.
2. **The dust and the shake sound are not spawned.** The port has no tile-dust
   layer (the same gap the failing mine tick records at
   `world_sim/editing.rs:1350`) and no `SoundEngine` handle in
   `collision.rs`. `tile_dust_amount` is the seam a dust layer would call;
   until it exists the scan is a pure geometry query.
3. **`advanced_tile_collision` and `no_slope_collision` are unexercised.**
   Their only callers are `NPC.Collision_MoveSandshark` (`NPC.cs:92732`) and
   `NPC.Collision_MoveSnailOnSlopes` (`:92782`); the sandshark and snail NPC
   families are unported, so both are marked `#[allow(dead_code)]` with the
   missing caller named in place rather than inventing one. They are covered
   by unit tests, not by gameplay. `build_tile_contacts` is not among them: it
   landed with its caller in S1-E-13e (`ApplyConveyorBeltMovementToVelocity`),
   and that branch's copy is the one in the tree.
4. **The `Main.tile[i ± 1, j] == null → new Tile()` allocations**
   (`:4514-4517`, `:4534-4537`, `:63533-63536`) fold out: the port's tile array
   is dense, so a missing neighbour reads as an empty tile through
   `world.tile()`'s `Option`, which is what the allocation would have produced.

## The Brain of Cthulhu's machine (S1-D-3e, 2026-11-14)

`AI_054` (`NPC.cs:32370-32656`) is the Brain of Cthulhu's family machine:
the creeper swarm's shield, the blink machine (the Brain teleports around
the player, fading out and in), the retreat when its swarm dies and the
despawn ramp when the player leaves the Crimson zone. The port ran a
stand-in — a 60-tick drift toward the player plus a 9-px dash.

The arm now carries the C#'s machine:

* **the normal phase** (`:32522-32527`): the velocity points at the player
  at 1 px/tick (the getGood world's 3);
* **the blink** (`:32532-32599`): the `localAI[1]` timer (120 + `Next(300)`
  ticks, re-rolled every tick) picks a tile 12-40 tiles from the player
  (the signs are random, the player's velocity leads the pick, the tile
  must be free of solid blocks and — after the 75th try — in line of sight
  of the player), the fade-in (alpha + 5/tick to 255) teleports the Brain
  onto it and the fade-out (alpha − 5/tick) returns to the normal phase;
* **the retreat** (`:32401-32518`): with no Creeper left the Brain switches
  to `ai[0] = -1` and drifts at 8 px through the 50/51 blend; its timer
  (60 + `Next(120)` ticks) picks a tile 10-12 tiles out (no sight gate) and
  the `-2`/`-3` states fade the Brain in on it and back out;
* **the despawn ramp** (`:32619-32636`): a dead player or a player out of
  the Crimson zone sinks the Brain (`velocity.Y += (localAI[3] - 60) * 0.25`)
  and fades it out.

The creeper swarm's spawn and the shield stay in the sim's pass
(`world_sim/npcs.rs`: the 20 Creepers + `dont_take_damage` while one
lives); the arm's "no Creeper left" test needs the live count, so the sim
writes it into `Npc::brain_local[2]` (the C#'s `num818`).

Deviations:

* **The gore/dust burst is SKIPPED** (`:32401-32419`) — no dust/gore layer.
* **The MP-only branches use the single-player values** (`Main.netMode !=
  0`): the port has no multiplayer arm, so the blink's period, the fade
  rates and the "crimson boss" bookkeeping are the single-player ones.
* **`justHit` rides the port's `hurt_cd`** (the hit cooldown) — the C#'s
  flag is a single tick, the port's window is the timer the other arms
  use for the same purpose (the port's convention, documented in the
  Goblin Archer's arm).
* **The sound cues are SKIPPED** (the retreat's roar `SoundID 3`/`15`,
  `:32408`/`:32418`, and the teleport's `Item8`, `:32505`/`:32622`) —
  the arm carries no audio seam (the port's convention for the boss
  machines; the S1-D-3e audit, 2026-11-18).
* **The `getGoodWorld` arms fold to the classic values** — the normal
  drift's 3-px speed (`:32538-32541`), the 40-Creeper swarm
  (`GetBrainOfCthuluCreepersCount`, `:50936-50943`) and the
  `brainOfGravity` write (`:32402-32405`) are the for-the-worthy
  branches; the port's boss arms run constants-off (no difficulty
  flags), so the classic 1-px drift and the 20-Creeper swarm stand.

**Audit (2026-11-18, `task/S1-D-3-aistyle54`, code-only mode).** A
line-by-line re-read of the whole `AI_054` block against `update_brain`
confirmed the machine (the swarm init/shield/count seam, the 50/51
retreat blend, the `60 + Next(120)` / `120 + Next(300)` timers re-rolled
every tick, the 10-12 / 12-40 tile picks with the sign rolls, the
velocity lead, the try-101 acceptance and the sight gate after the 75th
try, the ±25 / ±5 fades, the despawn ramp). Two real defects were fixed
surgically:

1. **The 6000-px Manhattan despawn gate was missing** (`:32387-32399`:
   `Math.Abs(center.X - player.Center.X) + Math.Abs(center.Y -
   player.Center.Y) > 6000f` → `active = false`, `life = 0`). The arm
   now deactivates (`hp = 0`) before any machine tick; the boundary is
   the C#'s strict `>` (exactly 6000 lives). The generic `tick_despawn`
   pass does not cover it — its only writer is the aiStyle-4 arm.
2. **The normal drift's f32 order** (`:32549-32551`): the C# computes
   the reciprocal first (`num816 = num817 / num816`) and then multiplies
   (`delta * num816`); the port ran `dx / d * speed`, which rounds one
   ulp away on some inputs. Witness: dx = 100, dy = 72 → the
   reciprocal-first product is `0.8115344`, the divide-first
   `0.81153435`. The arm now scales by the reciprocal.

Witness tests WRITTEN, NOT RUN (code-only mode — no compiler invoked):
`s1_d_3e_tests::{s1_d_3e_audit_the_brain_despawns_beyond_6000_manhattan_px,
s1_d_3e_audit_the_normal_drift_scales_by_the_reciprocal}`. The RNG
argument: the fixes add no draws (the despawn gate returns before any
roll; the reciprocal reorders arithmetic only), so the `UpdateNpcs`
stream order is unchanged — the per-tick draw sequence stays
`Next(300)` → (on fire) the pick's `Next(12,41)`×2 + `Next(2)`×2 per
try, and the retreat's optional `Next(5)` → `Next(120)` → the pick's
`Next(10,13)`×2 + `Next(2)`×2.

## The Skeletron head's machine (S1-D-3f, 2026-11-14)

`AI_011` (`NPC.cs:21919-22298`) is the Skeletron head's family machine:
the two hands' spawn, the spin state, the charge, the enraged day-time
state and the despawn. The port ran an EoC-shaped v1 — a 480-tick hover
into an 8-px dash — and the head never spawned its hands (the hand's own
arm was ported but nothing created the hands).

The arm now carries the C#'s machine:

* **the spin state (`ai[1] == 0`, `:22019-22117`)**: the `ai[2]` timer
  (800 ticks → the charge), the rotation (`velocity.X / 15`) and the hover
  acceleration — the 250-px band above/below the player, the 0.02/0.05
  accelerations and the 2/8 caps (the expert's 0.03/0.07 and 4/9.5);
* **the charge (`ai[1] == 1`, `:22118-22244`)**: the defense drops by 10,
  the timer (400 ticks → the spin) and the 1.5-px rush (the expert's 3.5
  with the per-distance ramp and the hand-count share);
* **the enraged state (`ai[1] == 2`, `:22245-22259`)**: the day-time (or
  the type-68) turns the head invulnerable — the damage and the defense
  9999 — and it rushes at 8 px;
* **the despawn (`ai[1] == 3`, `:22260-22270`)**: a dead player or one
  2000 px away sinks the head and damps it;
* **the expert's spin shot** (`:21978-22018`): every 80 ticks (40 with no
  hand left) the head fires a **Skull (270)** — the projectile's row is
  new (`Projectile.cs:3558-3566`: 26x26, the aiStyle-1 flight, penetrate
  3, alpha 255, hostile).

The hands' spawn rides the sim's pass (the C#'s `ai[0] == 0` init,
`:21924-21941`): the lower hand (`ai[0] = -1`) and the upper hand
(`ai[0] = 1`, `ai[3] = 150`). The live hand count — the C#'s `num168` —
rides the head's `ai[3]` (the sim's write), because the arm reads it for
the expert's shot cadence and the charge's speed.

Deviations:

* **The dust is SKIPPED** (`:22280-22296`) — no dust layer.
* **The sounds are SKIPPED** (the spawn cue, the spin cue and the charge
  cue) — no sound layer.
* **The red-hat adjustments** (`RedHatSkeletronAdjustmentsEnabled`, the
  `flag21` rows) are the world-seed flags the port does not carry; the
  getGood world's rows (the 40-creeper count, the 0.8 spin period) ride
  the classic values.
* **The MP-only branches** (`Main.netMode != 0`) use the single-player
  values.

## The King Slime's machine (S1-D-3g, 2026-11-14)

`AI_015_KingSlime` (`NPC.cs:43121-43414`) is the King Slime's family
machine: the hop cycle, the shrink/grow teleport, the hp-scaled body and
the minion batches. The port ran a simplified arm — a hop on a timer, a
stand-in teleport next to the player, a fixed body — and it spawned **a
minion on every landing**, while the C#'s batches come every 5 % of the
hp (1-3 slimes, `Next(1, 4)`).

The arm now carries the C#'s machine:

* **the hop cycle** (`:43285-43326`): the grounded timer runs at 2/tick
  plus the hp-scaled additions (the 0.8/0.6/0.4/0.2/0.1 life bands), the
  hop itself is the -8/-6/-13 jump with the 4/4.5/3.5 push, and the air
  control is the 0.2 push (or the 0.93 damping) toward the facing;
* **the teleport** (`:43177-43211`, `:43219-43284`): the player out of
  sight for 300 ticks shrinks the King Slime (the scale ramp over 60
  ticks), it blinks onto the picked spot and grows back (30 ticks). The
  spot comes from `AI_015_KingSlime_FindTeleportSpot` (`:43087-43119`):
  a solid (or platform) tile with clear air below and a sight line to the
  player, in the 10/7 ring around the player and then the 6/2 one; the
  anti-cheese case (out of sight for 360 ticks or the player 2000 px away)
  lands on the player instead;
* **the hp-scaled body** (`:43340-43356`): `num9 = life / lifeMax * 0.5 +
  0.75` drives both the draw scale and the 98x92 box — the port's new
  `Npc::size_override` carries the per-NPC box (the C#'s `base.width`/
  `base.height`);
* **the minion batches** (`:43357-43395`): every 5 % of the hp the King
  Slime spawns 1-3 slimes (the `ai[3]` hp latch).

Deviations:

* **The dust and the gore are SKIPPED** (`:43253-43281`, `:43327-43339`) —
  no dust/gore layer.
* **The MP-only branches use the single-player values.**
* **`NPC.timeLeft` is not ported**: the port's NPCs carry no despawn timer,
  so the C#'s "the closing timer clears the state" arm (`:43212-43218`) and
  the `timeLeft > 10` gate on the teleport (`:43180`) ride the normal
  machine.
* **The getGood world's rows** (the shrinking scale factor, the 6-px air
  control) are the classic values — the port carries no world-seed flag.
* **The minions' `ai[0] = -1000 * Next(3)` / `ai[1] = -1`** (`:43386-43388`)
  ride the port's slime spawn: the slimes' own machine (`AI_001_Slimes`) is
  not ported yet.
* **The minion positions** stay the sim's (the surface near the King
  Slime) rather than the C#'s random offsets inside its box.

## The wiring tools (S1-L-6b1, 2026-11-14)

The wiring is now placeable in play: `tr-core/src/edit.rs` grows
`place_wire`/`kill_wire` (the C#'s four `WorldGen.PlaceWire*`/`KillWire*`
functions — one per `Tile.wire*` bit, `WorldGen.cs:58111-58230` — folded

(`Collision.SwitchTiles`, `Player.cs:32177/32339/34823`), the pressure-plate

## The Deerclops' ice-spike rows (S1-D-4b-5b, 2026-11-14)

`AI_123_Deerclops_MakeSpikesForward`/`MakeSpikesBothSides` +
`TryMakingSpike` + `TryMakingSpike_FindBestY` (`NPC.cs:44466-44534`,
`:44575-44640`) are the Deerclops' signature attack: the spikes rain down
on the ground near the player, in volleys.

The port fired a stand-in — all twenty spikes at once, from the Deerclops'
feet, straight up. The arm now carries the C#'s shape:

* **the forward row** (state 1, `:44466-44500`): from the 36th tick, every
  fourth tick makes four spikes (the row's spread is 20 tiles);
* **the both-sides row** (state 4, `:44502-44532`): from the 56th tick,
  every second tick makes the row's spikes on both sides (the spread is 15
  tiles);
* **the spike's landing row** (`:44586-44640`): `FindBestY` walks the
  column toward the player's feet and keeps the walkable row closest to
  them, then walks up through the solid tiles and down to the first
  walkable one;
* **the spike's flight** (`:44582`): the `(0, -1)` vector rotated by
  `whichOne * dir * 0.7 * (PI / 4 / howMany)` and the `ai1` scale factor
  (`0.1 + rand * 0.1 + xOffset * 1.1 / howMany`).

The two tile probes the C#'s helper uses ride with it:
`WorldGen.ActiveAndWalkableTile` (`WorldGen.cs:70300-70318` — the tile is
active, solid and not framed off) and `WorldGen.SolidTile`
(`:70111-70132` — the full solid block, no slope and no top-only tile).

The rubble's own tile scan (`AI_123_Deerclops_ShootRubbleUp`,
`:44448-44465`) is still the port's stand-in — the follow-up row.

## The switch bridge (S1-L-6b2, 2026-11-14)

`crates/tr-app/src/collision.rs::switch_tiles` ports `Collision.SwitchTiles`
(`Collision.cs:3227-3360`): the entity→switch scan over the pressure plates
(135), the land mine (210), the geyser trap (443) and the projectile
pressure pad (442). The C#'s shape is kept — the ±1-margin box around the
entity, the type-442 projectile-pad branch (the four frame rects and the
`Utils.FloatIntersect` test, `Utils.cs:982-989`), the "the entity moved onto
it" rule (the entity's box must reach the tile's `y + 12` line and its old
box must not have been over it) and the frame-row table that picks who may
trigger which plate (the rows 2/3/4/6/7 answer only the player, row 5 answers
nobody).

The player's call site runs in the fixed step (`Player.cs:28274-28275`, the
`objType` 5 call) and reads the new `Player.old_x`/`old_y` — the C#'s
`Entity.oldPosition` (`Player.cs:28071`), captured before the tick's
movement. The tile-use arm is the new `edit::TileInteraction::HitSwitch`:
using a lever (132), a switch (136) or a timer (144) trips the wiring
(`Player.cs:32171-32179`), which the app answers with `Wiring::hit_switch`.

Deliberate deviations:

1. The scan's answer is the C#'s return value: only the pressure plates
   consume the entity — the mine and the geyser arms `continue` the scan
   (`Collision.cs:3319`/`:3326`), so they fire their effect without
   consuming it. The port keeps that shape.
2. The row-7 pressure plate's break (`WorldGen.KillTile`, `:3348-3352`)
   drops the plate's item; the port's core has no item pool, so the drop
   travels back to the app as `SwitchOutcome::dropped` and is spawned there.
3. The C#'s net messages (59/13/17) are out — the local wiring state is the
   truth.

Out (the rest of S1-L-6b): the NPC call site (`NPC.cs:90504`, whose fuse arm
covers only NPC kinds the port does not ship), `PressurePlateHelper`'s
plate 428 (`PressurePlateHelper.cs`, the "stays pressed while a player
stands on it" plate), the Actuation Rod (3620) and the multi-wrench (3625).

## The weighted plate and the actuation rod (S1-L-6b3, 2026-11-14)

The rest of the wiring row landed with S1-L-6b3:

- **The NPCs trip the plates too.** The world sim runs the same
  `Collision.SwitchTiles` scan over the updated NPCs (the `objType` 2 call,
  `NPC.cs:90504`), reading the new `Npc.old_x`/`old_y` — the C#'s
  `Entity.oldPosition` (`NPC.cs:92605`, right before the position
  integration). The port sets the pair at the head of the NPC update (the
  C#'s set it right before the integration, after the AI shaped the
  velocity); for the port's walkers the two are the same position.
- **`PressurePlateHelper.UpdatePlayerPosition`** (`PressurePlateHelper.cs:60-100`)
  is `world_sim::wiring::update_pressure_plates`: the weighted pressure
  plate (428) holds while the player's deflated box reaches the plate's
  lower ten pixels and releases when the player leaves it — each transition
  fires the plate's switch (`PokeLocation`, `:157-165`, with the teleport
  block for one iteration). The C#'s helper keeps the last position per
  player; the port takes it as a parameter (the sim captures the player's
  `prev_x`/`prev_y` before the tick's movement — the position the C#'s
  `PlayerLastPosition` holds). The C#'s per-plate 255-slot bool array is a
  set of the held plates in the port (one player).
- **The Actuation Rod (3620)** is `Wiring.Actuate` (`Wiring.cs:390-405`),
  now `Wiring::actuate`: the tile must carry the actuator bit and the flip
  runs the de-activate/re-activate cascade. The player's per-tick lock
  (`Player.ActuationRodLock`/`ActuationRodLockSetting`, `Player.cs:2616-2618`,
  cleared by `ResetEffects` at `:18804`) keeps one tile from flipping twice
  (`:46894-46897`).

Deliberate deviations:

1. The C#'s `NPC.cs:90504` fuse arm (`ai[0] = 1; ai[1] = 400; ai[2] = 0` for
   the explosive NPC kinds) has no ported member — the kinds in the list are
   not in the port's roster — so only the plate trip lands.
2. The multi-wrench (3625) stays out: it needs the `WiresUI` tool modes
   (`Player.cs:46903-46918`) and `Wiring.MassWireOperation`
   (`Wiring.cs:419-453`).
3. `Collision.GetTilesIn`'s clamp is now the C#'s `Utils.Clamp`
   (`Utils.cs:223-234` — the max is tested first), so a world shorter than

The Flying Dutchman's cannons (`NPCID.FlyingDutchmanCannon`, 492) ride the
aiStyle-75 mount machine ✓, but the port never gave them the C#'s
`type == 492` block (`NPC.cs:35753-35823`): the 240-tick reload, the
line-of-sight gate, the shell's shot and the eight-ray aim. The port's
`DUTCHMAN_SHELL` row (240, the aiStyle-2 projectile) had no arm either, so
the shell had neither a shooter nor a behaviour.

The arm now carries both halves:

* **the cannon** (`:35753-35823`): the `ai[3]` reload counts to 240, the
  line-of-sight gate (the `Collision.CanHit` box test) opens the shot, and
  the shell flies at the player (the normalized direction × 14, minus 5 on
  the Y). Between the shots the cannon aims with the eight-ray scan — the
  closest of the eight rays around the cannon sets its `ai[2]` (the octant
  the sprite reads back), and the aim clears when the sight line is lost.
  The cannon owns its `ai[3]` (the C#'s block counts its own reload), so

* **the shell** (the aiStyle-2 block, `Projectile.cs:23366-23410`): the
  shell spawns at alpha 255 (`SetDefaults` `:3226`) and turns invisible on
  tick 3 (the `ai[0] > 2f` gate); the `ai[0] == 3f` dust/gore burst is

  and the 16-tick `+0.18f`/`×0.991f` gravity delay now run inside
  `ai_style2`'s per-kind ladder (the earlier landing's unconditional
  alpha-0 pre-step is gone).

Deviations:

* **The dust and the gore are SKIPPED** (the shell's burst) — no dust/gore
  layer.
* **The cannon inherits the Dutchman's velocity and `timeLeft`** in the C#;
  the port's carrier link carries the position and the timers only, so the
  cannon keeps its own movement.

The aiStyle-2 arm (`ai_style2`, `Projectile.cs:23205-23689`) landed its

and pins the exact per-arm `ai[0]` increment semantics:

  blanket skip was wrong and is fixed.

* **The 304 spawn latch** (`:23240-23244`): `localAI[0]++` and alpha 0 on
  the first tick; the decay arm's two `if`s are kept separate (the aim

## The debug god mode (S1-E-34, 2026-11-16)

No new damage-path code. `Player.creative_god_mode` — the journey Godmode power —
already gates every way a player can take damage: `Hurt` returns before the
iframes, the defense reduction and the knockback
(`Player.cs:38203-38206`), `KillMe` refuses the death (`:38809-38812`),
`Update_NPCCollision` returns before the whole contact pass (`:31321-31324`) and
`Main.UpdateWorld_Players` refills life/mana/breath (`Main.cs:17869-17873`).

What the task actually adds is the **debug surface**: a twelfth row on the F3
panel's World tab (`God Mode: ON/OFF`) that flips a new
`Player::debug_god_mode`.

Deliberate deviation (one-line-cited at the site): the tick ORs
`debug_god_mode` into `creative_god_mode` instead of writing it directly,
because `Player.ResetEffects` re-derives `creative_god_mode` from the journey
power **every tick** (`:18789` clears it, `:25493-25497` re-reads it), so a
direct toggle would last exactly one tick. Keeping a separate field also keeps
the two independent: the journey power's own toggle is untouched, and the debug
flag cannot silently turn the power on. CheatSheet's `GodMode.cs:56-67` and
HEROsMod's `GeneralMessages.cs:182-190` are mod sources that are not part of
`decompiled/`, so this row implements the *behaviour* the ROADMAP row describes
("damage is swallowed while on") on top of the existing vanilla gate rather
than porting either mod.

## The Eye Fire / Flames Trap and the Baby Bird (S1-D-4b-5c, 2026-11-16)

Two leftover styles ride the Eye and Moon Lord chains: **23** and **158**.

* **Style 23 is two types.** `aiStyle = 23` covers the Eye Fire (**101**,
  `ProjectileID.EyeFire`) and the Flames Trap (**188**,
  `ProjectileID.FlameTrap`). They share the whole arm; only the trap arms the
  launch-counter floor (`if (ai[0] < 8) ai[0] = 8;`, `Projectile.cs:25863-25868`)
  and the 60-tick life cap (`:25871-25874`). Both count launches in
  `localAI[0]` (`:25869`, `:25892`), which `Damage_CanDealDamage` (`:12448`)
  reads to refuse the shot while the counter is still below 7 — so the counter
  is load-bearing state, not decoration.
* **Style 158 is one type**, the Baby Bird pet (**759**): `projFrames[759] = 5`
  (`Main.cs:8506`). The arm keeps the pet alive while the `babyBird` buff flag
  is set (`timeLeft = 2`, `:48760-48769`), walks its five frames at six ticks
  per frame wrapping at `projFrames - 1` (`:48770-48777`), and snaps onto the
  owner's home spot on the **last** frame when inside the
  `8 + |player.velocity|` band (`:48919-48927`) — the walk never reaches the
  last frame itself, which is why the perch frame is only visible while
  sitting. The target scan is `Minion_FindTargetInRange` (`:48990-49027`) with
  the four reach helpers `CanHitWithOwnBody` / `CanHitWithOwnMeleeWeapon`
  (`:12400-12444`).

Deliberate deviations and skips (all one-line-cited in the code):

* **Dust, gore and sound are skipped** in both arms — the pool has no
  `Main.dust` layer and no sound sink, matching the `ai_volcano` /
  `ai_sharp_tears` precedent above. The `Dust.NewDust` calls in the C# blocks
  are recorded at the site, not ported.
* **The two separation loops and the group index are computed pool-side.**
  `AI_158` walks `Main.projectile` twice to find its sibling birds and its own
  index among them (`:51895-51911`); a slot arm cannot see its siblings, so
  `ProjectilePool::baby_bird_group` pre-computes the group index and both
  separation vectors and hands them to `ai_baby_bird`. The arithmetic is the
  C#'s verbatim; only the *where* moved.
* **`gravDir = 1` and `mounted_center == center` are folded.** The port has no
  gravity flip and no mount pivot offset, so `AI_158`'s
  `RotatedRelativePoint(MountedCenter)` chain reduces to
  `Center + gfxOffY - (0, 21) + (0, headgear - 2)`. `Player::`
  `apply_head_offset_from_mount` and `rotated_relative_point` are ported
  faithfully anyway (the mount ids that do move the head are live), so the fold
  is one call site, not a missing function.
* **`correctSlopeCollision` is `projPet`, so `pet_movement` skips the slope
  pass.** `Projectile.cs:707` sets `correctSlopeCollision = projPet`;
  `AI_158`'s pet movement therefore runs `Collision.TileCollision` with
  `fallThrough = fall2 = true` and no `correctSlopeCollision` pass. The port
  calls `collision::tile_collision(..., fall_through = true, fall2 = true)` and
  omits the slope correction — faithful to the C# for this flag combination.
* **`NPC.boss` has no port field.** The arm's boss bypass
  (`if (npc.boss) ...`) reads `crate::revenge::BOSS_KINDS` instead; the set is
  derived from the C# `npc.boss` assignments, so the predicate is the same.

(`ai_baby_bird` + `ai_158_home_location` + the pool-side `baby_bird_group`,

module was created (`projectile_styles_e.rs` would have duplicated the arms);
the slice is a documentation + re-verification pass, run in **code-only mode**
(no cargo/rustc/test runs — verification is a line-by-line C# re-read plus the
existing tests-as-code: `s1_d_4b_1_the_volcano_flashes_and_dies_in_five_frames`,
`s1_d_4b_5_the_sharp_tears_spike_fades_and_dies`, the `s1_d_4b_5c_*` set).
Re-verified faithful (gates before the `ai[0]++` advance, the `Opacity`
property view `:540-549` over `alpha`, the two-remap alpha flash, the home-spot
ring/stack arithmetic, the 6-tick walk wrapping at `projFrames - 1`). Two
observations recorded, neither a behaviour change on the port's kind set:
* **The kind rows cover the ported types only.** Style 157 has three C# types —
  756 (`:7793-7806`), 961 (`:9078-9088`), 1041 (`:9834-9847`) — and the port
  carries only the 961, so `ai_sharp_tears` ports the 961's parameter row
  (documented at the arm). If 756/1041 are ever added, the arm needs their rows
  (the 1041's frame machine `:51406-51409`/`:51420-51424` and its
  `flag = false` dust gate) and the 756's light tail (`:51490-51493`). Style
  189 likewise: the port carries the 1125 (`:10528-10542`) but not the 978
  Volcano (`:9253-9269`); `ai_volcano`'s else-branch keeps the 978's scale ramp
  for completeness.
* **Stale citation ranges in the 157 comments.** The arm and its dispatch
  comment cite `:51358-51477`, but the machine runs to `:51494` and the
  fade-in/fade-out/kill blocks sit at `:51463-51489` (the comments point at
  dust-block lines). The ported logic itself matches the true lines; the
  comments were left untouched to keep this slice a zero-code change.
RNG argument (by construction): the 157 arm draws exactly one `Main.rand`
value — `Next(maxValue)` for the first-tick frame roll (`:51431`), ported as
`rng.next_range(0, 5)` on the pool's threaded stream; every other draw in the
C# arm belongs to the skipped dust blocks. The 158 machine draws **no**
`Main.rand` at all (target scan, separation and home chain are deterministic).
The 189 arm's draws all ride the skipped dust/gore blocks (`:42302-42367`), so
the ported alpha/scale/frame path draws none — the `ai_eye_fire` precedent.

## The Retinazer's machine (S1-D-3i, 2026-11-14)

**Census correction (S1-D-3q, 2026-11-18):** the arm ported below is NOT
the Retinazer's — `NPC.cs:32761-33043` is the shared MourningWood (325) /
Everscream (344) aiStyle-57 floater; the Retinazer (125) is aiStyle 30
(`:10526`, arm `:26405+`). The style ids were fixed by S1-D-2; the machine
re-port is a D-3 follow-up. See "The aiStyle-57 shared-kind census
(S1-D-3q)" below.

`AI_057` (`NPC.cs:32761-33043`) is the Retinazer's family machine — the
Twins' left boss ✓ (the Spazmatism is an aiStyle-3 ground fighter ✓).
The port ran one EoC-shaped v1 arm for both Twins: a hover, a dash and a
decay.

The Retinazer's arm now carries the C#'s machine:

* **the idle** (`ai[0] == 0`, `:32794-32815`): the `ai[1]` counter (the
  faster it loses hp, the faster it counts) and, at 300, the next state
  (the stomp 1-2, or the beam 3-4 below a quarter hp);
* **the stomp** (1, `:32836-32866`): the flaming wood every 15 ticks;
* **the spin** (2, `:32868-32929`): the Greek fires every eighth tick
  between the 60th and the 240th;
* **the beam** (3, `:32930-32956`): the flaming wood every 30 ticks;
* **the charge** (4, `:32957-32990`): the Greek fires every tenth tick;
* **the movement** (`:32991-33040`): the horizontal drift toward the
  player (the speed cap 2, 3 and 4 per the hp band, 8 in the day-time)
  with the damp inside 50 px, and the vertical hover — the player-overlap
  test, the solid-tile probe under the boss and the rise/fall ramps.

The shots' rows come with it: the flaming wood (325) and the Greek fires
(326/327/328) get their `SetDefaults` slices (`Projectile.cs:3249-3277`).
The Spazmatism (326) leaves the shared v1 arm for the aiStyle-3 walker
(the cap-2 group, `:57554`).

Deviations:

* **The light and the dust are SKIPPED** — no dust/light layer.
* **The day-time `EncourageDespawn(10)`** rides the world's own day arm (the
  port's NPCs carry no despawn timer).

## The Skeletron Prime's machine (S1-D-3j, 2026-11-14)

`AI_032` (`NPC.cs:27626-27942`) is the Skeletron Prime's family machine
— the hover (0), the charge (1), the day-time rage (2) and the despawn
(3). The port's `update_prime` had the shape but not the numbers: the
hover's bands were a sign-based steer instead of the C#'s velocity
bands, the charge never doubled the damage and the defense, and the rage
was not invulnerable.

The arm now carries the C#'s machine:

* **the hover** (`:27679-27764`): the 600-tick cycle into the charge, the
  rotation (the drift / 15) and the acceleration bands — the vertical one
  above the player (200 px) and below it (500 px) with the 0.1 acceleration
  and the 2 cap, the horizontal one 100 px either side with the same
  acceleration and the 8 cap (the expert's 0.03/4/0.07/9.5);
* **the charge** (`:27765-27859`): the damage and the defense double, the
  400-tick cycle back to the hover, the roll (`direction * 0.3`) and the
  rush (2 px, the expert's 6 with its distance ramp);
* **the rage** (`:27860-27892`): the damage and the defense 9999 and the
  8-32 chase;
* **the despawn** (`:27893-27941`): the sink and the damp.

The four limbs' spawn stays in the sim's pass (`wants_limbs` ✓ — the C#'s
`ai[0] == 0` init, `:27632-27660`).

Deviations:

* **The Mech Queen's rows** (`NPC.IsMechQueenUp` — the half-drift rotation,
  the 450 px offset, the limb scaling) are skipped: the port has no Mech
  Queen.
* **The day-time `EncourageDespawn(10)`** rides the world's own day arm (the
  port's NPCs carry no despawn timer).

## The Eye of Cthulhu's machine (S1-D-3k, 2026-11-14)

`AI_004` (`NPC.cs:19960-20801`) is the Eye's whole family machine — the
hover phase (0), the two spin phases (1, 2) and the final dash phase (3) —
plus the servant bursts. The port's `update_eye_of_cthulhu` already carried
the phase-1 hover, the dash chain and the final phase's shape; three deltas
remained, and the servant (the Eye's minion, type 5) ran on the *shared*
hover archetype instead of the C#'s own `AI_005` branch.

**The spin hand-off (the inverted reset).** The C#'s spin block
(`:20287-20301`) ramps `ai[2]` (the spin speed) to 0.5 in phase 1 and decays
it in phase 2; the phase hand-off (`:20356-20361`) resets `ai[2]` **only**
when the phase reaches 3 (`if (this.ai[0] == 3f) this.ai[2] = 0f;`). The
port had the test inverted (`if self.ai[0] != 3.0`), so the phase-1 → 2
hand-off zeroed the spin speed: the Eye's third phase stood still instead
of decaying from 0.5, and the phase-2 → 3 hand-off kept a stale speed. The
fix restores the C#'s hand-off: the phase-2 spin now decays from 0.5 to 0
over its 100 ticks, and the final phase starts with the spin stopped.

**The final phase's damage.** The C#'s final phase writes
`this.damage = GetAttackDamage_LerpBetweenFinalValues(23, 18)`
(`:20392-20408`) — the classic difficulty remaps onto the first value, so
the contact damage rises from the `SetDefaults` 15 to **23** in the final
phase. The port kept the 15 for the whole fight; the arm now carries the
override (`damage_override = Some(23)`). The defense drop (`this.defense = 0`,
the same block) was already there.

**The servant's spawn point.** `NPC.NewNPC` takes the spawn point as the
NPC's **bottom centre** (`NPC.cs:80770` — `nPC.Bottom = new Vector2(X, Y)`,
whose setter writes `position = (X - width/2, Y - height)`, `Entity.cs:122-132`)
and the call site truncates it to whole pixels (`NPC.cs:20180`:
`(int)vector2.X, (int)vector2.Y`). The port placed the servant at
`(X - 10, Y - 10)` — 10 px too low and un-truncated. The spawn helper now
writes the bottom-centre convention and the truncation.

**The servant's own machine.** The Servant of Cthulhu (type 5) runs
`AI_005_EaterOfSouls` — the C#'s type-5 branch (`:50379-50383`: the speed 5,
the accel 0.03) plus the shared fly core (`:50418-50579`) and the type-5
rotation (`:50652-50655`). The port ran it through the shared hover
archetype, which misses two things the C# does:

* the aim is quantised to the **8-px grid** — the target's centre and the
  servant's own centre both floor to 8 px (`:50421-50424`) and the aim is
  the difference of the snapped values;
* the approach's **double-add on a sign reversal** is gated by `flag5`
  (`:50447`), which is *true* for type 5.

The servant's own arm (`update_servant_of_cthulhu`) now carries the C#'s
branch: the snapped aim, the 5-speed / 0.03-accel approach with the
double-add, the dead-target flee vector (`num4 = direction * num/2`,
`num5 = -num/2`, `:50480-50484`) and the velocity tilt
(`rotation = atan2(velocity.Y, velocity.X) - 1.57`). Its `noGravity` +
`noTileCollide` (`SetDefaults` case 5) make the step a raw integration —
no tile collision (the shared archetype bounced the servant off tiles).

The residuals of the S1-D-1 hover section (the 8-px floor and the `flag5`
gate) therefore remain only for the kinds that still ride the archetype —
the Eater of Souls (6), the Hornet (42) and the Meteor Head (23) — where
`flag5` is false for the first two: the shared `hover_step` still
over-adds for them. That is the S1-D-3l follow-up.

Deviations:

* **The dust and the gore** (the 1-in-5 dust at `:20062-20067`, the
  spin-phase gore at `:20365-20375`) are skipped — the port has no dust or
  gore layer.
* **The expert / `getGoodWorld` branches** (the rage sub-states `ai[1] =
  3/4/5`, the expert servant bursts, the phase-3 dash speed bonuses) are
  constants-off: the port has no difficulty flag, so the classic path runs
  verbatim and the skipped arms carry their C# cites.
* **The day-time `EncourageDespawn(10)`** (`:20071-20073`) rides the sim's
  day cull (the Eye rises out of the player's view and is removed).

## The NPC hit and death sounds (S1-E-21a, 2026-11-14)

The first wave of the sound bank (S1-E-21) landed with S1-E-21a: the NPCs
now play their **own** hit and death cues.

`NpcKind::hit_sound` / `NpcKind::death_sound` (`crates/tr-app/src/npc.rs`)
carry the C#'s per-kind table — `NPC.HitSound` / `NPC.DeathSound`
(`NPC.cs:6475-6477`, the `SetDefaults` assignments). The C#'s `null` guard
(`NPC.cs:8537`) is kept: the kinds with no row in `SetDefaults` (the Brain
Scrambler 381 and the Ray Gunner 382) play nothing. The cue names are the
legacy asset names — the sound id 3 family is `NPC_Hit_N` and the sound id 4
family is `NPC_Killed_N` (`LegacySoundPlayer.cs:646`/`:676`).

The two call sites are the C#'s: the melee strike plays the kind's hit cue
at the NPC's position (`NPC.StrikeNPC`, `:81544-81553`) and the death plays
the kind's death cue at its centre (`NPC.checkDead`, `:91852`).

Deliberate deviations:

1. The C#'s trackable styles pick a random variation
   (`LegacySoundStyle.Style`, `LegacySoundStyle.cs:33-38`); the port plays
   the first file of the family (the `_0` asset) — the same asset family, a
   fixed member. The C#'s own pick comes from a clock-seeded static random,
   so it is not reproducible there either.
2. ~~The legacy per-sound pitch and the per-family instance reuse (the C#'s
   `SoundNpcHit[n]` pool) stay unported~~ — **closed by wave C below**
   (2026-11-18): the case-3/4 maths, the pitch draws and the slot pools are
   ported.
3. The C#'s special hit cues for the newest NPCs (the Turkey/Undead/Vampire
   hurts, `NPC.cs:81535-81545`) have no ported kinds.

## The NPC hit/death sound plays (S1-E-21 wave C, 2026-11-18)

Wave C ports the **playback** half of the NPC hit/death sounds — the S1-E-21a
table stayed, but the plays were flat `play_at` calls with no case maths, no
pitch and no volume arms. Now:

- `sound.rs::npc_hit_case3` ports `LegacySoundPlayer.cs:646-672` (case 3):
  styles 20..54 ×0.5 (`:647-650`), the 57 playing guard returns before any
  draw (`:651-654`), 57 ×0.6 (`:655-658`), 55/56 ×0.5 (`:659-662`), one
  `Main.rand.Next(-10, 11) * 0.01` pitch draw (`:670`).
- `sound.rs::npc_killed_case4` ports case 4 (`:673-695`): styles 23..57 ×0.5
  (`:674-677`), 61/62 ×0.6 (`:678-685`), the 10 playing guard (`:686-689`),
  one `Next(-10, 11) * 0.01` pitch draw (`:693`).
- `audio.rs::play_npc_hit_sound` / `play_npc_death_sound` run the façade
  (`SoundEngine.cs:93-99`): the `GetRandomPitch` NextFloat on the audio-only
  `sound_style_random` (variance 0 for every NPC style — the draw still
  happens), the attenuation gate (`LegacySoundPlayer.cs:369-436`) BEFORE any
  gameplay draw, then the case maths. The final
  `Clamp(pitch + pitchOffset, -1, 1)` is `:1410`. The style row comes from
  the generated `soundid.rs` table through `npc_sound_style` (the asset name
  → `NPCHitN`/`NPCDeathN`, the trackable `_0` pins → their style, so the
  Deerclops' hit rides its 0.3 style volume).
- The instance pools: `npc_hit_slots[59]` (`SoundNpcHit` is
  `new Asset<SoundEffect>[59]`, `LegacySoundPlayer.cs:74`) stops + re-creates
  the slot's sink (`:663-667`); `npc_killed_slots` (a map over
  `SoundID.NPCDeathCount = 69`, `SoundID.cs:1383`) overwrites WITHOUT a Stop
  (`:690` — the old sink detaches and plays out), exactly the two cases'
  different semantics. Headless nothing plays, so the guards never trip —
  the engine's fresh-instance-table behaviour.

The call sites and their named streams (`Main.SwapRandom`,
`Main.cs:17749-17809`):

| Site | C# | Port | Stream |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Melee strike | `NPC.StrikeNPC` `NPC.cs:81544-81553` via `Player.ItemCheck_MeleeHitNPCs` | `world_sim/editing.rs` (the landed strike) | `UpdatePlayers` (`Main.cs:17754`) |
| Projectile strike | `Projectile.Damage` → `StrikeNPC` (`Projectile.cs:13649`) | `projectile.rs::damage_pve`/`damage_pve_boxed` queue → `world_sim/projectiles.rs` drain | `UpdateProjectiles` (`Main.cs:17775`) |
| Death | `NPC.checkDead` `NPC.cs:78186-78194` (**`base.position`** — the old port played at the centre citing `:91852`, which is actually the eel-whip DoT's `HitSound` site) | `world_sim/npcs.rs` death retain | `UpdateNPCs` (`Main.cs:17767`) — see deviation 2 |
| Net client strike | `MessageBuffer.cs:1797` runs the full `StrikeNPC_Inner` on the client | `app/netglue.rs` `S2c::NpcStrike` | the bare-`Main.rand` stand-in (`Main.Update` `Main.cs:16895` → `Netplay.UpdateInMainThread` runs outside every swap) |

The host's own strike path plays nothing: the C#'s `netMode == 2` guard
(`LegacySoundPlayer.cs:386`) — the port's listener carries `server: true` on
the Host role (S1-E-24).

Deliberate deviations (wave C):

1. **Death-stream placement.** The C# runs `checkDead` inside `StrikeNPC`,
   so the death pitch draw rides the *striking* stage's stream
   (`UpdatePlayers`/`UpdateProjectiles`). The port batches deaths into the
   NPC pass's retain, so the draw rides `UpdateNPCs` instead. One draw per
   death, same window; the stream assignment differs (the port's death
   batching predates this wave — M4-NPC).
2. **Projectile draw position.** The C# draws the hit pitch mid-damage-walk
   (between the strike and the loot/immunity rolls); the port's pool cannot
   reach the audio, so the strikes queue `(cue, x, y)` intents
   (`drain_npc_hit_sounds`, the `take_cart_sounds` precedent) and the pass
   tail plays them — the draws land after the walk's other rolls instead of
   interleaved. Same count, same window, same stream; the interleave differs.
3. The trackable `_0` variation pin (deviation 1 of S1-E-21a above) and the
   unported pet-hurt switch arm (`NPC.cs:81490-81549`, the type-1
   `ai[1]` cases — the port ships no pet kinds) stay.
4. The 229 shimmer-variant death override (`NPC.cs:78187-78190`,
   `NPCDeath6`) has no ported kind — the invasion Pirate 229 is unported.

Tests: `s1_e_21c_npc_hit_case3_tweaks_the_volume_and_guards_57`,
`s1_e_21c_npc_killed_case4_tweaks_the_volume_and_guards_10` (sound.rs — the
volume arms + the guard-before-draw contract),
`s1_e_21c_the_npc_hit_draws_ride_the_passed_stream_only_when_audible`,
`s1_e_21c_the_npc_death_draws_ride_the_passed_stream_only_when_audible`,

one-draw-after-the-gate proof, the case-42 draw-free contract, the style
resolution), `s1_e_21c_every_kind_hit_and_death_cue_resolves` (npc.rs — all
199 kinds' cues resolve to a bank asset + a style row; closed the

`s1_e_21c_the_death_play_draws_one_pitch_on_the_npc_stream`

## The tile-break sound table (S1-E-21c, 2026-11-16)

`WorldGen.KillTile_PlaySounds` (`WorldGen.cs:66427-66575`, called from
`KillTile` `:63558`) is the biggest single missing cue table: ~200 tile types
resolve to one of 13 asset families. It is a pure per-type switch — no state,
no draw except the 147/224 roll — so it ports as a table.

`tr-core/src/edit.rs::kill_tile_sound(kind, frame_x, fail)` returns
`KillSounds { primary, extra, shatter }`; the app maps each `(sound id, style)`
through `world_sim/editing.rs::kill_cue` to a pinned asset and the case's
volume scale (`LegacySoundPlayer.PlaySound`, `:360-1100`). `break_tile` plays
the hit cell's cues **once**, before the loot, and the pot events now play
their real `CheckPot` cues (4/6/13 → `NPC_Killed_1`/`Grass`/`Shatter`) rather
than the `Dig_1` stand-in.

Deliberate deviations:

1. **Variation families are pinned** (research D3): `Dig_0..2`, `Tink_0..2`
   and `Item48`/`Item49` are a per-play `Main.rand`/`genRand` pick in the C#;
   the port plays one fixed member (`Dig_1`, `Tink_1`, `Item_48`). Audio-only:
   no state depends on the pick.
2. **The per-play pitch jitter is not applied at the call site**: the
   `LegacySoundPlayer` cases roll `Main.rand.Next(-10,11)*0.01` (and the
   item/dig windows) per play. `sound.rs` already carries the roll machinery
   (`legacy_family_pitch`, S1-E-22) with `Playback.pitch`; the headless
   `Audio::play_at` path plays without a resampler, so the roll is not wired
   here. Recorded as an audio-output gap, not a behaviour one.
3. **The per-family instance pools are not modelled**: the C# stops and
   recreates `SoundInstanceDig[n]`/`SoundTink[n]`/`SoundItem[n]` per play. The
   port's `play_at` opens a fresh `rodio` stream per call; the audible result is
   the same single-shot cue (the tracked-sound layer, S1-E-23, is for the
   looping/ambient families).
4. **The per-drop sound is gone**: the port used to play `Dig_1` once per
   dropped item in `break_tile`. The C# plays the break cue once, at the hit
   cell, from `KillTile_PlaySounds` — `Item.NewItem` plays nothing. The
   per-drop cue was an invention and is removed.
5. **The failure-tick callers stay unported**: `Player.cs:39880` and
   `Projectile.cs:70219` play the table with `fail: true` while a pickaxe
   chips an unbreakable tile / a drill bit bites. The port has no per-tick chip
   path (it refuses the break outright), so only `fail: false` is wired; the
   table itself carries the `fail` arms (the glass pop and the shatter tail).

## The hover family's residuals (S1-D-3l, 2026-11-14)

`AI_005_EaterOfSouls` (`NPC.cs:50244-50760`) is the shared fly core of the
hover family. The port's `npc_ai::hover_step` had the shape — the target
vector scaled to the kind's `num`, the `num2` approach, the type-42 scale
factor and its surface-gated damping — but five things of the source were
missing, and the frame clock ran twice.

**The 8-px aim floor** (`:50421-50424`). The C# floors the target's centre
and the NPC's own centre to the 8-px grid and takes the aim as the
difference of the snapped values:
`num4 = (int)(num4 / 8f) * 8; vector.X = (int)(vector.X / 8f) * 8;`. The
port aimed at the exact centre. The floor is now in `hover_step` (and in
the Servant of Cthulhu's own arm, S1-D-3k).

**The `flag5` gate** (`:50447`). The approach's extra add on a sign
reversal is gated:
`flag5 = type ∉ {6, 42, 94, 139, 173, 619} ∧ type ∉ [231, 235]`. The port
applied it to every hover kind, so the Eater of Souls (6) and the Hornet
(42) over-added on every reversal. `HoverParams` now carries `double_add`
and the table sets it per kind.

**The dead-target flee vector** (`:50299`/`:50480-50484`). A dead player
replaces the aim with `num4 = direction * num/2; num5 = -num/2` — the NPC
flies off along its facing. `HoverTarget` now carries the dead flag.

**The per-kind rotation arms** (`:50580-50655`). The C# ends the core with
one of four shapes, and the port had none of them:

| kind | arm | the port |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6/94/173/619 | `rotation = atan2(num5, num4) - 1.57` (the aim tilt) | — |
| 23 | the sprite-aim arm: the sprite direction follows the aim's x sign, `rotation = atan2(num5, num4)` (+π to the left) | — |
| 42/176/205/231-235 | the sprite direction follows the velocity's x sign, `rotation = velocity.X * 0.1` | — |
| the rest | `rotation = atan2(velocity.Y, velocity.X) - 1.57` | — |

`HoverParams::rotation` now selects the arm (`HoverRotation`).

**The tile collision** (`:50656-50688`). The C#'s bounce arm covers the
kinds that collide with the tiles: `velocity.X = oldVelocity.X * -num14`
(`num14` = 0.7, 0.4 for the types 6/173) plus the small-velocity clamps
(`|v| < 2` → ±2 on the x, `|v| < 1.5` → ±2 on the y). The port bounced
every hover kind with a flat ×0.5 — and it bounced the kinds that
`SetDefaults` gives `noTileCollide` (the Eater of Souls and the Meteor
Head), which in the source fly straight through the tiles. `HoverParams` now
carries `no_tile_collide` and `bounce`.

**The frame clock ran twice.** `update_hover` advanced the frame counter
*and* `find_frame` advanced it again (the C#'s `NPC.FindFrame` is the only
owner), so the hovers' flap advanced at half the stride. The frame handling
now lives in `find_frame` alone — and the Hornet gets the C#'s four-phase
flap (`:74907-74934`: two ticks a phase over the rows 0/1/2/1) instead of
the port's 8-tick stride over three rows.

Deviations:

* **The tile collision** is the port's rectangle probe
  (`crate::player::collides_rect`) instead of the C#'s tile sweep with
  `oldVelocity`; the bounce's factor and the clamps are the source's.
* **The dust and the wet arms** (`:50695-50730`) are skipped — the port has
  no dust layer and no wet flag on the hovers.
* **The per-difficulty / secret-seed overrides** (`:50308-50316` the remix
  values for type 6, `:50345-50348` type 231's 3/0.017) are constants-off.
* **The `facing` write** at the end of the step is the port's convention
  (the C#'s `base.direction` is not written by `AI_005`); the render uses
  `spriteDirection`, which the rotation arms now own.
## The player voice cues (S1-E-21b, 2026-11-14)

The second wave of the sound bank: the player's own hurt and death cues.

`Player.Hurt`'s tail plays the hurt cue (`Player.cs:38525` →
`PlayHurtSound`, `:38569-38712`) and `Player.KillMe` plays the death cue
(`:38868` → `PlayDeathSound`, `:38715-38744`). The port queues the cue on
the Player (the `take_hurt_sound`/`take_death_sound` handoff — the Player
has no audio device) and the fixed step drains it.

Two behaviour changes ride the wave:

1. The hurt sound now rides the **damage path** instead of the frame's
   hp-drop heuristic (`app/frame.rs`'s `last_hp` compare) — the C#'s
   `PlayHurtSound` is called from `Hurt`, so the damage-over-time ticks
   (the poison, the burning) no longer play a hurt sound.
2. The death sound is new: the legacy "Player Killed" id 5
   (`Player.cs:38737`, the default arm of `PlayDeathSound`).

Deliberate deviations:

1. The C#'s voice system (`Player.voiceOverride`/`voiceVariant`/`Male`,
   `Player.cs:1346`/`38581-38710`) is not ported — the default voice
   variant 1 (`Player.cs:56045`, the legacy "Player Hit" id 1) stands in.
2. The C#'s hurt cue picks a random variation (`Main.rand.Next(3)`,
   `LegacySoundPlayer.cs:505`); the port plays "Player_Hit_0".
3. The C#'s death cue switches to the remastered hurt cues in the Don't
   Starve and 10th-anniversary worlds (`Player.cs:38737-38740`); the port
   plays the legacy cue everywhere.
4. The C#'s local-player hurt sound plays non-positionally
   (`Player.cs:38572`); the port's drain plays it without a position ✓.

## The explicit carrier links (S1-D-6b, 2026-11-14)

The C#'s boss-part links are index links into `Main.npc` — `NPC.ai[3]`
points at the carrier (`NPC.cs:6161`), `AI_077`'s `localAI[0..2]` point at
the Moon Lord's three parts (`NPC.cs:41229-41232`), and `AI_082`'s leech
blob holds its head's index + 1 (`NPC.cs:36630-36640`). The port's
`App::npcs` compacts every frame (the death retain), so a Vec index does
not survive the frame; the port used to re-derive the links by KIND search
every tick ("the first alive Moon Lord core").

**The stable identity.** `Npc.uid` (`NPC.whoAmI`, `NPC.cs:6145`) is the
port's stand-in: the sim hands every NPC its id once (`App::next_npc_uid`)
and never reuses it. The links now ride the ids:

* the Moon Lord's hands and head carry the core's id in `carrier_uid` (the
  C#'s `ai[3]`) and the core keeps the parts' ids in `moon_parts` (the
  C#'s `localAI[0..2]`) — set at the spawn, exactly like the vanilla;
* the leech blob's anchor is the head's id;
* the core's part check (`NPC.cs:41250-41269`) resolves the ids each tick
  (`moon_parts_lost`), because the core's own AI has no NPC list.

A part whose carrier died falls with it (`Main.npc[ai[3]]` inactive), and a
second Moon Lord never steals the first one's parts — with the kind search
it did.

**Per-carrier resolution (re-verified 2026-11-18).** Each carrier family now
has its own resolution test: `the_moon_lord_parts_keep_their_own_core` (the
hands/head ↔ core, `NPC.cs:41229-41232`/`:41579-41583`),
`the_leech_blob_keeps_its_own_head` (the clot ↔ head, `AI_082`'s anchor
`NPC.cs:36630-36640` — two families on the field, the clot mirrors ITS
head's centre and falls with it while the other head lives) and
`the_true_eye_keeps_its_own_core` (the True Eye ↔ core, `AI_081`'s anchor
`NPC.cs:42466-42470`, the link handed out by `MoonLord_SpawnTrueEyeOfCthulhu`
`:41154` — the eye survives the OTHER core's death and falls with its own).

**Deliberate deviation — the unlinked-part fallback.** The C# resolves
`Main.npc[(int)ai[3]]` unconditionally: a part whose `ai[3]` was never set
points at slot 0 and dies when slot 0 is inactive or the wrong type
(`NPC.cs:41579-41583`). The port's pre-pass instead falls back to a KIND
search for the first alive core/head of the family when `carrier_uid == 0`
(`world_sim/npcs.rs`'s carrier pre-pass) — a part spawned outside the Moon
Lord's spawn arm (the debug spawn, a save load) still finds its family.
Once the link is handed out it is explicit and never re-searched, so the
two-family isolation above holds. The True Eye's spawn site
(`MoonLord_SpawnTrueEyeOfCthulhu`, `NPC.cs:41134-41155` — the head-loop
phase maths over `CountNPCS(400)`) is not ported; the eyes reach the field
through the debug/net spawns and the pre-pass resolves their links the same
way.

**The Old One's Army's wave-7 anchor.** `DD2Event`'s tier-3 budget reads
the Betsy's own life (`NPC.FindFirstNPC(551)`, `DD2Event.cs:1487-1494`):
`currentKillCount = 100 - life/lifeMax*100` and the budget is 100; with no
Betsy on the field the C#'s `-1` arm takes the budget of 1. The port had
the anchor stubbed (`betsy_hp_ratio` was a hard 0.0, so the wave always
showed 100). The app now resolves the Betsy (`dd2_betsy_hp_ratio`) and the
tier's table reads it.

**The tiered wave budget.** `CheckProgress` (`DD2Event.cs:367-392`) takes
the budget and the kill worth from the ongoing difficulty
(`GetInvasionStatus` → `Difficulty_N_GetRequiredWaveKills`,
`GetMonsterPointsWorth` at `:546-554`), and the wave's roster from the
same tier (`GetEnemiesForWave`). The port's kill report used the tier-1
table for every tier; it now picks the tier's roster, budget and worth.
The per-monster exceptions inside the C#'s worth rows (the Dark Mage /
Ogre / Wither Beast zero-point kills at the wave cap, `DD2Event.cs:1106`/
`:1199`/`:1509`) are still the port's flat per-tier worth — a follow-up.

**Still open (S1-D-6c).** The Moon Lord core's vulnerable phase: the C#'s
`flag2` check (`NPC.cs:41270-41285`) hands the core its vulnerable state
(`ai[0] = 1`, `dontTakeDamage = false`) once all three parts are in their
death state. The port's core stays in its `ai[0] == 0` phase with
`dont_take_damage = true`, so the melee cannot touch it and only the
projectile path (which lacks the C#'s `dontTakeDamage` gate,
`Projectile.cs:12662-12666`) can land a hit. Both halves belong together:
the gate alone would make the Moon Lord unkillable.

## The Moon Lord core's phases (S1-D-6c, 2026-11-14)

`AI_077_MoonLordCore` (`NPC.cs:41157-41575`) runs the core through four
phases, and the port's state machine had lost two of them:

| phase | the C# | the port (before) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| init | `localAI[3] == 0` → 1, `ai[0] = -1` (`:41163-41168`) | `ai[0] == 0` → -1, **every tick** |
| spawn-in | `ai[0] == -1`, 60 ticks, then the hands + the head (`:41193-41235`) | the same, but the phase re-armed |
| waiting | `ai[0] == 0`: the hover + the part bookkeeping (`:41236-41291`) | unreachable — the init re-armed the phase |
| vulnerable | `ai[0] == 1`: the hover, `dontTakeDamage = false` (`:41294-41310`) | unreachable |
| death | `ai[0] == 2` (`:41307-41445`) | the same |

**The init latch.** The C#'s latch is `localAI[3]` (0 → 1) — a one-shot.
The port tested `ai[0] == 0` instead, so every return to the zero state
re-armed the spawn phase: the core asked for its parts again every 60
ticks and a second pair of hands + a second head rode out behind the
first. `moon_spawn_latch` is the port's `localAI[3]`.

**The vulnerable phase.** The C#'s `flag2` check (`:41270-41285`) hands
the core `ai[0] = 1` and `dontTakeDamage = false` once all three parts
are in their death state. The port had no such transition: the core stayed
shielded and only the projectile path (which lacked the C#'s
`dontTakeDamage` gate) could land a hit. `moon_parts_dead` is the sim's
resolution of the C#'s check (the core's own AI has no NPC list — the
same shape as the carrier mirrors).

**The projectile's shield gate.** `Damage_PVE`'s outer walk skips the
shielded NPC (`Projectile.cs:12583`: `!nPC.dontTakeDamage`). The port's
`damage_pve` had no such gate, so the shots went through the Moon Lord's
shield and the Brain's Creeper shield. The box walk (`Damage()`,
`:14087-14119`) has no gate in the C# — the port keeps it that way.

**The C#'s `flag` arm.** `NPC.cs:41251-41269` takes the core down when a
slot points at no living part. In the C# a dead part stays `active`
through its death animation, so the arm only fires for a part that
vanished; the port removes the dead parts at once, so "the part is gone"
is the normal death and the arm would kill the core on the first part's
fall. The port implements the `flag2` arm only — the `flag` arm's
counterpart does not exist in the port's immediate-death model.

## The town-NPC melee swing (S1-D-3n, 2026-11-15)

`NPC.AI_007_TownEntities` carries the town-NPC family (the `aiStyle 7` arm,
`NPC.cs:52965-55561`). Its melee state (`ai[0] == 15`, `NPC.cs:54995-55114`)
reads four per-type numbers: `num78` (the swing damage, scaled by
`NPC.GetAttackDamage_ForTownNPC`), `num79` (the swing knockback) and
`num80`/`num81` (the swing item width and height, taken by
`NPC.GetSwingStats`). The C# rows live at `NPC.cs:55018-55054`:

| NPC | type | damage | knockback | item |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dye Trader | 207 | 11 | 4.25 | 32x32 |
| Tax Collector | 441 | 9 | 3.5 | 28x28 |
| Stylist | 353 | 10 | 5 | 32x32 |
| town pets | - | 10 | 3 | 32x32 |

**The port.** `crates/tr-app/src/npc_ai.rs::TownWeaponParams` carries those
four numbers as the `DYE_TRADER`, `TAX_COLLECTOR`, `STYLIST` and `TOWN_PET`
rows, with the C# line cites; the table test
`s1_d_3n_tests::the_town_weapon_presets_match_the_csharp_table` pins them.

**The deliberate gap.** The swing machine itself is not ported: it needs
`NPC.GetSwingStats` (`NPC.cs:66485`), `NPC.StrikeNPCNoInteraction` and
`GameDifficultyData.TownNPCDamageMultiplier` (`NPC.cs:7062-7065`), and the
port has no swing-stats helper, no NPC-to-NPC strike path and no difficulty
multiplier for the town-NPC damage. Porting the machine is a follow-up under
S1-D-3; the preset table lands first so the numbers have one home. `num77`
and `maxValue4` are not read by the swing code and stay unported.

## The moon-event wave machinery + the roster ladders (S1-F-13, 2026-11-15)

The a-slice landed on `S1-F-13-moon-wave-machinery` (phases: the machinery
`882bf20e`, the ladders `9455e325`). The rate/pacing half was already on
`SpawnContext`'s `moon_event` flag (`get_spawn_rate`'s `:396` arm — the C#
`:771-774` moon override, folded next to the invaders override); the wave
machinery and the two roster ladders are new:

- **State** (`World`): `wave_number` (i32, starts 1), `wave_kills`,
  `total_invasion_points` — runtime-only (the C#'s moon-event state rides
  `Main` statics and is saved only inside the invasion-progress's own save
  section the port's format does not mirror — the persistence deviation).
- **Walk**: `CheckProgressFrostMoon`/`CheckProgressPumpkinMoon`
  (`NPC.cs:78445-78600`/`:78588-78719`) as `World` methods, called on the
  death site beside `report_invasion_kill` (`world_sim/npcs.rs`) — the
  per-kind points tables (snow `:78518-78549`; pumpkin `:78658+`), the 1×
  scalar (single-mode: the C#'s master 2.5 / expert 2 arms collapse),
  `wave_kills >= requirement(&& != 0)` → `wave_kills = 0`, `wave_number++`.
  The waves key on the vanilla `NPC.type` u16 (all 30 wave kinds are
  unported until S1-F-13b/c, so the tests drive them directly);
  `MOON_WAVE_REQUIREMENTS.get()` saturates out-of-range waves to the
  terminal 0 (the C# array would throw; waves only reach 0..=20).
- **Start/stop**: `start_pumpkin_moon`/`start_snow_moon`
  (`Main.cs:10979-11017` — the flags, the mutual clear, the resets,
  waveNumber=1) and `stop_moon_event` (`:10953-10976`) at BOTH boundaries —
  the dusk day→night clear (`:65147-65148`) and the dawn clear (`:65392`),
  riding the port's clock mirrors (`world_sim/clock.rs`, the F-14 pattern).
- **Triggers**: the medallion 1844 / Naughty Present 1958 ride editing.rs's
  event-item arms (the `use_snow_globe` seam; the C#'s mid-swing
  `ItemTimeIsZero && itemAnimation > 0` precondition, gated `!day_time &&
  !DD2Event.Ongoing` and the other event — `Player.cs:43974-43985`/
  `:44041-44052`) — ApplyItemTime + sound 15, one stack spent like the
  port's other event items.
- **Boss cap**: the weighted `npcSlots` count over kinds 315/325/327/328/
  344/345/346 vs `players × defaultMaxSpawns×(2+0.3·players)` (the
  `Spawner` ctor `NPC.cs:262-286`) — all seven kinds unported, so the cap is
  false until F-13b/c; the slots table travels with the kinds.
- **The pumpkin-327 quirk**: in the pumpkin cases 18/17/15/14
  (`NPC.cs:3263`/`:3281`/`:3329`/`:3351`) the leading 327 `if` is a
  SEPARATE statement from the `else if` chain after it — its roll always
  draws, and when both fire the C# spawns BOTH NPCs in one attempt. The
  picker returns the first (`pumpkin_327_chain`, the stream stays 1:1 — the
  second spawn's dispatch lands with the pool work); the unconditional
  roll is kept for stream parity.
- **The ladders**: `spawn_npc_at`'s zone chain gained the frost
  (`NPC.cs:2804-3222`) and pumpkin (`:3224-3548` — the eclipse arm opens
  `:3549`) arms at the C#'s dispatch position (after the skyMob dispatch
  and the invaders arm), keyed `!day_time && (world.snow_moon ||
  world.pumpkin_moon)` with the surface band `y/16 <= world_surface` (the
  `remixWorld` alternative's reduction). Every `Main.rand.Next(n)` is
  re-expressed on the spawner's `FastRandom` with the vanilla thresholds;
  the per-kind `CountNPCS` caps gate the C#'s `&&` (the roll is always
  drawn). The arms' picks are the vanilla `NPC.type` u16 — the C#'s only
  no-spawn outcomes (the wave-14 chain's no-`else` miss, the gated boss
  trio) included — and every picked wave kind is unported until F-13b/c, so
  the dispatch consumes the pick and returns no NPC (the Wyvern-arm
  consume-and-return-None shape). `total_invasion_points` is write-only in
  the port (its C# readers are the out-of-scope broadcast/MP).
- **RNG-order (S1-A-10)**: the ladders draw on the one spawner stream in
  the C# arm order (style `Next(7)` → the head `Next(30)` → the chain's
  `Next(n)`s); the walks, start/stop, the dawn stop and the triggers draw
  nothing.

## The Dark Mage's machine (S1-D-3o, 2026-11-16)

`AI_109_DarkMage` (`NPC.cs:65791-66186`) carries the Old One's Army's
casters (types 564/565). The whole arm is ported in
`crates/tr-app/src/npc.rs::update_dark_mage`, in the C# statement order:

- the per-kind block (`:65813-65829`: the rotation = `vx * 0.04`,
  `spriteDirection`, the tunables — `num3` 2, `num4` 0.05, `num5` 0.2,
  `num6` -0.05, `num7` -0.4, `num8` 0.5, `num9` 0.1, `num10` 0.5,
  `num11` 0.02; note `flag5 = false`, so the upward probe at
  `:66058-66078` never runs);
- the materialize (`:65928-65962`): `localAI[3]` (the port's
  `caster_counter`) ramps 0 → 60, `alpha = 255` on the first tick, then
  `alpha -= 5` clamped at 0;
- the cast cycle (`:65834-65881`) behind `flag6`/`num12 = 0.9`, whose
  tail (`:66024-66028`) returns before the gravity/steer block: the summon
  673 at `ai[0] == 64` (`ai[1] == 2`), the shadowflame 675 at 32
  (`ai[1] == 0`, `direction` re-aimed from the shot vector), the heal 674
  at 40/48/56 (`ai[1] == 1`), and the `ai[0] <= 0` re-roll (-20 after the
  shadowflame, -120 otherwise);
- the re-arm (`:65882-65927`): `ai[0] == 0 && localAI[3] >= 60` picks the
  97/127/183 window per `ai[1]`, gated by `flag9` (`:65905-65909` — the
  shadowflame round needs the target within 1000 px and in line of sight);
- the walk-anchor stuck detector (`:65968-66019`) and the
  `TargetClosestOldOnesInvasion` retarget / `FaceTarget` write of
  `direction`+`directionY` (`:66009-66012`, inside the detector's
  `localAI[2] >= 0` branch);
- the probe columns (`:66020-66072`), the float gravity (`:66079-66097`),
  the `collideX`/`collideY` bounces off `oldVelocity` (`:66098-66121`) and
  the four steer blocks (`:66122-66185`).

`Npc` gained `direction_y`, `collide_x`, `collide_y`, `old_vx`, `old_vy`
and `dark_mage_local[3]` (the C#'s `directionY`, `collideX`, `collideY`,
`oldVelocity.X/Y` and `localAI[0..2]`).

**The deliberate gaps.** `DD2Event.RaiseGoblins` (`DD2Event.cs:716-...)`
needs `_deadGoblinSpots`, the DD2 event's dead-goblin coordinate list, which
the port's sim does not carry: the summon request rides `wants_sphere` as a
single `DD2GoblinT1` at the mage's centre instead of one raised goblin per
recorded death. `DD2Event.CanRaiseGoblinsHere` (`:699-714`, the
three-deaths-in-800-px gate) is likewise unmodelled, so the `ai[1] == 2` arm
is never dropped mid-sequence. The re-arm's `flag8` scan (two damaged NPCs
in the 1200x400 box, `:65884-65896`) needs the NPC list the AI method cannot
see, and the `OnlyCrystal` half of `TargetClosestOldOnesInvasion`'s search
(`NPCUtils.cs:268`, the 548 crystal) needs it too — the player arm of the
search is modelled. `GetAttackDamage_ScaledByDifficulty` runs
classic (the port has no difficulty-scaled NPC damage for this kind). The
three tracked sounds (`DD2_EtherianPortalSpawnEnemy` at `localAI[3] == 30`,
`DD2_DarkMageSummonSkeleton` at `ai[0] == 80`, `DD2_DarkMageCastHeal` at
`ai[0] == 126`) and the portal dust ramp (`:65944-65961`, dust type 27)
ride the audio and dust passes, which the port's NPC AI does not drive yet.

## The F3 developer workbench (S1-E-29, 2026-11-16)

The F3 cheat-sheet panel is **project-specific**: vanilla Terraria 1.4.5.8 binds F3
to `Loadout3` (`PlayerInput.cs:2090,2203,2315,2427` в†’ `TriggersSet.cs:813-816` в†’
`Player.TrySwitchingLoadout(2)`) and ships no debug overlay, so there is no vanilla
panel to be 1:1 with. The port's panel is therefore a dev tool, and the deviations
below are recorded rather than resolved:

* **The crate seam.** The panel lives in `tr-debug` (state, layout, hit-testing,
  `Event` intents) with `tr-app` supplying the rows, the drawing and the action
  application. The direction is forced: `tr-app` is a binary crate (`[[bin]]`, no
  `[lib]`), so it cannot be a dependency of `tr-debug`. The gameplay consequence is
  nil вЂ” the actions are the unchanged code; only the hit-testing moved.
* **The Cargo feature.** `debug` (default OFF) gates the module, the `App` field,
  its two initialisers and the six call sites, so a release build without it
  contains no panel. `TR_DEBUG`/`TR_STATS`/`render/debug.rs` are **not** gated: they
  are the separate F1 stats overlay and the deterministic-screenshot workflow needs
  `TR_DEBUG=0`.
* **Recipes tab.** Gives `craft::RECIPES[i].create` straight into the inventory with
  no station, ingredient or crafting-hour check. That is deliberate for a debug give
  and is *not* a claim about `Recipe`'s availability rules (`Recipe.cs:15162-15191`
  etc. stay unported).
* **Action semantics.** The World rows now call the real C# entries (S1-E-37, landed
  2026-11-16) instead of flipping flags — `WorldGen.StartHardmode`
  (`WorldGen.cs:31701-31719`, the runner half *and* the `Lang.misc[15]` broadcast plus
  progression 9), `Main.StartInvasion` (`Main.cs:64435-64486`), `Main.StartSlimeRain`/
  `StopSlimeRain` (`:64742-64820`) and the blood-moon hit body (`:65344-65346`). The
  goblin row's old `80` and the slime row's `43200` were both wrong and are gone. The
  panel cannot switch hardmode back off: the C# `StartHardmode` returns early when
  `hardMode` is set (`:31703`), and the port's `start_hardmode` does the same, so the
  old toggle-off revert is gone. The **kill-all row stays project-specific**: no
  `KillAll`/`KillAllNPCs` exists in the decompilation, so its `hp = 0` sweep is the
  port's own dev shortcut and is not claimed as a port. The pause row *is* exact
  (`WorldUpdateStepper.cs:45-49`) and its test pins it. `main.remixWorld`/
  `isThereAWorldSurface`/the announcement and `netMode` arms of the invasion and slime
  functions fold out — the port is single-player and none of those flags exist.
* **Upstream reference only.** The feature set takes *behaviour* references from
  CheatSheet (no licence file, credits Gameiki) and HEROsMod (GPLv3); no code, data
  or art is copied or adapted, so nothing of theirs ships.

## S1-L-1 - scene metrics: ScanOnScreenTiles / ScanNPCPositions / the ore finder (2026-11-16)

The scan now runs the whole `SceneMetrics.Scan` body (`SceneMetrics.cs:326-351`) in
source order: `ScanTiles`, `ScanOnScreenTiles`, `ScanNPCPositions`,
`AggregateTileCounts`, `CalculateZones`. Readings behind deliberate deviations:

* **The visual rect.** `Main.cs:62536-62537` is `Main.GetAreaToLight()` then
  `.Inflate(28, 28)`; `GetAreaToLight` (`:63926-63936`) is the *scaled* camera rect,
  `floor(pos/16) - 1` to `floor((pos+size)/16) + 2`. The port has no
  `GameViewMatrix`, and its `camera` + `screen / zoom` is exactly the world-space
  view the tile pass already draws (`render/tiles.rs:312-318`), so the rect is
  derived the same way. Zoom is the only divergence: vanilla's scaled camera differs
  from ours by the view matrix translation, which the port does not model. The rect
  only gates the music box / clock / fountain / monolith reads, all of which are
  single-tile proximity probes - a one-tile difference shifts a fountain colour by at
  most one tile of the view, never the pixel output of an unrelated pass.
* **`ScanNPCPositions` is gated on `npcs` being passed**, not on the C#
  `settings.ScanNPCPositions` bool (`Main.cs:62541` always sets it; `Player.cs:16683`
  also always sets it). `scan_scene_at` (the unit-test entry) passes none, so the
  array stays zeroed there - the C# would clear it in `Reset` regardless (`:786`).
* **`nPC.active` is approximated by `hp > 0`.** The port reaps dead NPCs at the end of
  the NPC tick (`world_sim/npcs.rs`'s `retain(|n| n.hp > 0)`), so a slot in
  `app.npcs` with `hp <= 0` is the transient state between the kill and the retain -
  which the C# would also skip via `active == false`.
* **`NPCBannerBuff` indexing** keeps the port's `vec![false; 320]`; the C# is
  `BannerSystem.MaxBannerTypes = 293` (`BannerSystem.cs:1453`). Only ids < 293 are
  ever written by `banner_num_from_frame`, so the wider vec is inert.
* **Not ported (no reader in the port):** `PartyMonolithCount` (the party monolith
  tile is not in the port's tile set), `MoonLordMonolith` (tile 623's state only
  feeds `ManageSpecialBiomeVisuals("MoonLord", ...)`, unported), `CanPlayCreditsRoll`
  (`ActiveMusicBox == 85` only gates the credits roll, which the port does not have),
  and the `AddPlayerEffects` arms for held items 148/3117/5322 plus
  `player.musicBox`/`musicBoxSilence`/`happyFunTorchTime` (`:747-774`) - the player
  struct has none of those fields. `shimmerWet` is the one `AddPlayerEffects` input
  the port does carry and it is wired (it was already).
* **`ActiveFountainColor` has no consumer yet.** `Main.CalculateWaterStyle`
  (`Main.cs:57387-57392`) returns it when `>= 0`, but the port's
  `biome::calculate_water_style` derives the style from the camera alone and does not
  take the metrics. Wiring it means threading the scan through three call sites
  (`frame.rs:1131`, `render/tiles.rs:322`, `rain.rs:941`) — the water-style half of
  the row, not this one.
* **`TownNPCCount` is now real.** It feeds `MusicEnv.town_npcs` (the `>= 3` town
  music gate, `Main.cs:12199`) and `SpawnContext.town_npcs` (the spawn-pressure
  tiers, `NPC.cs:604-621`), both of which were hardcoded to `0` with an "M4-TOWN"
  comment. The port does spawn town NPCs (`NpcKind::is_town_npc`), so this was a
  real behavioural gap, not a placeholder.

### S1-E-37's remaining deviations

Three, all forced by the port's shape:

* **The bare RNG stream.** The C# debug console is a chat-command dispatcher
  (`ToolkitDebugCommands`) running outside every `Main.SwapRandom` block, so the
  `Main.rand` it touches is the bare stream. The port has no chat-command layer
  (S1-E-29's deviation) and models it with `NamedRngs::global()` (the `key: None`
