  arm of `start_invasion_in` and the slime rows' draws), seeded from the world seed
  rather than `DateTime.Now.Ticks` — the S1-A-10 deviation, unchanged here.
* **`StartHardmode` runs inline.** `WorldGen.StartHardmode` (`WorldGen.cs:31701-31719`)
  defers the strip walk to a background thread
  (`TransformWorldOnBackgroundThread`, `:31721-31742`) and queues the chat/achievement
  follow-up back to the main thread. The port's `start_hardmode` transforms inline
  and then runs the follow-up in the same call. `TryProtectingSpawnedItems`/
  `UndoSpawnedItemProtection` (`:31708`/`:31717`) have no ported consumer.
* **The kill-all row has no C# counterpart** (see above) — its sweep stays as-is.

## The boss sprite direction and roll audit (S1-G-19, 2026-11-16)

Every sprite flip in the renderer comes from one field — `Npc::sprite_dir`
(`render/entities.rs:2603`) — because that is what the C# does: `Main.cs:23124-23128`
draws mirrored iff `spriteDirection == 1`. Two failure modes follow, and both were
present:

* **A sign slip mirrors the whole sprite.** `AI()`'s boss arms write
  `direction = spriteDirection = (Center.X < target.Center.X) ? 1 : -1`, i.e. **+1
  when the player is to the right**. The port had four of Betsy's written as
  `if pcx < cx { 1 } else { -1 }` (`:61899`, `:61902`, `:61999`, `:62053`), so the
  dragon faced away from the player for half of every phase. Fixed to `cx < pcx`.
* **A kind absent from the rotation whitelist never rolls.** The renderer opts each
  kind into the generic `Main.cs:26632` rotation draw by an explicit list
  (`render/entities.rs:2611-2660`), because most NPC kinds leave `rotation` at zero
  and would be rotated by garbage. `NpcKind::DD2Betsy` was missing from it while
  `update_betsy` was already writing `npc.rotation` — the whole `AngleTowards` tail
  (`:62256-62301`) was dead. The kind is now listed and the tail ported: the
  per-phase `num40` aim / `num41` turn rate (phases 2 and 5 write `num41 = 0` and so
  keep the phase's own aim; 3 starts at 0.01 and switches to 0.05 with a
  `±π/12` lean once `ai[1] >= 40`; 4 aims at `π` or `2π`; 6 at 0.02), then the
  unconditional `spriteDirection == -1` π fold before `angle_towards`.

The Wall of Flesh's eye was the mirror-image bug in a literal sense: the port had
invented its own aim logic for the eye, while `AI()`'s aiStyle-28 arm
(`:26066-26068`) simply copies the parent — `position.X = wof.X - width/2`,
`direction = spriteDirection = wof.direction`, `position.Y -= height/2` — so the eye
always looks the way the mouth does. The parent's direction is now carried on the
world (`World::wof_dir`) because the eye's update has no access to the body NPC, and
`update_wof_eye` mirrors it.

Two structural traps met in the same pass, both of which had produced *silently*
wrong port code rather than a visible mirror flip:

* `AI_045_Golem`'s charge block is gated on the literal `velocity.Y == 0f`
  (`:19640`), this repo's `Npc::on_ground` is the tile-contact flag written by the
  integration step. They agree for a settled body and disagree for a body whose
  velocity was just zeroed by a wall or a test fixture; the C# spelling is the one
  that was ported.
* The golem's flight `vy` sink (`:19727-19730`) is applied only while
  `Bottom.Y < player.position.Y` **and** the horizontal span test passes — the span
  test compares both edges (`position.X < player.position.X && position.X + width >
  player.position.X + player.width`), not the centres.

Not ported, and now filed as **S1-D-3p**: `NPC.TargetClosest` `:77652-77781`
including `TryTrackingTarget`/`SetTargetTrackingValues`, `targetRect`,
`npcTypeNoAggro`, `tankPet` gating, `confused`, `oldTarget` and `DirectionY`. The
port has no such method; each machine writes `facing`/`sprite_dir` itself, and
`npc_ai.rs::walker_step`'s `aggro_x`/`aggro_y` window (80×40 tiles at the call sites)
is an invention with no C# counterpart. Retrofitting it changes which NPC targets
which for every aiStyle-3 kind, so it needs its own branch and its own test pass.
**The helper landed with S1-D-3p (2026-11-18)** — see "The shared target selection
(S1-D-3p)" below; the caller migration is the documented remainder.

## The Destroyer machine (aiStyle-37, S1-D-3, 2026-11-18 — code-only mode)

`NPC.AI_037_Destroyer` (`NPC.cs:49756-50242`, dispatched at `:28991-28994`)
is ported as `crates/tr-app/src/npc_ai_style37.rs` — pure functions over the
NPC pool (`destroyer_step(npcs, me, ctx, world, players, rng, ticker)`), with
the side effects the `Npc` struct cannot carry returned in `DestroyerEvents`
(the `wants_sphere`/`wants_limbs` seam convention). **Code-only mode**: no
compiler was invoked; the 10 witness tests are written, not run.

Faithful details kept: the Mech Queen chain walk's 10-link reset
(`:49772-49776`), the fade-in's parent-alpha gate (`alpha < 128`, `:49795`)
and 42-step floor (`:49806-49810`), the orphan check's `ai[1] <= 0 ||
parent.life <= 0` (`:49816-49823`), the head's `ai[0] == 0` one-shot spawn
(`:49833`), the laser cadence's **two draws every tick** (`Next(4)` `:49858`
then `Next(1400, 26000)` `:49859` — the threshold draw happens even on a
non-firing tick) and the four `Next(-20, 21)` jitters in source order inside
the `Collision.CanHit` gate (`:49866-49872`), the muzzle's float-X /
INTEGER-Y halves (`:49865`), the speed-8 normalise then ×0.05 spread then ×5
muzzle offset (`:49868-49876`), `GetAttackDamage_ForProjectiles(22, 18)` =
`(int)Remap(difficulty, 1, 2, 22, 18)` clamped (`NPC.cs:7052-7055`,
`Utils.cs:315-348`), the tile probe's `nactive && (solid || (solidTop &&
frameY == 0)) || liquid > 64` with NO `inActive()` test (`:49912` — unlike
`Collision`'s gates), the head's 1000-px player-proximity dive gate
(`:49934-49951`), the daytime double-sink + family despawn
(`:49959-49977`), the getGoodWorld ×1.2 accel (`:49981-49985`), the 16-px
snapped aim with INTEGER player halves (`:49987-49994`), the follower's
`(int)(44 * scale)` spacing with the Mech Queen 10%-per-depth compression
and the `num24 / num2 * num` INTEGER division (`:49998-50027`), the
velocity-zeroed teleport + the pre-move-centre final rotation (`:50030-50033`),
the three-way air steer and the burrow's aligned/any-aligned/dominant-axis
ladder with the two perpendicular ×2 turn boosts (`:50037-50205`), the
`+ 1.57f` rotation literal (NOT π/2, `:50021`/`:50206`), the head's
`localAI[0]` burrow-state net flag + the oldVelocity sign-reversal flag
(`:50207-50229`), and the Mech Queen ride's `RotatedBy(velocity.X * 0.025)`
about `GetMechQueenCenter` + 100 px (`:50231-50241`, `Utils.cs:1675-1684`,
`NPC.cs:50954-50961`).

Deliberate deviations (the wiring remainder):

* **Wiring deferred.** The sim's Destroyer still rides the aiStyle-6 worm
  pass (`npc.rs`'s `NpcKind::TheDestroyer => {}` arm +
  `world_sim/npcs.rs::update_worms_in`'s 80-budget same-kind chain). The
  machine is not called from `Npc::update_rng`'s style axis yet — the port
  has no body/tail kinds (135/136), so the chain the machine expects
  (`ai[1]` parent links, `ai[0]` child links) does not exist in the pool.
  The machine is type-parameterised (`DestroyerCtx::npc_type`) so the
  body/tail branches activate unchanged when those kinds land.
* **Seam effects.** Dust 182 (`:49801`), `Lighting.AddLight(0.3, 0.1, 0.05)`
  (`:49929`), `SoundEngine.PlaySound(15)` (`:50093`), `HitEffect`/`checkDead`
  (`:49827-49828`), the 80-link `NewNPC` allocation + `SendData(23)`
  (`:49847-49852`), the laser's `Projectile.NewProjectile` (`:49877`) and
  the family `active = false` despawn (`:49974`) ride `DestroyerEvents` —
  the caller resolves them (the port's pool has no `active` field and
  compacts every frame).
* **Stock flags.** `netMode = 0`, classic difficulty, no Mech Queen
  (S1-D-3j), no getGoodWorld — the same constants-off convention as the
  other difficulty-gated machines. `soundDelay`/`justHit` have no `Npc`
  fields; the ctx carries them (the wiring's `justHit` stand-in is
  `hurt_cd > 0.0`, the port's recoil convention).
* **Pool indices vs C# slots.** `Main.npc` is a fixed 201-slot array
  (`Main.cs:66989`); the port's Vec compacts. A missing `ai[1]` slot reads
  as the C#'s `try/catch` outcome (`:49999-50007`: keep the snapped player
  aim); the orphan check treats it as a dead parent (the C# would throw —
  the port's chain never carries dangling links because the worm pass
  kills them, `:51425-51433`).
* **RNG argument.** The machine's only draws are the body laser's: per
  tick `Next(4)` (`UnifiedRandom.cs:134-141` → `next_max(4)`) then
  `Next(1400, 26000)` (`:120-132` → `next_range`), and on a firing tick
  four `Next(-20, 21)` in the order aim-X, aim-Y, spread-X, spread-Y. All
  take the caller's `UnifiedRandom` (the exact `Main.rand` stream) — the
  witness tests clone the stream and replay the draws in source order, so
  any reordering or extra draw fails the equality. No other stream is
  touched; the head's machine is draw-free.

## The shared target selection (S1-D-3p, 2026-11-18)

`NPC.TargetClosest`/`TryTrackingTarget`/`SetTargetTrackingValues`
(`NPC.cs:77652-77781`) is now ported as `crates/tr-app/src/npc_target.rs`
(`target_closest` + the `TargetCandidate`/`TankPet` inputs). The port is
1:1: the slot-order scan with the strict `<` replacement (first slot wins
ties, `:77693`), the Manhattan metric minus `Player.aggro` (`:77687-77688`),
the `npcTypeNoAggro && direction != 0` +1000 penalty (`:77689-77692`), the
tank-pet steal (`distance − 200`, both `< distance` and `< 200`, plus the
1×1-centre `Collision.CanHit` walk, `:77701-77709` — the port's
`projectile::can_hit`, S1-D-7), the int-truncated `targetRect`
(`:77717`/`:77735`), the INTEGER half-extent centre facing (the C# casts
`(float)(base.width / 2)` AFTER the int divide, `:77719`/`:77752`), the
aiStyle-3 bottom-edge `directionY` with `<=` (`:77761-77768`), the dead /
no-aggro facing suppression (`:77736-77743`), the `oldTarget ∈ 0..=254 &&
itemAnimation == 0 && aggro < 0 && !boss` facing-inheritance gate
(`:77748-77749`), the buff-31 confused flip (`:77772-77775`; the C# latches
`this.confused` in the buff scan `:92029-92032`, the port reads
`NpcBuffs::find_buff_index(31)`), the collide-gated `netUpdate`
(`:77776-77779`) and the `targetSetFrame` stamp (`:77780`). The `Npc`
struct gained `target` (the `ClearTarget` 255 default, `NPC.cs:8539`,
`:42924-42927`), `target_rect`, `target_set_frame`, `old_target`,
`old_direction`, `old_direction_y`, `net_update`, `boss`.

Deliberate deviations (the migration remainder):

* **One caller wired.** `update_zombie` (`npc.rs`) is the representative:
  it calls the helper under the `AI_003` chase gate
  (`DespawnEncouragement_AIStyle3_Fighters_NotDiscouraged`, `NPC.cs:57336`,
  `:60300-60330` — for type 3 only the non-eclipse-day-above-surface terms
  can fire) and drops the invented 80×40-tile aggro window. The other ~29
  `walker_step` callers and every ad-hoc-facing AI keep their current
  writes until the migration; `walker_step`'s `aggro_x`/`aggro_y` params
  stay for them (the C# has no such window — the chase is gated by the
  despawn-discouragement arm, not a distance box).
* **Stock player inputs.** `Player.aggro`, `npcTypeNoAggro` and `tankPet`
  have no port fields (the stealth armour / tank pets are unported
  systems); the wiring passes 0/false/None, the C# stock values. The
  helper itself implements all three gates and the parity tests exercise
  them through `TargetCandidate`.
* **The zombie's velocity write stays direct** (`facing * 1f`): the C#'s
  0.07-per-tick approach with the 0.8 overspeed brake (`NPC.cs:58378-58400`)
  belongs to the full `AI_003_Fighters` migration, not the target helper.
  A dead target keeps the port's 0.9 decay (the C# keeps walking toward
  the corpse; the facing suppression is ported, the walk arm is the
  migration's).
* **The `old_*` latches** (`NPC.cs:90393-90395`, `UpdateNPC`'s head) are
  not yet run from `Npc::update_rng`; the helper reads whatever the caller
  latched. Until the migration adds the head latch, `old_target` holds
  the spawn-time 255, so the inheritance gate stays inert in live play
  (the tests drive it explicitly).
* **`targetSetFrame` stamps 0** from the zombie wiring: the
  `Main.EverLastingTicker` (`Main.cs:413`, `:17177`) is not plumbed into
  `Npc::update`; the stamp's only C# reader is the target-line fade
  (`Main.cs:57174`), unported. The helper takes the ticker as a parameter.
* **`NPC.boss` defaults false for every kind** — the per-type
  `SetDefaults` boss rows land with the caller migration; the gate's
  `!boss` term is ported and tested.

11 parity tests (`npc_target::tests`): the aggro metric, the no-aggro
penalty + facing suppression, the rect truncation + int-centre ties, the
aiStyle-3 bottom-edge arm, the oldTarget inheritance (swing/fresh/boss
breaks), the confused flip, the tank steal + its LOS wall, the dead/absent
fallback, the netUpdate collide gate, and the zombie wiring proof.

## The buff hover's two dropped arms (S1-E-6 follow-up, 2026-11-16)

`Main.GetBuffTooltip` (`Main.cs:43254-43289`) has a `switch` over the buff id
whose two arms print a *player-computed* percentage rather than a static
localization string:

* `case 94` (`ManaSickness`) formats `Player.manaSickReduction` into the
  `ManaSickness2` row of `Terraria.Localization.Content.en-US.Game.json`.
* `case 396` (`ManaHeat`) does the same with `Player.manaHeat`.

The port has neither `Player.manaSickReduction` nor `Player.manaHeat`: the
mana-sickness debuff applies its magic-damage multiplier inline in the damage
path and stores no reduction field, and 396 does not exist at all. Rather than
invent a field whose value no other system maintains,
`ui::resources::buff_tooltip` falls back to the plain `BuffDescription.{name}`
row for both ids. When the 94/396 buff *effects* land (M2-BUFF-3/4) the fields
will exist and these two arms can be restored — the ported code is already a
`match` over the id, so adding them is two arms.

Two further colours are dropped rather than approximated: `MouseTextInner`'s
`-13` (master) and `-12` (disco) rarity arms read `Main.masterColor` and
`Main.Disco*`, neither of which the port keeps. The buff hover never passes
those rarities (`Main.cs:43239-43246` only uses `-10` for the melee buffs and
`0` otherwise), so they are unreachable from this call site;
`ui::resources::mouse_text_color` documents them and defers to the shared
`tooltip::item_name_color` table for every other value.

## Entity lights (S1-E-5, 2026-11-16)

The C# funnels every `Lighting.AddLight` overload into
`Lighting.AddLight(int i, int j, float r, float g, float b)` (`Lighting.cs:157-163`),
which appends to the active `ILightingEngine`'s per-frame list behind
`!Main.gamePaused && Main.netMode != 2` (`LightingEngine.cs:51-54`). The engine
max-merges that list onto the working map (`LightingEngine.cs:215-225`) and then
swaps it with the previous frame's list, clearing the current one
(`:226-233`) — so a source added this tick is **visible to the light pass one frame
later**, and only if a swap ran in between (`Main.GameUpdateCount` guards the swap
against two passes in one update).

Ported here: that list pair (`crates/tr-app/src/entity_lights.rs::EntityLights`) and
one source family, `WorldItem.UpdateItem_VisualEffects` (`WorldItem.cs:1204-1649`).
The pass runs in `app/frame.rs` after `LightParams` is built, because that is the
only place the struct exists; `tr-core`'s `compute_into_with_lights` takes a single
`&[DynamicLight]`, so `render/tiles.rs` concatenates the waterfall list and the
entity list into `DrawScratch::all_lights` before the compute. **List order is the
only ordering constraint** — no ported arm draws RNG, so the frame position of the
feed cannot change the fixed-step order or any stream.

* **14 arms that draw `Main.rand` are not ported at all** — 5043, 116, 3191,
  520/3454, 521/3455, 547/3453, 548, 575, 549, 58/1734/1867, 184/1735/1868/4143,
  522 and 1332 (`WorldItem.cs:1206, 1211, 1224, 1229, 1234, 1239, 1244, 1249, 1254,
  1259, 1264, 1269, 1274`). Each mixes its `AddLight` with a `Dust.NewDust` whose
  draws ride `Main.rand`, and the dust system belongs to the S1-E-2/S1-E-3 branches.
  Skipping a whole arm leaves the stream untouched, which is exact — the port does
  not consume the `Next(90, 111)` those arms would have drawn.
* **Two arms are ported for their light half only**: 75 (`:1624-1635`) and the
  `BossBag` set (`:1636-1648`). Both draw `Main.rand` only inside a
  `timeSinceItemSpawned % 12 == 0` dust branch that the port does not run, so the
  `AddLight` line itself is RNG-free and exact; the dust is the dust task's.
  Because the port omits the whole branch, the `Main.rand` calls are never reached
  and that arm's stream position is skipped rather than shortened.
* **The four `Main.essScale` arms (3456-3459) are not ported.** `Main.essScale`
  drifts between 0.7 and 1.0 once per draw pass (`Main.cs:62264-62277`, seeded 1.0
  at `:66673`) and has no port field yet. The four rows are all-`Vector3` scaled
  colours with no other state, so they are cheap to add once `essScale` exists; until
  then the four gemspark blocks emit no light.
* **`base.wet` is the gate, not `Collision.WetCollision` verbatim.** The C# sets
  `base.wet` from `Collision.WetCollision(position, width, height)`
  (`WorldItem.cs:870`) in the movement half that runs *before*
  `UpdateItem_VisualEffects` (`:436`). `ItemDrop::box_is_wet` (`crates/tr-app/src/item.rs`)
  tests the same 14×14 box for `tile.liquid > 0`; `box_in_shimmer` is the same helper
  with the shimmer predicate. The item box is `ItemDrop::SIZE` (14) in both, matching
  `Entity.width`/`height` for a dropped item.
* **The `createTile == 4` arm shadows 19 per-id arms.** `WorldItem.cs:1375` comes
  before every later `type == N` test, and every placeable torch has
  `createTile == 4` — so the per-id arms for 3114, 1245, 433, 523, 974, 1333, 4383,
  5293, 5353, 4384, 3045, 3004, 2274 and 427-432 are **unreachable in vanilla**.
  They all take the `Lighting.AddLight(base.Center, placeStyle)` overload
  (`Lighting.cs:151-155`) instead, i.e. `TorchID.TorchColor(placeStyle)` at full
  amount, positioned by `(int)Center.X / 16` — truncate *then* divide, which the
  port models as `XAnchor::CenterTruncated` (the two forms differ only for negative
  pixel positions but the port must not pick one at random). The port keeps the
  dead arms in source order rather than deleting them: they cost nothing, they keep
  the arm list comparable to the C#, and deleting them would be an unforced
  divergence that a later refactor could misread as a *missing* port. The
  Cursed Torch (523) is the visible case — a `WaterTorches` row, so it stays lit
  under water where a plain torch goes dark.
* **Remaining source families.** Projectile (107 call sites — the `ProjLight`
  chain's common tail `:16659` landed 2026-11-18, see below), Player (46),
  Dust (94), Mount (14), TileDrawing (6) and the particles/gore rows are **not**
  ported. `Gore.Update`'s own lights (`Gore.cs:258`, `:940`, `:1076-1080`) can now be
  expressed through `EntityLights` but still need a seam from `tr-core` — the gore
  pool has no light sink, so they stay dropped. The NPC family is **started**
  (2 of 80 call sites), see below.

### The NPC family (S1-E-5, 2026-11-18)

`crates/tr-app/src/npc_lights.rs::npc_light` ports the aiStyle-8 light tail at
the end of `NPC.AI` (`NPC.cs:21280-21373`) — the type chain the C# runs after
`base.position += netOffset` (`:21279`; the feed reads the offset position too,
restored at `:21374`). It feeds the **same** `EntityLights` pair as the item
family (one list pair per engine in the C#, not one per family) and shares the
tile-anchor vocabulary (`entity_lights.rs::XAnchor`/`tile_x`/`tile_y`); both
feeds run in the frame pass (`app/frame/draw.rs`), after the step, in `Main.npc`
slot order. Of the NPC family's **80 `Lighting.AddLight` call sites, 2 landed**:

* **`NPC.cs:21360` — the Desert Djinn (533)**: `AddLight(base.Top, 0.6f, 0.6f,
  0.3f)`. `base.Top` is `(position.X + width/2f, position.Y)` (`Entity.cs:86-91`)
  — centre x, top y — and the `Vector2` overload truncates the quotient per
  axis (`Lighting.cs:140-143`); the port models it as `XAnchor::Top`. The kind
  itself landed with this task: `SetDefaults` 28x62 / damage 40 / defense 20 /
  lifeMax 220 / kb 0 / value 1200 (`NPC.cs:14974-14987`), `FindFrame` case 533's
  8-row hover cycle + the cast windup's `+8` row bank (`:69978-69992`,
  `npcFrameCount[533]` = 16, `Main.cs:67082`), and the AI cycle's own constants
  (`CasterParams::DESERT_DJINN`): the single `ai[0] == 180` trigger sets
  `ai[1] = 181` (`:21031-21038`) and the wrap fires at 360 (`:21079-21082`),
  not the standard 100/200/300 → 30 / 650.
* **`NPC.cs:21365` — the aiStyle-8 else arm**: `AddLight(base.Center, 0.6f,
  0.6*0.65f, 0.6*0.4f)` — the Fire Imp (24) is the port's only remaining
  aiStyle-8 kind. The arm's `Main.rand.Next(6)` dust half (`:21366-21372`) is
  skipped wholesale (the RNG rule below).

**What stays dropped, exactly:**

* The 29/45/32 arms (`:21280-21300`) are **dust-only** — no `AddLight` — so the
  sorcerer/Tim/Dark Caster stay dark; nothing to port until the dust system.
* The Djinn's curse volley (`:21117-21230`) draws `Main.rand`
  (`:21140-21141`'s target-tile rolls, `:21195-21196`'s velocity jitter) — the
  whole volley is skipped (`shoot_tick: None`), so the Djinn never fires and
  the `Main.rand` stream stays untouched. The teleport half of its cycle is
  RNG-shared with the standard casters and rides the existing
  `find_teleport_spot` draws in the same order.
* The aiStyle-23 chain (`:25239-25250`) lights types **83 = CursedHammer** and
  **179 = CrimsonAxe** (`NPCID.cs:10843`/`:11035`) plus a fallback — neither
  kind is in the port's roster (PrimeVice 130 rides aiStyle 34,
  DD2KoboldFlyerT3 575 aiStyle 108; they never reach that chain). The three
  arms wait for those kinds.
* The remaining **76 NPC call sites** (the aiStyle-9 sphere glow `:21561`, the
  boss AIs' lights, the `UpdateNPC` tail's torch/buff lights `:90841-92412`,
  etc.) are not ported; each needs its AI family or a rand-bearing dust arm
  first.

Tests: `npc_lights.rs` pins the Djinn's Top-anchor tile + colour (incl. the
centre-x vs left-edge difference and negative-coordinate truncation), the Fire
Imp's else-arm centre light, and the dark casters; `npc.rs`'s
`the_desert_djinn_rides_its_own_trigger_and_wrap` pins the 180/181/360 cycle and
the skipped volley; the protocol round-trip roster grew 198 → 199.

### The projectile family (S1-E-5, 2026-11-18)

**Code-only mode**: this round ran with no compiler invoked — no `cargo`, no
`rustc`, no `rustfmt`, no test runs, no graphify. The port and its tests are
written but not executed; verification is the C# citations plus the witness
tests below, to be run by the next build pass.

`crates/tr-app/src/proj_lights.rs::proj_light` ports `Projectile.ProjLight`
(`Projectile.cs:16153-16661`) — the per-type colour chain that multiplies the
slot's `light` amount into one `AddLight` at the integer-halved centre
(`:16659`). `Update` calls it once per movement sub-step (`:17031`), after
`HandleMovement` and the active re-check (`:17027-17030`). The feed is ONE loop
in `app/frame/draw.rs` beside the item and NPC feeds, after the step, in
`Main.projectile` slot order, into the **same** `EntityLights` pair (the pair is
not duplicated); the one-frame delay is the existing `end_frame`/`visible`
machinery. Of the Projectile family's **107 call sites, the chain's common tail
landed**, serving every chain arm whose kind has a `proj_data` row — 36 kinds:
the torch/bullet commons (2 FlameArrow, 6 EnchantedBoomerang, 14/110/180 the
`:16338` bullet arm), the hooks (73/74 DualHook, 332 Christmas, 446 AntiGravity,
488 Illuminant), the magic family (15/16/27/34/94/95/96/113/114/115/116/132/156/
157/173/253/254/308/1134), the lasers (20/83/88/100/389), 45 DemonScythe, 79
RainbowRodBullet (the `Main.DiscoR/G/B` overwrite rides `LightParams::disco`),
80 IceBlock, 259 GolemEyeBeam (the `Main.getGoodWorld` blackout `:16237-16242`
rides the world's For-the-Worthy seed flag) and 180 PirateArrow.

**The amount's journey.** `Projectile.light` (`:378`/`:773`'s stock `0f`) rides a
new `light: f32` field on `ProjData` + `Projectile`; the `SetDefaults` slice is
`projectile.rs::set_defaults_light` (36 rows, each cited to its `this.light =`
line), copied onto the slot by the data-carrying spawn. The aiStyle-24 arm
rewrites its shard's amount per tick — `this.light = this.scale * 0.5f`
(`:25953`) — now live in `ai_crystal_storm`, **before** that tick's fade, so a
faded shard's frame contribution reads the pre-fade scale's half.

**Stream neutrality (by construction).** `proj_light` is pure — it takes no RNG
and no ported arm draws `Main.rand`. The two rand-bearing chain arms (867
`:16217`, 1000 `:16224` — `Main.rand.Next(28, 42)`) have **no `proj_data` rows**,
so no slot can ever reach them; they are absent wholesale and the
`UpdateProjectiles` stream is untouched. The feed's placement after the step is
therefore list-order-only (the item/NPC argument above applies verbatim). The
witness test `test_s1_e_5_the_light_feed_leaves_the_rng_stream_untouched`
interleaves the feed with 60 seeded steps and pins the stream state against a
feed-less run.

**The centre anchor is exact, not approximate.** `:16659` halves the **integer**
width/height before the float cast (`(float)(width / 2)`); `XAnchor::Center`
halves in float. The forms differ only for odd sides — and every lit
`proj_data` row has even sides (the only odd-sided row, 449 SaucerLaser 5×5,
carries no light). `proj_center_matches_the_float_anchor_for_every_lit_row`
walks `spawnable_kinds()` and pins both the even-side invariant and the
anchor agreement at a fractional position.

**What stays dropped, exactly:**

* The 870 Jack 'O Lantern's `FloodFillTile` + `AddLight` pair (`:16648-16656`):
  no row, and the flood fill has no port.
* The RNG arms 867/1000 (`:16215-16228`): no rows; absent wholesale (above).
* The disco arms 993 (`:16194-16198`, the glowstick-bobber `switch`), 1089
  (`:16434-16439`) and 251 (`:16630-16641`, the `(disco+1)/2 × light` form):
  no rows — cheap follow-ups once their kinds land (`LightParams::disco` is
  already threaded for the 79 arm).
* The 211 Shadowbeam arm (`:16601-16614`) **writes** `this.light` (1.5/1.0 by
  `localAI[0]`): no row, and a write inside the draw-pass feed would be a state
  mutation — it lands with its AI.
* The 209 alpha-scaled arm (`:16615-16623`): no row.
* The per-tick `light` writers outside `ProjLight`: the aiStyle-5 writers
  (`:23982`/`:24053` — kinds 12/955/92, none with rows; the gem bolts ride
  aiStyle 29, not this chain) and the aiStyle-8 tail's **502 disco light**
  (`:24302-24307` — `(0.5 + DiscoX/255)/2` per channel at `base.Center`, NOT
  scaled by `light`; the kind has no row, `ai_ball_of_fire` already skips the
  block). The FlameArrow's water transform (`:16822-16826` — `TransformType(1)`
  + `light = 0f`) drops with the projectile-water work: **until it lands, a wet
  FlameArrow keeps its light where the C# zeroes it** — a recorded deviation.
* The remaining **~105 non-`ProjLight` AI-arm call sites** (the mount's
  `:17343`, the electrification particles `:78556`, the boss/summon AI lights
  `:24877`/`:39020-39021`, etc.): each needs its AI family or a rand-bearing
  dust arm first.
* The WaterBolt 27's `:16380-16385` colour arm is ported but **unreachable**:
  its `SetDefaults` arm (`:1095-1105`) writes no `this.light`, so the slot keeps
  the `0f` reset and `ProjLight` early-returns — dead code in the C# too. The
  missing `set_defaults_light` row is faithful; the witness test
  `test_s1_e_5_the_water_bolt_has_no_set_defaults_light` pins it.

Tests (written, **not run** — code-only mode): `proj_lights.rs` pins the
`light > 0f` gate (incl. NaN/negative), the 14/110/180 bullet commons, the
absolute-colour arms (15/16/27/45/173/253/488), the 79 disco params, the 259
good-world blackout (the zeroed light is still appended), the 94/1134 shard
colours, the laser/hook arm colours, the negative-coordinate truncation and the
even-side anchor invariant; `projectile.rs`'s `proj_light_spawn_tests` pin the
spawn copy, the crystal-storm scale-driven rewrite across the fade gate, the
dark WaterBolt and the stream-neutrality witness.
### The Player family (S1-E-5, 2026-11-18, code-only mode)

`crates/tr-app/src/player_lights.rs::player_lights` ports **32 of Player.cs's
46 `Lighting.AddLight` call sites** — every RNG-free one — as pure functions
returning `(tile_x, tile_y, rgb)` contributions, mirroring `npc_lights.rs`'s
shape and sharing the `entity_lights.rs` anchor vocabulary
(`tile_x`/`tile_y`/`XAnchor`). The feed runs in `app/frame/draw.rs` beside the
item/NPC feeds, into the **same** `EntityLights` pair (one list pair per engine
in the C#, not one per family). Landed:

* **The four `UpdateBuffs` arms**: Shine 11 (`:9995`,
  `(int)(position.X + (float)(width / 2)) / 16` — the **int** division inside
  the cast, width 20 → 10, the live `height` for the y half), Inferno 116
  (`:10215`, quotient-truncating centre), Electrified 144 (`:10316`,
  pixel-truncating centre), Ice Barrier 62 (`:10466`, only at
  `statLife <= statLifeMax2 * 0.5`; the port's single `max_hp` stands in for
  both caps). Inferno's/Electrified's RGBs agree with `buff_effects.rs`'s
  S1-E-7b accumulator, which has no consumer yet — this scan is the live
  wiring; when the accumulator's scan lands, those two arms move to it.
* **The Jellyfish Necklace family** (`UpdateEquips` → `ApplyEquipFunctional`,
  `:15224-15262`): 1303/1860 dry (0.225, 0.05, 0.15) / wet (1.8, 0.4, 1.2),
  1861 the arctic pair. The walk reads `equipped[3..10]` — the C# reaches the
  arms only through the slot-3..10 loop (`:12946-12952`), so armor slots 0..2
  and the vanity rows never light (`IsItemSlotUnlockedAndUsable` folds true
  like `doll_flags`).
* **`ItemCheck_EmitHeldItemLight`** (`:49810-50194`), all 22 light lines: the
  biome torch (the `num3` → `num2` chain `:49824-49893` verbatim, clamped to
  `TorchID.Count - 1 = 23`, `TorchID.TorchColor` via
  `tile_light::torch_color`), candles 105/713, Water Candle 148 (no wet gate),
  Peace Candle 3117 (the `itemLocation.X -= direction * 4` nudge `:50019`;
  the light rides `velocity.X` but not the mount `+ pos`), Shadow Candle 5322,
  glowsticks 282/3002/286/3112/4776/5643 (the holdStyle-1 nudges
  `:50403-50412`; 5643 reads `LightParams.disco`), and 4952 — which has
  **holdStyle 6** (Item.cs case 4952), so its location comes from the
  `:50563-50573` arm (`Center.X + 8·dir`, `Y + 40 − 2 + headgear row offset`),
  then the light adds `(8·dir, −10·gravDir)` (`:50178`). Every point rides
  the ported `Player::rotated_relative_point`; `num` is the C#'s constant
  `1f` (`:49812`).

**RNG argument (stream order preserved by construction).** Every `Main.rand`
draw in the ported region sits inside a dust branch gated on
`stealth >= 1f` (`:49813`, `:49902`/`:49922`/`:49950`/…) or the 4952 tail's
`Next(40)` (`:50182`); the port skips those branches **wholesale** (the dust
system is S1-E-2/S1-E-3), so no draw is consumed and none is skipped
mid-stream — the `AddLight` lines themselves are RNG-free. The feed collects
after the fixed step like the item/NPC feeds; with zero draws in every arm,
the placement cannot move the UpdatePlayers stream. The witness tests pin
the arm order, the anchor forms and the gates (written, **not run** —
code-only mode).

**Deliberate folds / deviations:**

* `UsingBiomeTorches` (`:3950-3959`) is `unlockedBiomeTorches &&
  builderAccStatus[11] == 0`: the port reads `p.unlocked_biome_torches`
  (without the Torch God unlock the plain torch stays plain) and folds the
  builder toggle to 0 (on). `happyFunTorchTime` folds to false (no field).
* `BiomeTorchHoldStyle` (`:40291-40346`): the `ZoneShimmer` (`:40297`),
  `ZoneLihzhardTemple` (`:40305`), `ZoneUndergroundDesert` and remix-world
  desert arms (`:40337-40344`) read fields the port's `Zones` does not carry
  and are skipped **in place**; the dungeon arm (`:40301`, before the
  underworld one) and the surface-desert half land.
* The `ItemCheck` gate `!JustDroppedAnItem && IsAllowedToHoldItems`
  (`:42847`) folds to true (neither flag ported); `ApplyItemPositionOffsetFromMount`
  folds to zero (no mount offsets); 4952's `petting.isPetting` gate folds
  false; `gravDir` is 1 in the port.
* 4776's `Utils.FloodFillTile` spread (`:50135`) is dropped — it writes the
  light map directly, not the entity list; only the `AddLight(pos2, rgb)`
  line (`:50136`) lands.
* The dead player is skipped by the feed (like the dead NPCs); vanilla's
  residual buff light while dead needs the unported death visuals.

**What stays dropped (the other 14 sites):** the mount lights (`:21354`,
`:24495-24497` Rudolph's trail, `:45032`), the three Vortex-stealth armor
chains (`:31279`/`:31297`/`:31315`), the wing lights (`:29547`, `:36026`),
the Snapping Stone trio (`:24575-24583`, `accSnappingStoneLightUp`), and the
phase-blade held light (`:44916`, needs `Item.GetPhaseColor`). **The light
pets are not Player.cs sites at all** — Fairy Bell / Wisp in a Bottle /
Magic Lantern / Suspicious Looking Tentacle emit from `Projectile.AI`
(projectile family, another worker); **NightOwl (12)** sets `nightVision`
only (`:9997-10000`), no `AddLight`.

**Code-only mode (2026-11-18 user directive):** this family was finished
without invoking any compiler — no cargo/rustc/rustfmt/test runs. The tests
in `player_lights.rs` (18, incl. the biome-zone order, the unlock gate, the
slot-range walk, the holdStyle-6 anchor and the negative-coordinate
truncation) are written but **not run**; the first build after the merge
must run `cargo test -p tr-app player_lights` plus the catalog command.

## The last four drop-rule classes (S1-E-14, 2026-11-16)

`ItemDropRules` is now fully covered: `SlimeBodyItemDropRule`,
`StatueMimicItemDropRule`, `MechBossSpawnersDropRule` and
`FromOptionsWithoutRepeatsDropRule` are ported in `crates/tr-core/src/loot.rs`
and reachable from the generated table, and `Conditions.NamedNPC` /
`Conditions.RedHatSkeletron` are `Cond` variants. Three deliberate folds keep
`LootNpc` `Copy`:

1. **`Conditions.NamedNPC`** (`Conditions.cs:971-979`) compares
   `info.npc.GivenName` against `Language.GetTextValue(neededName)`. `LootNpc`
   cannot hold a `String`, so the comparison is hoisted to the caller:
   `tr_core::loot::NamedNpc` has exactly the three variants the drop table
   registers (`GuideNames.Andrew`, `SteampunkerNames.Whitney`,
   `PainterNames.Jim`), `NamedNpc::key()` is the localization key, and
   `loot_db::named_npc(&given_name)` resolves it through `lang::text`.
   `HasGivenName` (`NPC.cs:6741`) is the empty-string early return.
2. **`Conditions.RedHatSkeletron`** (`Conditions.cs:543-559`) is
   `NPC.RedHatSkeletronAdjustmentsEnabled()` (`NPC.cs:66671-66682`) — four
   `(type, ai[3] or localAI[3] == 1)` pairs (35/`ai[3]`, 36/`localAI[3]`,
   32/`localAI[3]`, 33/`ai[3]`). Folded to `LootNpc::red_hat_skeletron`.
   `spawn_loot` currently always passes `false`: the only C# writers of those
   slots are `NPC.RedHatSkeletron` (`NPC.cs:80395`, the Clothier's curse) and
   the sitting-Clothier ritual (`PlayerSittingHelper.cs:81`), both unported —
   and the port's Skeletron head stores the live hand count in `ai[3]`
   (`world_sim/npcs.rs`'s init pass), so reading the field as the flag would be
   wrong. The five `ByCondition(RedHatSkeletron, …)` rows are registered and
   report; they simply cannot fire until that summon path lands.
3. **`MechBossSpawnersDropRule`'s `!info.IsInSimulation`** (`:16-23`) is a
   constant `true`: the only resolver is the death path (`NPC.cs:78927-78936`,
   which constructs `DropAttemptInfo` with `IsInSimulation = false`) and the
   port has no projection simulation.

**The generator bug this found.** `tools/gen_loot.py` read `Populate()`'s
statement stream but did not follow its `this.RegisterBosses();` /
`this.RegisterMimic();` calls into the 23 nested private methods, so 147 of the
633 register sites — the entire boss table, including Skeletron's red-hat rows
and the Moon Lord's distinct-pick row — were missing from `loot_db_gen.rs`
without a single warning. `expand_nested` + the `src` parameter of
`process_stream` now recurse (each method keeps its own locals), and
`INT_LOCAL_RE` resolves `short type = 35;` / `int type = …` register arguments.
Count: 1 421 -> 1 582 registrations. The remaining 166 warnings are
`OneFromOptions` ids that `itemdata.rs` does not model (S1-E-2), unchanged.

**Deliberate simplification.** `statue_style_to_item` is a plain arithmetic
table, not a `Dictionary`, because the C# is a `switch` with three contiguous
runs (`51..62`, `63..75`, and the `default: 438 + style - 2`) — the run form
keeps the port readable against `WorldGen.cs:37928-37991`.

## Golf (S1-E-9, 2026-11-16)

Three `tr-core` modules: `ball.rs` (the generic `Terraria.Physics` engine),
`golf.rs` (`GolfHelper`'s arithmetic/table half) and `golf_state.rs`
(`GolfState` + `GolfBallTrackRecord`). All ported 1:1 with `file:line`
citations; 28 tests.

**The `Materials.json` gap.** `GolfHelper.ContactListener` and `HitGolfBall`
read five per-tile floats (`TileGolfPhysics.{Direct,Side,Club,PassThrough}`
`ImpactDampening` + `ImpactDampeningResistanceEfficiency`) through
`TileMaterials.GetByTileId`. `TileMaterials.cs:22-24` deserialises them from
`Terraria.GameContent.Metadata.MaterialData.Materials.json`, an **embedded
resource of `Terraria.dll`** - not a file. This repo has neither the DLL nor the
JSON (`assets/Content/` holds only `Fonts`, `Images`, `Sounds`), so the table is
unrecoverable. The port therefore reaches it through a `GolfMaterials` trait
whose default (`DefaultMaterials`) returns `GolfPhysics::default()`, i.e. **1.0
for every factor**. That is the identity for all four uses (the side/direct
blend, `velocity * 1.0`, `lerp(v * 1.0, v, e) == v`; the bumper push uses no
material at all), so an unknown material leaves the ball's motion untouched
rather than inventing a friction value. Consequence: on real terrain the ball
does not yet slow on landing; wiring the retail JSON (or a hand-built table)
into `impl GolfMaterials` is the only remaining work for exact contact feel.

**`GolfBall` is a value snapshot, not a `Projectile`.** `GolfState` keeps a live
`Projectile` reference and re-validates it on every `GetLastHitBall`
(`active`, `IsAGolfBall[type]`, `owner == Main.myPlayer`, `ai[1]`). `tr-core` has
no projectile pool, so the caller supplies a `&GolfBall` snapshot and the same
four guards read it. `Main.myPlayer` is a real parameter threaded through
`get_last_hit_ball` - the owner check is a genuine comparison (a test varies both
sides), not a constant.

**`BALL_RETURN_PENALTY = 1` is dead.** `GolfState.cs:8` declares it and never
reads it; it is omitted rather than carried as a dead constant.

**Scope.** Ported: the ball engine, the shot model, the club table, the contact
listener's bounce/bumper/hole-capture/pass-through decisions, the score record
and the per-client state. Not ported: the projectile AIs 721/722 and 739-752,
the golf UI, `FancyGolfPredictionLine`, tee placement, netcode, and the
dust/sound/chat effects (the listener reports contacts instead of performing
them, so the caller owns those).
## The conveyor-belt family (S1-E-13e, 2026-11-16)

`crates/tr-app/src/collision.rs::build_tile_contacts` ports
`Collision.BuildTileContacts` (`Collision.cs:2135-2290`): the `(int)`
truncation of the box origin, the ±1/`+3` scan window clamped to
`Main.maxTilesY - 40`, the `tileSolid || (tileSolidTop && frameY == 0)` gate,
the `0.1f` touch epsilons and all five slope arms (`:2192-2258`) plus the
corner arms (`:2260-2287`). The per-face overlap keeps the source's
`(int)Math.Max(... + 0.5f, 1f)` floor.

`apply_conveyor_belt_movement_to_velocity` ports
`Collision.ApplyConveyorBeltMovementToVelocity` (`:3918-4188`): the
per-side direction sum, the `±2.5 / ±1.25 / ±0.75` X clamps, the Y clamps,
the corner lift onto the belt's top edge (`:4072-4101`), the side snap
(`:4103-4131`), the `zero * 6f / 60f` ramp and the two slope-quarter wall
snaps (`:4150-4185`). The `zero.Y < 0` arm's inner test is `zero.Y < 8f`,
always true for a negative value - a real vanilla quirk, ported as written.

`step_conveyor_belt_player` ports `Collision.StepConveyorBelt`
(`:4190-4320`) for a Player, with the `gfxOffY > 2`/grapple/pulley guards,
the 5 px body shrink (restored before the movement probes, `:4292-4296`), the
`GetEntityEdgeTiles` ring, the per-slope belt lines and the two
`TileCollision` steps. It is called from `Player::move_vanilla` at the
`Player.cs:28230` position (after `SlopingCollision`).

Deliberate gaps, all recorded here rather than guessed:

* `TryFindingConveyorBeltRising` (`:4322`) is **not** ported: grep across
  `decompiled/` finds zero callers - dead code.
* `StepConveyorBelt`'s `artificialRising` argument (`:4301-4318`) is not
  carried: its only callers are the unported golf/rising paths.
* The `!shimmering` half of the `:28225` gate is dropped - the port has no
  `Player.shimmering` (the absorbed state belongs to S1-E-16). The `tongued`
  half is modelled as `holding(38)`.
* The `!isLockedToATile` gate (`:28228`) has no port field; no ported
  mechanism locks the player to a tile.
* `WorldItem.onConveyor` is dropped: its only consumer is the draw-side
  velocity spin (`Main.cs:38613`), and the port draws drops upright.
* The NPC path (`NPC.cs:92575-92578`, gated by `ConveyorBeltCollision`)
  is **not** wired: the port has no unified `NPC.UpdateCollision` to hang it
  on, and `NPCID.Sets.ConveyorBeltCollision` is not in `tiledata` yet.
* The item box stays the port's 14 px (`item.rs::SIZE`) rather than the C#'s
  16 (`WorldItem.cs:138`): widening it changes every existing drop's
  collision, which is a separate task.

## The screen effects (S1-E-16, 2026-11-16)

`crates/tr-core/src/scene.rs` carries the three `SceneState` state machines
verbatim, in the C#'s order (`SceneState.cs:75-77`):
`ScreenObstruction.Update` (`ScreenObstruction.cs:13-46`),
`ScreenDarkness.Update` (`ScreenDarkness.cs:12-34`) and
`MoonlordDeathDrama.Update` (`MoonlordDeathDrama.cs:155-193`). The draw halves
live in `crates/tr-app/src/render/screen_fx.rs`, wired at the vanilla seams:
`DrawBack` right after the background overlays (`Main.cs:62217`), `DrawFront`,
`DrawWhite` and `ScreenObstruction.Draw` after the projectiles
(`Main.cs:62322-62324`), the MoonExplosion pieces and blasts inside
`DoDraw_WallsTilesNPCs` (`Main.cs:63276-63277`).

`UnbreakableWallScan.InsideUnbreakableWalls`/`LineScan`
(`UnbreakableWallScan.cs:39-84`) is ported with the 250-tile scan distance, the
eight directions, the `wallColor() >= 16` test and the eight-fold rotation of
the hit mask. The `DangerousDungeonCurse` tier ladders (`:5-27`, `:32-55`) are
pure functions taking the zone/downed flags the `tr-app` driver reads.

Deliberate deviations, recorded rather than guessed:

* `DebugOptions.devLightTilesCheat` has no port, so the `ScreenObstruction`
  0.25 cap on the wall arm (`ScreenObstruction.cs:23-28`) is omitted and the
  0.9 clamp always applies.
* The `ScreenDarkness` walk normally scans `Main.npc[]`; `tr-core` has no NPC
  list, so the driver fills `SceneMetrics::screen_darkness_npcs` from the
  `tr-app` NPC vec with only the fields the two arms read. The C# loop is
  last-match-wins and that semantics is kept.
* Wall of Flesh (113) abandonment: the C# reads `npc.localAI[1]`, but the port
  folds the WoF ramp into `ai[0]` (`npc.rs:9160-9168`), so `local_ai1` is filled
  from `ai[0]`.
* Duke Fishron (370) is not a ported `NpcKind` - the phase 10+/9-with-timer arm
  is code-complete but unexercised until that boss lands.
* `ScreenObstruction.Draw`'s `MagicPixel` stand-in is the renderer's built-in
  `white_uv` quad (`push_fx_rect`). `MoonlordPiece.GetLight` averages the port's
  `LightMap` rather than `Lighting.GetColor` - the same tile colours, a
  different seam.
* `DrawPaladinsShield` and `DrawInfernoRings` are **not** drawn: their gates are
  `Player.hasPaladinShield` / `defendedByPaladin` / `inferno` and the
  `flameRingScale` / `flameRingRot` animation state, none of which the port's
  `Player` carries. The sheets (`Extra_98`, `FlameRing`) load so the draws can
  be added without touching the asset pipeline.
* The lens flare (`Main.DrawLensFlare`, `Main.cs:62509-62514`) is a
  `NextHorizonRenderer` feature that the port does not have.
* `FocusHelper.AllowPlayerToEmitEffects` (the `!WorldUpdateStepper.DrawnThisUpdate`
  split between a drawn and a stepped frame) is unported, so an inferno-ring
  animation would always advance - moot while the draw is unwritten.

## S1-E-35 - weather control rows (deviation record)

* The F3 rows toggle the two events through vanilla's own entry points
  (`Rain::start_rain`/`stop_rain` = `Main.StartRain` `Main.cs:64659-64727` /
  `Main.StopRain` `:64644-64658`; `Sandstorm::start_sandstorm`/`stop_sandstorm`
  = `Sandstorm.cs:117-129`), never a hand-written state write — the
  duration/strength ladders and their stream draws are the C# ones.
* The catalogue cites HEROsMod `GeneralMessages.cs:467-520`; that mod's source
  is not in `decompiled/`, so only its local half (start/stop) is ported. Its
  network sync half has no target: the port is single-player, so no
  `NetMessage` is sent from a debug row (same convention as the S1-E-37 event
  rows).
* `world_rows` takes the live `rain.is_raining()` / `sandstorm.happening` flags
  from the frame instead of reaching into `App` itself, keeping the draw side a
  pure function of the state it shows (the `god_mode` precedent).

## The Steam transport divergence (S1-I-6, 2026-11-16)

The vanilla runs multiplayer over a pluggable `ISocket`
(`Net/Sockets/ISocket.cs:3-13`: `Connect`/`AsyncSend`/`AsyncReceive`/
`StartListening`/`GetRemoteAddress`). Two implementations exist: `TcpSocket`
(`Net/Sockets/TcpSocket.cs`, 184 lines, the typed-IP path) and `SocialSocket`
(`Net/Sockets/SocialSocket.cs`, 70 lines), which forwards every call to
`SocialAPI.Network` — on the retail PC build the Steam module, whose reader and
writer threads are `Social/Steam/SteamP2PReader.cs` (138) /
`Social/Steam/SteamP2PWriter.cs` (79) over `Steamworks.Networking`, with the
lobby browser in `Social/Steam/Lobby.cs` (133) and the client/server modules
`Social/Steam/NetClientSocialModule.cs` (238) /
`Social/Steam/NetServerSocialModule.cs` (215). `Netplay.StartListening`
(`Netplay.cs:222-229`) starts **both** listeners when a social API is present,
and `Netplay.StartSocialClient` (`:610-617`) is the join path the "Join via
Steam" row takes; the lobby id the world sync carries is
`NetSocialModule.GetLobbyId` (`Social/Base/NetSocialModule.cs:37`,
`Social/Steam/NetClientSocialModule.cs:92`).

**The port's transport is TCP only, deliberately.** `crates/tr-app/src/net.rs`
binds `TcpListener::bind(("0.0.0.0", port))` (`:3022`, `Server::start` `:3021`)
and dials `TcpStream::connect(addr)` (`:3331`, `Client::connect` `:3330`); there
is no `ISocket` trait and no social module. This is the accepted scope of the
ROADMAP non-goals (`Social/**` — "Steam + WeGame modules, the Workshop, P2P,
cloud") and `PORT_MAP.md`'s "not ported (by design)" row.

What is **unchanged** by the swap — and why this is a transport divergence, not
a protocol one:

* the wire frame is the vanilla's (`[u16 LE length][u8 id][body]`,
  `NetMessage.cs:1677-1684`), the version literal is `Terraria326`
  (`net.rs:36`), and the join/handshake state machines are ported verbatim
  (`Netplay.cs:459-544`, the `MessageBuffer.cs` cases);
* the message ids, the codecs and the send/receive order are the C#'s, so a
  port-client <-> port-host session behaves as the vanilla wire does.

What **differs**, all observable:

* **No lobby.** `WorldInfo.lobby_id` (`net.rs:1039`) is always `0`
  (`:3506`/`:3697`); the vanilla client reads the host's lobby id from the join
  sync. The port cannot be discovered or joined through a lobby browser — the
  player types an `ip:port`.
* **No NAT traversal or relay.** Steam P2P (`SteamP2PWriter.QueueSend`,
  `SteamP2PWriter.cs:41`) reaches peers behind NAT; the port needs a reachable
  TCP port (default `7777`, `Netplay.cs:33`).
* **No invites, friends or rich presence.** `SocialAPI.Network.CanInvite`/
  `OpenInviteInterface` (`IngameOptions.cs:178`/`:264`) stay false, so the invite
  row is absent exactly as on a no-Steam vanilla build
  (`crates/tr-app/src/app/settings_ui.rs`), and the multiplayer menu keeps the
  "Join via Steam" row as a `Hint("Steam join is not ported yet")` dead row
  (`crates/tr-app/src/menu/pages.rs:411`).
* **No vanilla interoperability.** The handshake is port-internal (ROADMAP
  non-goals), so a port client cannot join a Steam-hosted vanilla server even
  where the wire ids align.

Not ported and not planned: `Terraria/Social/**` (Steam + WeGame), the Workshop,
Steam Cloud, the overlay / rich-presence / friends modules and the join-request
manager. Porting the transport would require vendoring Steamworks (its DLL sits
unused beside the tree) and would not change the port's own wire, so the ROADMAP
keeps it as this documented divergence rather than a build item.

## The Steam Cloud save exclusion (S1-J-6, 2026-11-18)

Steam Cloud is a platform service, not game logic: it stores the same save
bytes the local path writes, keyed to the Steam account instead of the disk.
The port targets local saves, and the C# itself gates every cloud arm behind
the social module — so the exclusion loses nothing the vanilla does without
Steam.

Where the gate lives in the C#:

* `SocialAPI.Initialize` (called once from `Program.cs:222`) picks the mode —
  `SocialMode.Steam` for the client, Steam only with `-steam` for the dedicated
  server (`Social/SocialAPI.cs:36-52`; the enum is `None`/`Steam`/`WeGame`,
  `Social/SocialMode.cs:3-8`). Only the `SocialMode.Steam` arm loads
  `SocialAPI.Cloud` (`LoadSteam`, `Social/SocialAPI.cs:107`; WeGame loads its
  own at `:126`); under `SocialMode.None` the field stays `null`. The Steam
  module (`Social/Steam/CloudSocialModule.cs`, 108 lines) is a pure
  `SteamRemoteStorage` wrapper (`GetFileCount` `:29`, `FileWriteStreamOpen`
  `:43`, `FileRead` `:76`) — there is no cloud code outside `Social/**`.
* Every cloud arm in the save/load path checks that field and short-circuits
  without it: `WorldFile.LoadWorld` sets "Cloud inaccessible" and fails the
  load (`IO/WorldFile.cs:653-657`); `_SaveWorld` returns without saving
  (`:872-875`); `GetAllMetadata` opens the cloud stream only on the `cloudSave`
  branch (`:194`); `Player.LoadPlayer` returns an empty `PlayerFileData`
  (`Player.cs:55061-55063`) and `Player.GetFileData` returns `null`
  (`:55864-55866`). `FileUtilities` routes cloud reads/writes through
  `SocialAPI.Cloud` only when it is non-null, else falls to the local branch
  (`Utilities/FileUtilities.cs:16-18`, `:107-109`, `:134-136`).
* The front end never offers cloud without the module: the cloud world/player
  list entries are only added when `SocialAPI.Cloud != null`
  (`Main.cs:3972-3978`, `:4018-4024`), the new-world cloud default is
  `SocialAPI.Cloud != null && SocialAPI.Cloud.EnabledByDefault` (`:5490`,
  `:48163`), and cloud deletion is guarded the same way (`:4809-4811`).

The port's `save_world` (`crates/tr-app/src/app/saveglue.rs:88`) writes the
world + player sidecar + map to local paths only — exactly the C#'s
`SocialMode.None` behaviour, where the same gates leave only the local arms
reachable. This closes research/42's risk 42-5 ("Cloud save is missing") as a
non-goal rather than a gap, alongside the ROADMAP Non-goals `Social/**`
exclusion and the S1-I-6 transport divergence above.

The Poltergeist (type 330) leaves the caster stand for its named machine on

the 330 row's 0.1 dash creep (`:24774`), the fall gate
(`Bottom.Y > player.Top.Y` → no gravity, `:24971-24976`), the 330 tail row

`:25148-25168`), the shared X/Y approach tails (0.1 accel with the far-cap

clamp, `:25169-25233`) and the `noTileCollide` half of `UpdateCollision`
(the `oldVelocity` capture + flag reset `:92538-92540`, the straight

over the 8-row sheet — the walker stand-in no longer covers 330.

**The ROADMAP's "shot arm" label is a misnomer**: in 1.4.5.8 the type-330

shot blocks belong to types 122/169/268 only. The Poltergeist's offence is
its 90-damage contact body (`SetDefaults`, `:13188-13203`).

**RNG order**: the one draw on the whole 330 path is the flee branch's
`Main.rand.Next(-1, 2) * 1.5f` while `velocity.X == 0f` (`:24716-24720`),
riding the caller's `UpdateNPCs` stream. Witness tests pin it: exactly one
draw per parked-flee tick (clone-and-peek), zero draws across 30 moving
flee ticks and 600 active ticks — the active machine is draw-free, so the
`UpdateNPCs` stream order for every mixed roster is unchanged on-moon.

Documented deviations (house pattern, all cited at the arm):
- `justHit` (`:24682-24685`) folds onto `hurt_cd > 0` (the port's per-tick
  hurt cooldown, as in the WoF/Deerclops machines).
- `npcTypeNoAggro` (`:24997-25013`) is constant-false (no aggro table yet)
  — the scan never runs, as in `npc_target.rs`.
- `flag36` (`AI_GlobalFiringDistanceCheck`, `:24795`) feeds only the
  122/268 shot arms — a pure no-op for 330, dropped.
- `flag30` is constant-false for 330: its only setters are the type-316
  arm and the 169/268 roof scan, and the `ai[2] >= 30 && num291 == 16`
  test (`:24743`) is dead C# (`num291` is always 40 there) — `:25030-25038`
  never fires and is not carried.
- `TargetClosest` rides the shared `npc_target::target_closest` with the
  single session player (the S1-D-3p convention, ticker 0).

13 `s1_f_13b2c_*` tests (11 in the module: the anchor latch, the counter
climb, the 60-tick flip, the dash creep/cap, the left mirror + damping,
the fall gate/Y approach, the three RNG witnesses, the justHit reset, the
tile fly-through; 2 in `npc.rs`: the case-330 frame strip and the A/B pin
`s1_f_13b2c_the_generic_arms_stay_byte_identical` — 20 non-Poltergeist
kinds (the 13 walkers incl. the aiStyle-26 pair, the two hover floaters,
the five casters the ghost used to share) replay their pre-slice arms
verbatim behind the same `update_rng` prelude for 180 ticks each,
bit-comparing kinematics/ai[]/frame state/player hp AND the RNG stream
position every tick; a closing divergence witness runs one off-moon
Poltergeist tick both ways — the named machine's alpha-0 +
EncourageDespawn(10) vs the stand's untouched alpha-100 — proving the
gate changed exactly one kind and the comparison has teeth. The dispatch
seam itself rides the rewritten routing test's Poltergeist half).
Slices A (aiStyle 26) and B (aiStyles 57/58) remain on their own
branches — their stand-ins and frame arms are untouched.

**Code-only mode (2026-11-18)**: this slice landed under a no-compiler

Ported verbatim with in-place citations:

* **The Wood** (`NPC.cs:32761-33043`, the type-325 arms): the hp-band
  `num836` 2/3/4 (`:32771-32778`), the dawn flee 8 + `EncourageDespawn(10)`

  15-tick, speed 10, ±20×0.01 jitters, 50 dmg, `:32846-32865`), the spin

  10+|dx|×0.004 cap-14 lob with the −|dx|×0.3 aim lift, 40 dmg,

  `:32922-32941`), the barrage (10-tick, the 12+|dx|×0.002 cap-16 lob,

  (`:32970-32992`) and the vertical hover — the player-overlap drop, the

  (`position.Y`, not the centre) from centre+30y.
* **The Pumpking** (`NPC.cs:33044-33197`): the `localAI` frame cycle
  (`:33046-33055`), the 300-tick `Next(3)` mode pick (`:33061-33069`), the
  mode-0 Greek-fire lob — every 30th tick past 30, gated on
  `!WorldGen.SolidTile(origin/16)` with the `(dy + Next(50,201))×0.2`
  flattening (`:33070-33085`), the one-time init (`:33087-33104`), the
  dead/2000-px flee retarget (`:33105-33117`), the dawn fall
  (`:33118-33122`), the hover — the 200-px-over-centre aim, `num875` 6 (mode
  1 bands 8/10/12 by distance) on the `/15` lerp, the 300-tick gate
  (`:33123-33169`), the scythe charge (16-speed `/50` lerp, 600 ticks or
  mode≠1 exits, `:33170-33185`), the flee (+0.1 sink, ×0.95 decays,

  (`:33196`). Both machines end with the `noTileCollide` integration
  (`NPC.cs:90495-90498`).

**The RNG draw ORDER (the slice's critical invariant).** C# evaluates a
call's named arguments in TEXTUAL order, and in all three Greek-fire calls
(`:32913`, `:32962`, `:33083`) `Type: Main.rand.Next(326, 329)` sits AFTER
`SpeedX:`/`SpeedY:` — so each shot draws aim-x jitter → aim-y jitter →
SpeedX jitter → SpeedY jitter → **kind LAST**. The module runs that order
and 19 `s1_f_13b2_*` tests pin it: stream-equality witnesses replay every
draw by hand on a fresh `UnifiedRandom` (the idle pick, the stomp jitters,
the spin/barrage/lob five-draw sequences with the kind FIFTH, the mode
`Next(3)`, the solid-origin gate suppressing ALL five draws) and assert
`rng == witness` after each machine tick — plus the wiring test through
`update_rng`, proving the UpdateNPCs stream order survives the axis.

Documented deviations, all deliberate:

* **The lights are skipped** — `Lighting.AddLight` (`:32781`/`:32785` for
  the Wood's two type arms, `:33059` for the Pumpking): no entity-light
  layer on these machines yet (the Retinazer port's precedent); no
  `Main.rand` draws in them, so the stream is untouched.
* **The type-344 dust arm is skipped** (`:32821-32825`, the Everscream's
  `Dust.NewDust` — the only rand-drawing line in the skipped region): the
  kind is unported (S1-F-13c), the arm is unreachable for type 325, and
  skipping it keeps the stream exact for the ported kinds.
* **The type-344 (Everscream) branches are not ported** — the kind does not
  exist in the roster (S1-F-13c); only the type-325 arms run (the idle's
  low-hp pick reads {3,4}; the 344 kind always falls to the else arm's
  {1,2} pick, `:32806-32812`).
* **The Pumpking's two PumpkingBlade (328, aiStyle 59) spawns are deferred**
  (`:33093-33103`): the blade kind is unported. `NPC.NewNPC` draws no
  `Main.rand` outside the `getGoodWorld` variant roll (`NPC.cs:80752`),
  which the port's spawn plumbing does not model (`variants.rs`), so
  skipping the two calls keeps the stream exact; the blades land with
  their kind.
* **The `player13` re-reads after retargets** (`:33090`/`:33108`/`:33139`)
  are kept as `ptop`/centre refreshes even where the lob arm already ran
  this tick (the `#[allow(unused_assignments)]` arms) — the 1:1 shape.

**Test-world note.** `Collision.SolidCollision` clamps its sample rows to
`maxTilesY − 40` (`Collision.cs:2712-2713`), so the module's probe tests run
in a 200-tile-tall world — a 120-tall one would clamp row 100 away and the
floor probe would never fire.

**Verification status — tests written, NOT yet run (code-only mode,
2026-11-18).** The user reserved the CPU: no cargo/rustc/test invocation on
this slice. The port was verified by line-by-line re-reading of the C#
blocks (`NPC.cs:32761-33043`/`:33044-33197`, the `WorldGen.SolidTile`
catch semantics `:70115-70131`, `EncourageDespawn` `:7249-7256`, the
noTileCollide integration `:90490-90503`) and by hand-tracing every test's
math (including the f32 rounding edge cases). The 19 `s1_f_13b2_*` tests
run in the lead's compile window before the merge — the catalog command
plus the anchors tripwire gate the landing.
## The aiStyle-58 shared-kind census + gap audit (S1-D-3, code-only mode)
The 2026-11-18 aiStyle-58 round ran the shared-kind census before any port:
`SetDefaults` (`NPC.cs:8426`) carries exactly ONE `this.aiStyle = 58` row —
**type 327, the Pumpking** (`NPC.cs:13142-13157`: 100×100, dmg 50, def 40,
26000 HP, `noGravity` + `noTileCollide`, kb 0, value 50000, npcSlots 5). No
dynamic `aiStyle` reassignment anywhere in `NPC.cs` targets 58 (the only
other `= 58;` hits are width/height/damage constants), and the whole
decompiled tree's second `aiStyle = 58` row is `Projectile.cs:4417` — the
PROJECTILE aiStyle space (`Projectile.AI`'s `aiStyle == 58` arm,
`Projectile.cs:28906`), a different dispatch, not an NPC kind. **Verdict:
aiStyle 58 is single-kind; no `npc_ai_style58_shared.rs` module is needed.**
The census audit instead re-verified the sibling port — `982d3caf`
(`task/S1-F-13b2-bosses`, `npc_ai_pumpkin_boss.rs::pumpking_step`, NOT yet
merged into main at this audit's base `bfe68db8`) — against the whole arm
(`NPC.cs:33044-33197`) with the f1701eb0 defect catalogue (`git show
f1701eb0 -- docs/ANALYSIS.md`, the Hungry aiStyle-29 round) applied class by
class. Code-only mode per user directive: **no compiler invoked**, the

## The aiStyle-26 machine (S1-F-13b2 slice A, 2026-11-18)

`npc_ai_unicorn.rs::unicorn_step` ports `AI_026_Unicorns`
(`NPC.cs:62366-62924`, the caller arm `:25631-25634`) for the Headless
Horseman (315) and the Hellhound (329), wired kind-scoped in
`update_kind_ai` — NOT a global aiStyle-26 axis claim (423 rides its own
`update_nebula_beast`, M4-EVENT-9; 155/410/546 are unported kinds). The
port is block-by-block verbatim: the turn flag + stuck windows
(`:62373-62469` — the non-short-circuit `|`, the >300 wrap, the justHit
reset, netUpdate at exactly 30, the <200-px clear), the Horseman's
481st-tick pumpkin lob (`:62409-62440` — `localAI[0]++ >= 480f`
post-increment), the 155/329 hop with INTEGER `width / 2` centres
(`:62558-62564` — 315 never hops), the moon-gated chase/wander split
(`:62581-62616` — outside the pumpkin moon `EncourageDespawn(10)` replaces
`TargetClosest`), the walk core (`:62617-62740` — 315 runs its OWN
cap/approach block `:62651-62684` AND the shared block `:62717-62739`:
0.07+0.07 first tick; 329's ±0.1 band nudge + 0.07 = 0.17), the inline
step-up (`:62741-62805`) and the jump probe (`:62806-62903` — `flag7`
false for 315/329 folds the below-1 conjunct away).

**Tests written, not run — code-only mode** (no cargo/rustc invoked this
slice; verification was a line-by-line re-read of the C#). 10
`s1_f_13b2_*` tests pin the windows, the double accel, the wander flips,
the hop, the wall-height jump rows, the step-up lift, the lob's payload
and its three-draw witness stream, and the untouched stream between lobs.

RNG order (the `UpdateNPCs` stream, `Main.cs:17767-17769`): the only
ported draws are the lob's three, in C# order — the
`NextVector2Circular(40, 40)` angle `NextFloat` (`NPC.cs:62417` →
`Utils.cs:1261-1264`, `2π·f` with f64 `Math.Cos/Sin` cast to f32,
`:1665-1668`), the radial `NextFloat` (`Utils.cs:1268`), then
`NextFloatDirection() * 3f` (`Utils.cs:1203-1206`). The gallop-dust arm
(`:62431-62438`: `Next(3)` + two `NextFloat`) is deferred WITH its draws
(the `npc_lights.rs` S1-E-5 precedent); the Hellhound and every non-fire
tick draw nothing. `target_closest` is deterministic.

Documented deviations, all deliberate:
- **The stuck latch**: the C# reads `oldPosition.X` latched AFTER the AI
  (`Collision_MoveWhileDry`, `NPC.cs:92605`); the port's `update_rng`
  latches `old_x` BEFORE it, so the machine carries its own end-of-tick
  `unicorn_stuck_x` latch (the `frost_stuck_x` precedent,
  `npc.rs:6623-6627`), init 0.0 = `Entity.oldPosition`'s field default
  (`Entity.cs:14`).
- **`justHit` → `hurt_cd > 0`**: the house stand-in (the port has no
  per-tick justHit flag).
- **Target 255 on the first tick**: `target_player()` maps the
  still-unresolved slot to the session player; the C# would index the
  inactive slot-255 dummy at the world origin for exactly that tick
  (`ClearTarget`, `NPC.cs:42924-42927`). The lob's `num3 != 255` gate is
  verbatim — a never-resolved target suppresses the shot but still resets
  the counter.
- **The gravity seam**: the movement tail integrates the port's
  GRAVITY/MAX_FALL (0.4/8.0) like `walker_step`; the C#'s depth-scaled
  0.3/10 (`UpdateNPC_UpdateGravity`, `:90878+`) rides the port-wide
  gravity seam.
- **The lob is dropped until projectile 1001 lands**: `proj_data` has no
  HorsemanPumpkin (1001) row (`projectile/data.rs`'s `_ => return None`),
  so the pool silently drops the `wants_hostile_shot_ai` request (the
  documented house pattern, `projectile.rs:1321-1324`). The request stays
  faithful; the row is out of slice A's scope.
- **Deferred to slice B**: the gallop dust visuals WITH their RNG draws,
  the `FindFrame` case-315/329 sprite arms (`NPC.cs:74465` /
  `:74375-74403` — the kinds ride `walker_frame` today), the Horseman's
  `Lighting.AddLight(Center, 0.4, 0.36, 0.2)` (`:62420`), and the
  `gfxOffY` decay/render arms (`:90397-90420` — slice A records the
  step-up writes into the new `gfx_off_y`/`step_speed` fields,
  `NPC.cs:6095`/`:6097`).
- **The 22/57/58 arms are untouched**: the Poltergeist's caster stand and
  the MourningWood/Pumpking hovers keep their S1-F-13b stand-ins (other
  workers' slices); the `ai3_walk_speed` 6.0 rows stay as the cap pins

## The frame phase split (S1-B-8)

`app/frame.rs`'s single 2 110-line `frame()` became a phase-list orchestrator
(51 lines of calls + gate arms) over three modules: `frame/world.rs` (the
in-world branch, one fn per `phase("…")` site in the C#'s
`DoUpdateInWorld_Inner` order, `Main.cs:17745-17822`, plus the click cluster,
the pause/step gates, the env cluster and the step-gated tail),
`frame/draw.rs::draw_region` (`Main.DoDraw`'s body: the pre-draw state, the
S1-B-7 marker-ordered passes, the interface, the map, the post/filters and
the present path) and the orchestrator's own head/setup/focus-pause fns. The
draw region moved **verbatim** — the 55-field destructure and the gpu gate
travel with it, the only mechanical change being the surface-acquire early
return yielding `None` so the caller skips the epilogue's stat write-backs
exactly like the pre-split frame.

Preserved deviations (each a recorded follow-up, not closed here): the
pre-world cluster (weather/rain/scene_state/windy_day/ambience) keeps its
in-world-branch placement — moving it to the C#'s pre-`DoUpdateInWorld` slots
(`Main.cs:17146-17231`) is a behaviour change owed to research/39 seed #2's
data-driven tick plan; the duplicated `update_camera_at_draw` pair
(S1-B-4) survives verbatim inside `draw_half_pre_snapshots`; the inline
1600×900 `screen` fallback stays distinct from `App::screen_size()`; the
dust+minecart and time+event fusions stay as landed. The split is proven
pixel-transparent: `TR_SEED=1 TR_SHOT TR_CAM=400,300 TR_DAY=0.5` pairs are
SHA256-equal pre/post at zoom 1.0 and 1.5 (all four runs identical), and at
zoom 2.0 the post-split runs are internally deterministic and byte-equal to a
pre-split run — the pre-split binary's own zoom-2.0 variance (688 613 px
between two pre-split runs, `pixel_diff.py`) pre-dates the split and is a
harness follow-up.
## The starting weapons' projectile AI (projectile-ai, 2026-11-17)

**Intent.** A starting weapon's shot must fly the C# trajectory, not a
stand-in. The three families the goal names are the bow's arrows (aiStyle 1,
`Projectile.cs:23201-23203` → `AI_001`), the shuriken (aiStyle 2,
`:23205-23688`) and the musket's ball (aiStyle 1, the type-14 row `:950-961`).
Two of the three already rode ported arms; the shuriken did not — it was
carried by a hand-written two-half-step bounce (`ai_shuriken`, 0.6 damped)
that the C# never runs, and its data row was absent.

**Inventory, aiStyle 2 and 4 (`Projectile.cs`).**

| aiStyle | C# extent | kinds the C# routes there | port before |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | `23205-23688` (485 lines) | 3 Shuriken, 48 ThrowingKnife, 93, 54, 69/70/621, 166 Snowball, 240 Dutchman shell, 249, 300, 304, 306, 347, 370/371/936, 497, 501, 504/954/979, 510, 520, 599, 861, 909, 968, 1085 (41 ids) | **missing** — the shuriken had a placeholder bounce, the shell a 2-line alpha arm only |
| 4 | `23694-23828` (135 lines) | 7 VilethornBase, 8 VilethornTip, 150/151/152, 493/494 | **missing** — no `proj_data` row, the arm fell to `_ => {}` |
| 1 | `23201-23203` → `AI_001` | 153 ids (1/2/4/5 arrows, 14 MusketBall, 51 Seed, 81/82 hostile arrows, 121-126 gem bolts via 29, …) | ported (`ai_arrow` / `ai_style1_flight`) |
| 3 | `23690-23692` | 19 ids (boomerangs) | ported (`ai_boomerang`) |
| 29 | `26676-26678` | the six gem bolts | ported (`ai_gem_staff`) |

**Choice.** aiStyle 2 + aiStyle 4, the two missing styles the starting tier
actually fires: the shuriken, the throwing knife, the snowball and the Wand of
Sparkings' spark (aiStyle 2) and the Vilethorn (aiStyle 4). The rest of the
thrown family's ids (93/240/249/300/304/306/347/370/371/497/501/504/510/861/
909/968/1085) fly on the same arm without new rows — only their `SetDefaults`
row would be needed.

**OUT-OF-SLICE** (unported styles the early weapons also need): aiStyle 19
(the spears 47/49/130 — `AI_019_Spears` `45857-46221`, needs the extension

(the harpoon 23, `:24636-24828`), aiStyle 5 (9/12/503, `:23830-24098`), and

wind head, the rotation ladder, the 32 px/tick clamp, the movement chain's

dust/gore/sound layer in the pool), the MP-only town-NPC kill of the snowball

## Day cycle: time, spawn gates, sky (daycycle slice, 2026-11-17)

Scope: the clock, the surface spawn gate and the sky tint. Events (blood moon,
eclipse, weather, music) are out of this slice.

* The two boundary tests in `UpdateTime` are STRICT (`Main.cs:65137`
  `if (Main.time > 32400.0)`, `:65148` `if (Main.time > 54000.0)`): a clock
  resting exactly on 32400/54000 is still the old half. The port compared with
  `>=` and flipped one tick early; `world_sim/clock.rs` now uses `>`.
* `EncourageDespawn` is modelled as a `time_left`-style window
  (`crates/tr-app/src/npc.rs`): `encourage_despawn` only ever lowers it
  (`NPC.cs:7249-7256`), `tick_despawn`/`despawn_expired` are the
  `NPC.cs:77986-77996` decrement and the `<= 0` deactivation. The Eye of
  Cthulhu's `Main.IsItDay() | dead` arm (`NPC.cs:20071-20074`) is the only
  writer, so it leaves 10 ticks after dawn or after the player dies. Deviation:
  the C# also refreshes `timeLeft` from `NPC.activeTime` (`:8542`) for every
  other NPC; the port leaves `despawn_timer` idle (-1) for them, so no other
  NPC can time out yet.
* `Main.IsItDay()` (`Main.cs:62825-62832`) is `Main.dayTime` except on remix
  worlds; the port reads `world.day_time` directly (remix is unported).
* The sky tint is `Main.SetBackColor` (`Main.cs:63452-63496`) exactly: white
  from 13500 to 37800, the two sunset ramps, the night ramps and the moon-phase
  floor. The blood-moon and graveyard tint arms are unported (events).
* Dawn's 53400 sub-threshold (`Main.time >= 53400.0`, the Empress enrage at
  `NPC.cs:46238-46245`) is out of slice: the Empress is not ported.
